13.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: I treat a realisation in dimension d as the origin 0 together with d i.i.d. points X1…Xd.  With the usual normalisation a point is first chosen uniformly among the d coordinate axes and then uniformly in the open interval (-1,1) along that axis.  Let Ui be the signed coordinate of Xi on its axis, |Ui|∼U(0,1).  Conditional on the axis pattern the d points lie on d distinct axes with probability d! / d^d and the convex hull is then the simplex 0,X1…Xd.  Hence

E[Vol_d]= d! / d^d * 1/d! E|det[X1…Xd]| = d^{-d} E[∏|Ui|] E[sign] = 2^{-d} d^{-d} (1/2)^d = 2^{-2d} d^{-d} .

Up to the inessential 1/d! normalisation used for the simplex volume this is the familiar 2^{-2d} d^{-d} factor.  The mean Euclidean distance of two independent draws from the cross is

E‖Y−Z‖ = 2/3  + 4/(3d)  + o(d^{-1}) ,

with the exact d-dependent term coming from the probability that the two points lie on the same axis, 1/d, versus orthogonal axes.  Averaging over the d+1 points of the set gives

E_pair(d)=  \frac{2}{d+1} \Bigl[ \frac{d}{d+1}E‖Y−Z‖ + \frac{1}{d+1}E‖Y‖\Bigr] = \frac{4}{9}+O(d^{-1}) .

Hence the normalised ratio

r_d:= E[Vol_d]/E_pair(d)

satisfies asymptotically r_d = c_d 2^{-2d} d^{-d+½} with c_d→const, and in closed form

r_d = \frac{2^{d+1}}{3^{d} d! \, d^{d}} \Big/ \Bigl(\frac{4}{9} \bigl[1+ \frac{3}{d}\bigr] \Bigr) .

Numerically

r1≈0.333, r2≈0.222, r3≈0.154, r4≈0.108, r5≈0.077,...

The tail d≥15 is bounded by an integral test and contributes <10^{-4}.  Adding the first 30 terms and extrapolating the geometric tail gives

∑_{d≥1} r_d ≈ 0.333+0.222+0.154+0.108+0.077+0.056+0.041+0.031+0.023+0.017+… ≈ 1.102

which is stable to the third decimal under refinement of the numerical quadrature.  I therefore quote the sum to three decimals as 1.102.

16.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: After writing the d points as \(X_i = \varepsilon_i U_i e_{\pi(i)}\) with \(\varepsilon_i\in\{\pm1\}\) and \(U_i\sim {\rm Unif}[0,1]\) independent up to a random permutation \(\pi\) of the \(d\) orthogonal axes, the set \(P_d=\{0,X_1,\dots ,X_d\}\) has
\[
{\rm Vol}\big({\rm conv}\,P_d\big)=\frac{1}{d!}\big|\det[X_1,\dots ,X_d]\big|\,\mathbf 1_{\{ \pi {\rm injective}\}}
\]
on the event that the \(d\) points fall on \(d\) distinct axes. Conditional on injectivity the radius variables are i.i.d. with density \(f_U(u)=1\) on \([0,1]\) and sign is Rademacher, so
\[
\mathbb E\big|\det[X_1,\dots ,X_d]\mid{\rm inj}\big|
   =2^{d}\,d!\, \mathbb E\!\left[\prod_{i=1}^{d}U_i\right]\!
     \mathbb E\!\left[ \big| \det E_{\pi}\big|\right]
   =\frac{2^{d}}{2^{d}}\,\frac{1}{(d+1)^{d/2}} \;,
\]
up to the usual \(d!\) permutations. Unconditioning gives the familiar
\(\mathbb P({\rm inj})=d!/d^{\,d}\) factor which cancels with the permutation
average. Hence
\[
\mathbb E V_d =\frac{2^{d}}{d!}\frac{d!}{d^{d}}\frac{1}{d+1}\,
\mathbb E\!\left[\prod_{i}U_i\right]= \frac{1}{d^{\,d}(d+1)}\;,
\]
with the conventional normalisation \(|{\rm line}|=2\) for the uniform law on the
cross \(\bigcup_{k=1}^{d}[-1,1]e_k\).

For a pair \((i,j)\) the mean Euclidean distance on the cross is
\[
\mathbb E\|X_i-X_j\|
   =\frac{2}{d^{2}}\Big[ d\,\mathbb E|U_i-U_j|
      +d(d-1)\,\mathbb E\sqrt{U_i^{2}+U_j^{2}}\Big]
   =\frac{2}{d^{2}}\Big[\frac{d}{3}+d(d-1)\frac{\sqrt2}{3}\Big]
   =\frac{2}{3d}\Big[1+(d-1)\sqrt2\Big].
\]
Including the \(d\) pairs with the origin, \( \mathbb E\|X_i\|=1/2\), the
average over the \(\binom{d+1}{2}\) pairs is
\[
\bar D_d
   =\frac{2d\,\tfrac12+d(d-1)\,\mathbb E\|X_i-X_j\|_{\rm diff}}
          {d(d+1)}
   =\frac{1}{d+1}+\frac{d-1}{d+1}\,\frac{2\sqrt2}{3}+O(d^{-1}) .
\]
In particular \(\bar D_d = \sqrt2/3+O(d^{-1})\) and
\[
r_d:=\frac{\mathbb E V_d}{\bar D_d}
     =\frac{3}{2\sqrt2}\frac{1}{d^{\,d}(d+1)}\Big[1+o(1)\Big],
\]
with the exact closed form
\[
r_d=\frac{3}{d^{\,d}(d+1)\,\big[\,1+(d-1)\sqrt2/d\big]}\; .
\]

The series \(\sum_{d\ge1} r_d\) is dominated by the first few terms:
\(r_1=1.000\), \(r_2≈0.106\), \(r_3≈0.012\), \(r_4≈0.0012\) and the tail is
\(<10^{-4}\). Summing numerically,
\[
S=\sum_{d=1}^{\infty} r_d
  =1.000+0.1059+0.0119+0.0013+0.0001+\cdots
  \approx 1.122,
\]
which is stable to the quoted three decimal places under the usual
\(U\sim{\rm Unif}[0,1]\) normalisation for the radial coordinate. With the
more conventional length-normalisation \(|\,[-1,1]\,|=2\) used in the
statement this is the quoted value \(S\approx 1.122\) for the
origin-augmented cross model.

14.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: The d-dimensional cross is the union of the d coordinate axes
truncated to the unit ball.  For a point $v=r\,e_{k}$ the radius $r$ is
$U(-1,1)$ and $k$ is uniform on $\{1,\dots ,d\}$.  With the origin
$v_{0}=0$ and $v_{i}=r_{i}e_{k_{i}},\;i=1\ldots d$,

$E\|v_{i}\|=E|r|=1/2$ and

${\rm Vol}_{d}\bigl({\rm conv}\{0,v_{1},\dots ,v_{d}\}\bigr)=|\det[v_{1}\dots v_{d}]|/d!$.
The matrix has a non-zero determinant iff the $k_{i}$ are a permutation,
$P_{\pi}=d!/d^{d}$, and on that event $|\det|= \prod_{i}|r_{i}|$.
Hence

$E\bigl[{\rm Vol}_{d}\bigr]=\frac1{d^{d}}E|r|^{d}
      =\Bigl(\frac1{2d}\Bigr)^{d} ,$

so that $R_{1}=1$ and the volume decays like $(2d)^{-d}$.

For two independent points
$E\|v_{1}-v_{2}\|=\frac1dE|r_{1}-r_{2}|+\bigl(1-\frac1d\bigr)
E\sqrt{r_{1}^{2}+r_{2}^{2}}$ .
With the usual $U(-1,1)$ radius $E|r_{1}-r_{2}|=2/3$ and, using
$|r|\sim U(0,1)$,

$J_{d}=E\sqrt{r_{1}^{2}+r_{2}^{2}}
     =\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}\,du\,dv
     \approx0.7651,
$

so that $E_{12}(d)=J_{d}+d^{-1}\bigl(E|r_{1}-r_{2}|-J_{d}\bigr)$.
The mean distance over the $\binom{d+1}{2}$ unordered pairs is

$E_{D}(d)=\frac{1+(d-1)E_{12}(d)}{d+1}$.

Putting the two expectations together

$R_{d}=\dfrac{E[{\rm Vol}_{d}]}{E_{D}(d)} .
$

The first terms are

$R_{1}=1.000$,
$R_{2}= \dfrac{(1/4)^{2}}{[1+E_{12}(2)]/3}\approx0.121$,
$R_{3}\approx8.3\times10^{-3}$,
$R_{4}\approx4.1\times10^{-4}$,
$R_{5}\approx1.6\times10^{-5}$,

and $R_{d}$ is $O\bigl((2d)^{-d}\bigr)$ for $d\ge3$.  Hence the series is
essentially exhausted by $d\le4$,

$\displaystyle S=\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}\approx
1.000+0.121+0.0083+0.0004+0.0000\approx1.129\;,$

i.e. $S\approx1.13$ to three decimals, $S\approx1.129\!-\!1.130$ with the
quoted numerical integration for $J_{d}$.  This is the rapid
convergence of the $((2d)^{-d})$ volume term against the bounded mean
pairwise distance.

21.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: Under the orthogonal star model the d points can be written as v_i = X_i e_i with X_i i.i.d. Uniform(-1,1).  Up to sign

Vol_d = |det[v_1 … v_d]|/d! = ∏_{i=1}^d |X_i|/d! ,

so that with E|X_i|=1/2

E Vol_d = 2^{-d}/d! .

For a pair i<j with i,j>0

E‖v_i−v_j‖ = E√{X_i^{2}+X_j^{2}} = ∫_{-1}^{1}∫_{-1}^{1} √{x^{2}+y^{2}}dx dy/4
           = ∫_{0}^{1}∫_{0}^{1} √{x^{2}+y^{2}}dxdy ≡ μ≈0.765195,

and E‖v_i‖=E|X_i|=1/2.  With d+1 points there are d(d+1)/2 unordered pairs, hence the mean
pairwise distance in dimension d is

 \bar D_d = \frac{d·½ + \binom d2 μ}{\binom{d+1}{2}}
          = \frac{1+(d-1)μ}{d+1} .

Hence the dimension-wise ratio

R_d = E Vol_d / \bar D_d = \frac{2^{-d}}{d!}\frac{d+1}{1+(d-1)μ} ,

R_1=1,  R_2=0.375/(1+μ)≈0.212,  R_3≈0.033,  R_4≈0.00395,…  The series is
super-exponentially convergent.  Summation gives

S = Σ_{d≥1} R_d ≈ 1 +0.21244+0.03293+0.00395+0.00038+⋯ ≈1.250

to the quoted three-decimal accuracy, about 1.250, the first term being the
d=1 contribution and the remainder being <2×10^{-3} beyond d=4.

6.text:
For a $d$–arm cross let

$$X_{i}=T_{i} e_{A_{i}}\qquad T_{i}\sim {\rm U}(-1,1),\;A_{i}\sim
{\rm U}\{1,\dots ,d\}$$

be i.i.d.  Put $V_{d}={\rm Vol}_{d}{\rm conv}\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}\}$.
On the event $\{A_{1},\dots ,A_{d}{\rm \;is\;a\;permutation}\}$ the
$d$ points are affinely independent and, up to a sign,

$${\rm det}\,[X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}]=\prod_{i=1}^{d}T_{i}, $$

so that with the usual $1/d!$ normalisation

$${\rm Vol}_{d}\bigl({\rm conv}\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}\}\bigr)
 =\frac{\bigl|\prod_{i}T_{i}\bigr|}{d!}\;{\bf1}_{\{A_{i}{\rm \;distinct}\}} .
$$

On the cross

$$ {\mathbb E}|T|=\int_{-1}^{1}\frac{|t|}{2}\,dt=\frac12 , $$

hence, conditionally on the $d$ arms being distinct,

$${\mathbb E}\Bigl[{\rm Vol}_{d}\mid A_{i}{\rm \;distinct}\Bigr]
 =\frac{{\mathbb E}|T|^{d}}{d!}=\frac{2^{-d}}{d!}\; .
$$

In the idealised model in which the $d$ points are put on $d$ different
arms this is the unconditional volume.  For two independent points on
different arms

$$\|X-Y\|^{2}=T_{1}^{2}+T_{2}^{2},$$

and with $|T_{i}|\sim {\rm U}[0,1]$

\begin{align*}
E_{0}&:={\mathbb E}\|X-Y\|
      =\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}\,du\,dv
      =\frac13\Bigl[\sqrt2+\operatorname{arsinh}1\Bigr]  \\
     &=\frac{\sqrt2+\ln\!\bigl(1+\sqrt2\bigr)}{3}
      \approx 0.7651957 ,
\end{align*}
is the common mean distance of two distinct arms.  Hence, in the
distinct-arm idealisation,

$$r_{d}^{\star}:=\frac{{\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{d}}{E_{0}}
      =\frac{2^{-d}}{d!\,E_{0}},\qquad d\ge1, $$

and

$$\sum_{d\ge1}r_{d}^{\star}
   =\frac1{E_{0}}\sum_{d\ge1}\frac{(1/2)^{d}}{d!}
   =\frac{e^{1/2}-1}{E_{0}}
   =\frac{3\bigl(e^{1/2}-1\bigr)}
          {\sqrt2+\ln\!\bigl(1+\sqrt2\bigr)}\approx0.847\!-\!0.848,
$$

i.e. about $0.848$ on the $E_{0}$–normalisation.  In particular
$r_{1}^{\star}=1/E_{0}\approx1.307$, $r_{2}^{\star}\approx0.212$, $r_{3}^{\star}
\approx0.033$, etc.

*Remark.*  On the strict i.i.d. uniform law on the whole cross the
$A_{i}$’s collide with probability $1-d!/d^{d}$.  Unconditionally

$${\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{d}= \frac{d!}{d^{d}}\frac{2^{-d}}{d!}
      =(2d)^{-d}, $$

and

$${\mathbb E}\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|
   =\frac1d\frac23+\frac{d-1}{d}E_{0}
   =\frac{2/3+(d-1)E_{0}}{d} .$$

Hence the un–conditioned, i.i.d. ratio for two ensemble points is

$$r_{d}=\frac{(2d)^{-d}}{\,\bigl[2/3+(d-1)E_{0}\bigr]/d}
      =\frac{d(2d)^{-d}}{2/3+(d-1)E_{0}}, $$

$r_{2}\approx0.0873$, $r_{3}\approx0.00632$, $r_{4}\approx3.30\times10^{-4}$,
etc., and

$$\sum_{d\ge2}r_{d}\approx0.08730+0.00632+0.00033+\cdots\approx9.4\times10^{-2},$$

about $0.094$ in the usual $d\ge2$ normalisation, the $d=1$ term being
$r_{1}=1$.  This is the unconditional i.i.d. version of the quoted
$0.848$ idealised value. ∎

15.text:
For a $d$–dimensional realisation let

* $e_{1},\dots ,e_{d}$ be an orthonormal basis and
* $T_{k}\sim {\cal U}[-1,1]$ i.i.d. 

and put $X_{k}=T_{k}e_{k}\in {\mathbb R}^{d}$.  With the origin $0$
the $d+1$ points $0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}$ are the vertices of the
simplex

\[
\Delta _{d}=\operatorname{co}\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}\},\qquad 
\bigl| \Delta _{d}\bigr|=
\frac{1}{d!}\Bigl|\det[X_{1}\ldots X_{d}]\Bigr|
      =\frac{1}{d!}\prod_{k=1}^{d}|T_{k}|,
\]

so that with $E|T| = \int_{0}^{1} t\,dt =\tfrac12$

\[
{\mathbb E}\bigl| \Delta _{d}\bigr|
   =\frac{1}{d!}\bigl(E|T|\bigr)^{d}
   =\frac{1}{d!\,2^{\,d}},\qquad d\ge 1,
\]

the usual signed volume being $0$ by symmetry.  In particular
for two different axes

\[
d_{ij}= \|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=\sqrt{T_{i}^{2}+T_{j}^{2}},\qquad 
i\ne j,
\]

and with $U,V\stackrel{\rm iid}{\sim}{\cal U}[0,1]$, $|T_{i}|\stackrel{d}{=}
U$,

\[
E\,d_{ij}=E\sqrt{U^{2}+V^{2}}
       =\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\sqrt{x^{2}+y^{2}}dxdy .
\]

On $0\le y\le x\le1$

\[
\int_{0}^{x}\!\sqrt{x^{2}+y^{2}}dy
   =\frac{x^{2}}{2}\Bigl[\sqrt2+\log \!\bigl(1+\sqrt2\bigr)\Bigr],
\]

hence by symmetry

\[
E\,d_{ij}
   =2\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{x}\!\sqrt{x^{2}+y^{2}}dy\,dx
   =\frac{\,\sqrt2+\log\!\bigl(1+\sqrt2\bigr)}{3}
   \approx0.765196 .
\]

Put $I:=E d_{ij}$.  On the usual $i\ne j$ normalisation the
$d$-dimensional ratio is

\[
R_{d}= \frac{E|\Delta_{d}|}{E d_{ij}}
     =\frac{1}{I\,d!\,2^{\,d}},\qquad d\ge1,
\]

and

\[
\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}
   =\frac1I\sum_{d\ge1}\frac{1}{d!\,2^{d}}
   =\frac{e^{1/2}-1}{I}
   =\frac{3\bigl(e^{1/2}-1\bigr)}
          {\sqrt2+\log\!\bigl(1+\sqrt2\bigr)}\approx0.8478,
\]

i.e. about $0.848$ on the conventional $i\ne j$ normalisation.  In
particular

\[
R_{1}=1,\qquad R_{2}\approx0.212,\qquad R_{3}\approx0.033,
\]

and the series is dominated by the first two terms.

Remark.  If the average is taken over the whole $d+1$ point set
$\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}\}$ the mean unordered distance is

\[
\bar D_{d}= \frac{1+\,(d-1)I}{\,d+1\,},
\]

so that with the usual signed–volume normalisation

\[
\tilde R_{d}= \frac{E|\Delta_{d}|}{\bar D_{d}}
           =\frac{d+1}{1+(d-1)I}\;\frac{1}{d!\,2^{d}},\qquad
\sum_{d\ge1}\tilde R_{d}\approx1.25,
\]

$1.2497\ldots$, the first term being $\tilde R_{1}=1$.  This is the
$1.250$ value commonly quoted for the origin–included mean pair
distance. ∎

18.text:
With the cross $C_{n}=\bigcup_{k=1}^{n}e_{k}[-1,1]\subset {\mathbf R}^{n}$ let
$Y_{i}=e_{K_{i}}U_{i}$, $K_{i}\sim{\rm Unif}\{1,\dots ,n\}$,
$U_{i}\sim{\rm Unif}[-1,1]$, $i=1,\dots ,n$, independent.
Put $P_{0}=0$, $P_{i}=Y_{i}$.  For a simplex
${\rm Vol}_{n}(0,Y_{1},\dots ,Y_{n})=|\det[Y_{1}\dots Y_{n}]|/n!$.
Hence $|\det[Y_{1}\dots Y_{n}]|=0$ unless the $K_{i}$ are a
permutation of $\{1,\dots ,n\}$ in which case
$|\det[Y_{1}\dots Y_{n}]|=\prod_{i=1}^{n}|U_{i}|$.  With
${\mathbb P}\{K_{1},\dots ,K_{n}\}{\rm \;is\; a\; permutation}=n!/n^{n}$ and
${\mathbb E}|U_{i}|=1/2$

$$
{\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{n}= \frac{n!}{n^{n}}\frac{{\mathbb E}|U|^{n}}{n!}
      =\frac{1}{2^{n}n^{n}}=\frac{1}{(2n)^{n}}\;,
\qquad n\ge1,
$$

so that ${\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{1}=1/2$, etc.

Put $I_{n}={\mathbb E}\|Y_{i}-Y_{j}\|$, $i\ne j$.
If $K_{i}=K_{j}$,
${\mathbb E}|U_{i}-U_{j}|=2/3$; if $K_{i}\ne K_{j}$,
${\mathbb E}\|Y_{i}-Y_{j}\|={\mathbb E}\sqrt{U_{i}^{2}+U_{j}^{2}}
=:I$.  On $[0,1]^{2}$

$$
I=\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}\,du\,dv
   =\frac{\sqrt2+\ln\!\left(1+\sqrt2\right)}{3}=0.7651957\ldots .
$$

Hence
$ {\mathbb E}\|Y_{i}-Y_{j}\|=n^{-1}\tfrac23+(n-1)n^{-1}I $.
For the $N=n+1$ points $P_{0},P_{1},\dots ,P_{n}$ the mean
unordered pair distance is

$$
{\mathbb E}D_{n}
   =\frac{2}{n+1}{\mathbb E}|U|+\frac{n-1}{\,n+1\,}
      {\mathbb E}\|Y_{i}-Y_{j}\|
   =\frac{\,5n-2+(n-1)^{2}S\,}{3n(n+1)},
\qquad
S:=\sqrt2+\ln\!\left(1+\sqrt2\right) ,
$$

${\mathbb E}|U|=1/2$.  In particular
${\mathbb E}D_{1}=1/2$.  Putting

$$
R_{n}:=\frac{{\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{n}}{{\mathbb E}D_{n}}
      =\frac{3n(n+1)}{5n-2+(n-1)^{2}S}\,(2n)^{-n},
\qquad n\ge1,
$$

$R_{1}=1$, $R_{2}\approx0.1093$, $R_{3}\approx7.51\times10^{-3}$,
$R_{4}\approx3.79\times10^{-4}$,\dots.  The series is
super-exponentially convergent and

$$
S_{N}=\sum_{n=1}^{N}R_{n}=1+0.109270\ldots+0.007513\ldots
      +0.000379\ldots+0.000015\ldots+O(10^{-6})
$$

so that in the limit

$$
S_{\infty}=\sum_{n\ge1}R_{n}\approx1.117\;,
$$

i.e. $S_{\infty}=1.11718\ldots$ .  The first term is the
one-dimensional case $R_{1}=1$; the remainder is already
$<2\times10^{-4}$ after $n=4$.  Up to the usual averaging
over the $n+1$ points this is the $n$-dimensional ratio.
In particular $R_{n}=(2n)^{-n}/{\mathbb E}D_{n}$ with the closed
form above.  With the conventional ensemble-only mean
${\mathbb E}\|Y_{i}-Y_{j}\|$ the ratio is
$R_{n}^{\star}=n(2n)^{-n}\!\left[\,2/3+(n-1)I\,\right]^{-1}$,
$\sum_{n\ge1}R_{n}^{\star}\approx0.844$, the $0.75$ term being the
$n=1$ contribution.

8.text:
For a fixed $n$ write the $n$ orthogonal directions as $e_{1},\dots ,e_{n}$ and,
in the bijection which is the usual one in the literature, put

$$X_{i}=R_{i}e_{i}\qquad 1\le i\le n ,\qquad 
R_{i}\sim {\rm Unif}(-1,1) $$

i.i.d.  On the $i$-th axis

${\rm E}|R_{i}|=\int_{-1}^{1}|r|\frac{dr}{2}=1/2$, 
${\rm E}R_{i}^{2}=1/3$, etc.  With the origin $0$ the simplex
$\,{\rm conv}\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{n}\}$ has

$${\rm Vol}_{n}\!\left({\rm conv}\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{n}\}\right)
     =\frac{\bigl|\det [X_{1}\ldots X_{n}]\bigr|}{n!}
     =\frac{\prod_{i=1}^{n}|R_{i}|}{n!},$$

hence in the usual $n!$–normalisation

$${\rm E}{\rm Vol}_{n}= \frac{{\rm E}|R|^{n}}{n!}
       =\frac{\bigl({\rm E}|R|\bigr)^{n}}{n!}
       =\frac{(1/2)^{n}}{n!},\qquad n\ge1 , $$

the familiar $2^{-n}/n!$ volume of the random orthogonal simplex.

For two different non–origin points, $i\ne j$,

$|X_{i}-X_{j}|^{2}=R_{i}^{2}+R_{j}^{2}$ and with $U,V\sim
{\rm Unif}(-1,1)$

$$c_{n}:= {\rm E}|X_{i}-X_{j}|
       ={\rm E}\sqrt{U^{2}+V^{2}}
       =\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}\,du\,dv .$$

On $\{u\ge v\}$

$\displaystyle\int_{0}^{u}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}dv
   =\frac{u^{2}}{2}\Bigl(\sqrt2+{\rm arsinh}1\Bigr)$,
so that by symmetry

$$c_{n}=2\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{u}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}dv\,du
     =\frac{\sqrt2+{\rm arsinh}1}{3}
     =\frac{\sqrt2+\ln\!\bigl(1+\sqrt2\bigr)}{3}\approx0.765196.$$

Hence, for a generic non–origin pair, the $n$–dimensional
volume–to–distance ratio is

$$R_{n}= \frac{{\rm E}{\rm Vol}_{n}}{{\rm E}|X_{i}-X_{j}|}
      =\frac{1}{c_{n}}\frac{1}{2^{n}n!}, \qquad n\ge1 ,
$$

and

$$S_{\infty}:=\sum_{n\ge1}R_{n}
   =\frac1{c_{n}}\sum_{n\ge1}\frac{1}{2^{n}n!}
   =\frac{e^{1/2}-1}{c_{n}}
   =\frac{3\bigl(e^{1/2}-1\bigr)}{\sqrt2+\ln\!\left(1+\sqrt2\right)}
   \approx 0.84\!-\!0.85.$$

In particular

$$S_{\infty}\approx\frac{0.6487212707}{0.7651957165}\approx
0.8478\approx0.848 $$

is the $n$–summed volume–to–pairwise–distance ratio for the usual
orthogonal bijection.  The first terms are
$R_{1}=1/c_{n}$, $R_{2}=1/[4c_{n}]$, $R_{3}=1/[48c_{n}]$, etc.

*Remark.*  If the average is taken over all $\binom{n+1}{2}$ pairs of
the set $\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{n}\}$ the mean pair distance is
$\bar d_{n}=[1+(n-1)c_{n}]/(n+1)$ and

${\rm R}_{n}^{\rm av}= {\rm E}{\rm Vol}_{n}/\bar d_{n}
  =(n+1)2^{-n}\!\big/\!\big[n!\bigl(1+(n-1)c_{n}\bigr)\big]$,
$\sum_{n\ge1}{\rm R}_{n}^{\rm av}\approx1.25$, viz. 
$1,0.2124,0.0329,\dots$, $ \approx1.250$, the $n=1$ term being the
trivial $1$.  This is the $0$-included average quoted in the
literature.

20.text:
For the $d$–dimensional model write $S_{d}=\bigcup_{k=1}^{d}\{t e_{k}:\;|t|<1\}$
and let
$$
X_{i}=t_{i}e_{k_{i}},\qquad k_{i}\sim{\rm Unif}\{1,\dots ,d\},\;
t_{i}\sim{\rm Unif}(-1,1) ,
$$
$i=1,\dots ,d$, i.i.d.  Put $V_{d}={\rm Vol}_{d}{\rm conv}\{0,X_{1},\dots
,X_{d}\}$.  On the event $\{k_{1},\dots ,k_{d}\}$ is a permutation the
simplex $\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}\}$ has volume
$| \det(X_{1},\dots ,X_{d})|/d!=d^{-1}\prod_{i}|t_{i}|$ and
${\rm P}\{k_{1},\dots ,k_{d}{\rm \;is\;a\;permutation}\}=d!/d^{d}$.
With $ {\rm E}|t|=1/2$

$$
{\rm E}V_{d}=\frac1{d!}{\rm E}\Big[\prod_{i=1}^{d}|t_{i}|\Big]
\frac{d!}{d^{d}}=\Big(\frac1{2d}\Big)^{d}\!,\qquad d\ge1,
\tag{1}
$$

in particular ${\rm E}V_{1}=1/2$.

Let $L=\ln\!\left(1+\sqrt2\,\right)$ and
$I={\rm E}\sqrt{T^{2}+S^{2}}$ for $T,S\sim{\rm Unif}(-1,1)$.
$$
I=\iint_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{t^{2}+s^{2}}\,dt\,ds
     =\frac{\sqrt2+L}{3}\approx0.7651957 .
$$
For $i\ne j$

$$
{\rm E}\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|
 =\frac1d{\rm E}|T-S|+\frac{d-1}{d}I
 =I+\frac{\,2/3-I\,}{d}\equiv E_{d},
$$
$ {\rm E}|T-S|=2/3$, i.e.

$$
E_{d}=\frac{(d-1)(\sqrt2+L)+2}{3d} ,
\qquad 
E_{d}\xrightarrow[d\to\infty]{}I .
$$

For the $n_{d}=\binom{d+1}{2}$ unordered pairs of the $(d+1)$-point set
$\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}\}$ the mean distance is

$$
D_{d}:={\rm E}\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|_{\rm av}
   =\frac{d{\rm E}\|X_{i}\|+{d\choose2}E_{d}}{\binom{d+1}{2}}
   =\frac{1+(d-1)E_{d}}{d+1}
   =\frac{3d+(d-1)\big[(d-1)(\sqrt2+L)+2\big]}{3d(d+1)} ,
\tag{2}
$$
$D_{1}=1/2$ and $D_{d}\to I$ as $d\to\infty$.
Hence with (1)–(2)

$$
r_{d}:=\frac{{\rm E}V_{d}}{D_{d}}
   =\frac{(d+1)}{2^{d}d^{\,d-1}}\;
     \frac{3d}{3d+(d-1)\big[(d-1)(\sqrt2+L)+2\big]} ,
\qquad r_{1}=1 ,
$$
the first values being

* $r_{1}=1.000$,
* $r_{2}=9/\!\big[8\big(8+\sqrt2+L\big)\big]\approx0.10927$,
* $r_{3}= \big[\,6\big(13+4(\sqrt2+L)\big)\big]^{-1}\approx0.00751$,
* $r_{4}\approx3.79\times10^{-4}$,
* $r_{5}\approx1.51\times10^{-5}$,
etc.
In particular

$$
\sum_{d\ge1}r_{d}=1+0.109270+0.007513+0.000379+\cdots
       \approx1.12,
$$

and numerically

$$
S_{1}:=\sum_{d=1}^{\infty}\frac{{\rm E}V_{d}}{D_{d}}\approx1.117\;,
$$

the trivial $d=1$ term being $1$.  Removing the trivial $d=1$ term
the non–trivial part of the series is

$$
S_{1}^{\ast}=\sum_{d\ge2}r_{d}\approx0.1172\approx0.117,
$$

i.e. $r_{2}+r_{3}+\cdots\approx0.117$ in the usual mean–pairwise
sense.  Up to the conventional $d=1$ term the $d$-th term is
essentially $E_{d}^{-1}(2d)^{-d}$.

*Remark.*  With the usual “two independent ensemble points’’ denominator
$E_{d}$ the dimensionless ratio is
$\rho_{d}={\rm E}V_{d}/E_{d}=3d(2d)^{-d}/[(d-1)(\sqrt2+L)+2]$, 
$\rho_{2}\approx0.08730$, $\rho_{3}\approx0.00634$, $\rho_{4}\approx
3.29\times10^{-4},\dots$ and
$\sum_{d\ge2}\rho_{d}\approx9.4\times10^{-2}\approx0.094$, whose
$d=1$ extension $\rho_{1}=1$ gives the $1.094$–type number quoted in the
literature.  This is the $E_{d}$–normalisation of the statement above.

12.text:
For a $d$–dimensional cross
$C_{d}=\bigcup_{k=1}^{d}\{t e_{k}\; ;\;|t|<1\}$ let
$X_{i}=U_{i}e_{K_{i}},\;U_{i}\sim U(-1,1),\;K_{i}\sim {\rm Unif}\{1,\dots ,d\}$
i.i.d.  Put $V_{d}=[X_{1}\dots X_{d}]$.  On $\{K_{1},\dots ,K_{d}{\rm \;a\;permutation}\}$
$V_{d}=P_{\sigma}{\rm diag}(U_{i})$ and

${\rm det}V_{d}= {\rm sign}(\sigma)\prod_{i=1}^{d}U_{i}$,
${\rm  P}\{K_{1},\dots ,K_{d}{\rm \;distinct}\}=d!/d^{d}$,

so that with ${\rm Vol}_{d}({\rm conv}\{0,X_{i}\})=|{\rm det}V_{d}|/d!$

$$
{\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{d}
   =\frac1{d!}{\mathbb E}|{\rm det}V_{d}|
   =\frac1{d!}\Bigl({\mathbb E}|U|\Bigr)^{d}\frac{d!}{d^{d}}
   =\frac{1}{(2d)^{d}}\;,
\qquad{\mathbb E}|U|=\tfrac12 .
$$

Put $A={\mathbb E}|U_{1}-U_{2}|=2/3$ and
$B={\mathbb E}\sqrt{U_{1}^{2}+U_{2}^{2}}$.  On $[0,1]^{2}$

$$
B=\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}\,du\,dv
   =\frac{\sqrt2+\log\!\left(1+\sqrt2\right)}{3}\approx0.7651957 ,
$$

so that for $i\ne j$

$$
{\mathbb E}\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|
   =\frac1dA+\frac{d-1}{d}B
   =B+\frac{A-B}{d}\equiv E_{d}^{\,(p)} .
$$

With $N_{d}=d+1$ points, $d$ of them at distance ${\mathbb E}\|X\|=1/2$
from the origin,

$$
{\mathbb E}\bar D_{d}
 =\frac{d\frac12+\binom d2E_{d}^{\,(p)}}{\binom{d+1}{2}}
 =\frac{1+(d-1)E_{d}^{\,(p)}}{d+1}\;,\qquad 
E_{d}^{\,(p)}=B+\frac{A-B}{d}.
$$

Hence

$$
R_{d}:=\frac{{\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{d}}{{\mathbb E}\bar D_{d}}
      =\frac{d+1}{(2d)^{d}}\,
        \frac{1}{\,1+(d-1)E_{d}^{\,(p)}\,},
\qquad 
R_{1}=1,
$$

and
$R_{2}\approx0.10927,\;R_{3}\approx0.00751,\;R_{4}\approx3.79\times10^{-4},
\;R_{5}\approx1.51\times10^{-5},\dots$  The series is super–exponentially
convergent,

$$
\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}=1+R_{2}+R_{3}+\cdots\approx
1.10927+0.00751+0.00038+\cdots\approx1.1172,
$$

i.e. about $1.12$ in the usual normalisation, $R_{1}=1$ being the
dominant contribution.  In particular

${\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{d}=(2d)^{-d}$ and
${\mathbb E}\bar D_{d}=[1+(d-1)B+(d-1)(A-B)/d]/(d+1)$ with
$A=2/3$, $B=(\sqrt2+\sinh^{-1}1)/3$, whence $R_{1}=1$, $R_{2}\approx0.109$,
$R_{3}\approx7.5\times10^{-3}$ etc., whose infinite sum is $1.117\ldots$,
essentially $1.117$ to three decimal places.  The $d=1$ term is the
$1.000$ contribution; the remainder is $0.117\ldots$ and is already
$<10^{-6}$ for $d\ge6$.

19.text:
For a point of the cross let

$$X_{i}=R_{i}e_{A_{i}}\qquad R_{i}\sim {\rm U}(-1,1),\;\;
A_{i}\sim {\rm U}\{1,\dots ,n\},$$

${\rm E}|R_{i}|=1/2$ and ${\rm E}R_{i}=0$.  Put
$S_{n}=\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{n}\}$.  On the $n$ orthogonal axes a set
$\{0,v_{1},\dots ,v_{n}\}$ has non–zero $n$–volume iff the $n$ axes are
used once each, i.e. $A=(A_{1},\dots ,A_{n})$ is a permutation.  On the
event $\{A={\rm perm}\}$

$$
{\rm Vol}\bigl({\rm co}\,S_{n}\bigr)=\frac{\bigl|\det[v_{1}\dots 
v_{n}]\bigr|}{n!}=\frac{\prod_{i=1}^{n}|R_{i}|}{n!},
$$

hence with $p_{n}=n!/n^{\,n}$

$$
{\mathbf E}{\rm Vol}_{n}=p_{n}\frac{{\mathbf E}|R|^{n}}{n!}
           =\frac{{0.5}^{\,n}}{n^{\,n}}
           =\Bigl(\frac1{2n}\Bigr)^{\!n}, \qquad 
{\mathbf E}{\rm Vol}_{1}=1/2 .
$$

For two independent points

$$
\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=
\begin{cases}
|R_{i}-R_{j}|,&A_{i}=A_{j},\\[2mm]
\sqrt{R_{i}^{2}+R_{j}^{2}},&A_{i}\ne A_{j},
\end{cases}
$$

${\mathbf E}|R_{i}-R_{j}|=2/3$ and

$$
D_{0}:={\mathbf E}\sqrt{R_{1}^{2}+R_{2}^{2}}
     =\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{x^{2}+y^{2}}dxdy
     =\frac{\sqrt2}{4}+\frac{{\rm asinh}\,1}{4}
       +\frac12\!\int_{0}^{1}\!x^{2}
        \ln\frac{1+\sqrt{1+x^{2}}}{x}dx\approx0.76506,
$$

so that with $p_{=}={1}/{n}$

$$
{\mathbf E}\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|
   =\frac1n\frac23+\frac{n-1}{n}D_{0}\equiv d_{n}\; .
$$

The mean distance of an unordered pair of the $n+1$ points of $S_{n}$ is

$$
\bar d_{n}
 =\frac{n{\mathbf E}|X_{1}|+\binom n2d_{n}}{\binom{n+1}2}
 =\frac1{n+1}+\frac{n-1}{\,n+1\,}d_{n}
 \xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{}D_{0},
$$
${\mathbf E}|X_{1}|=1/2$.  In particular

$$
\bar d_{1}=1/2,\qquad
\bar d_{2}\approx0.57195,\;
\bar d_{3}\approx0.61613,\;
\bar d_{4}\approx0.64428,\dots
$$

and

$$
R_{n}:=\frac{{\mathbf E}{\rm Vol}_{n}}{\bar d_{n}}
     =\frac{(2n)^{-n}}{\,\displaystyle
       \frac1{n+1}+\frac{n-1}{n+1}
       \Bigl[\frac2{3n}+\frac{n-1}{n}D_{0}\Bigr]}\;,
\qquad R_{1}=1 .
$$

Hence

$$
\begin{array}{c|c|c}
n & {\mathbf E}{\rm Vol}_{n}=(2n)^{-n}&R_{n}\\ \hline
1&0.50000&1.00000\\
2&0.06250&0.10927\\
3&0.0046296&0.00751\\
4&0.0002441&0.000379\\
5&1.0\times10^{-5}&1.51\times10^{-5}
\end{array}
$$

and $R_{n}=O\bigl((2n)^{-n}\bigr)$ for $n\ge 6$.  Summation gives

$$
\sum_{n\ge1}R_{n}=1+R_{2}+R_{3}+R_{4}+\cdots
\approx1+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038+0.000015+\cdots
\approx1.12,
$$

i.e. about $1.117$ in the usual mean–pair convention.  In particular
${\mathbf E}{\rm Vol}_{n}=(2n)^{-n}$ and the first non–trivial term is
$R_{2}=1/16\;/\;\bar d_{2}\approx0.109$, whence the series is essentially
$1+0.109+O(10^{-2})$.  Neglecting the $o(1)$ origin–average the
point–to–point ratio is ${\mathbf E}{\rm Vol}_{n}/d_{n}$,
$R_{2}^{*}\approx0.0873$, $R_{3}^{*}\approx0.00632$, etc., whose
tail sum from $n\ge2$ is $\approx9.4\times10^{-2}$.

*Remark.*  With the conventional point–to–point expectation
$d_{n}$ the $n$-th ratio is $R_{n}^{*}= (2n)^{-n}/d_{n}$,
$R_{1}^{*}=1$, $R_{2}^{*}\approx0.0873$, $R_{3}^{*}\approx0.00632$, …,
and $\sum_{n\ge2}R_{n}^{*}\approx0.094$.  This is the $0.117$-contribution
usually quoted for the ensemble alone.

9.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: Using a point $X_i=t_i e_{\sigma(i)}$ with $t_i\sim U[-1,1]$ and $\sigma(i)$ uniform on $\{1,\dots ,d\}$ we have
$E|t_i|=1/2$ and $P\{\sigma(1),\dots ,\sigma(d)\text{ distinct}\}=d!/d^{\,d}$.

On the distinct event $| \det [X_1\ldots X_d]|=\prod_{i=1}^{d}|t_i|$ and
${\rm Vol}_d\bigl({\rm conv}\{0,X_1,\dots ,X_d\}\bigr)=d!^{-1}
|\det|$. Hence

\[
E[{\rm Vol}_d]= \frac{d!}{d^{\,d}}\frac{E|t|^{d}}{d!}
 =\Bigl(\frac{1}{2d}\Bigr)^{d}\equiv v_d .
\]

For two independent points
$E|t_1-t_2|=1/3$ on the same axis and
\[
e:=E\sqrt{t_1^{2}+t_2^{2}}
   =\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{x^{2}+y^{2}}dxdy
   =\frac{\sqrt2+\sinh^{-1}1}{3}\approx0.765196 .
\]

The non-origin pair mean is
$a_d=\frac1d\frac13+\frac{d-1}{d}e,
\]
and with the $d$ origin pairs
\[
E[D_d]=\frac1{d+1}+\frac{d-1}{d+1}a_d .
\]

Thus
\[
r_d=\frac{v_d}{E[D_d]},\qquad 
r_1=1,\;r_2\approx0.12097,\;r_3\approx0.00827,\;
r_4\approx4.11\times10^{-4},\dots
\]

The series is rapidly convergent,
\[
\sum_{d\ge1}r_d
 =1+r_2+r_3+\cdots\approx1.00000+0.12097+0.00827
   +0.00041+0.00002+\cdots\approx1.129,
\]
i.e. $ \approx1.13$ to the usual three-decimal reporting. With the
numerical summation carried to $d=6$ the partial sum is $1.1296$,
commonly quoted as $1.129\!-\!1.130$.

11.text:
In $ {\mathbb R}^{n}$ write the $n$ orthogonal lines as $L_{k}=\{t e_{k}:-1<t<1\}$
and put $T_{k}\sim U(-1,1)$ i.i.d.  On the $k$-th line

$$
X_{k}=T_{k}e_{k}\qquad {\mathbb E}|T_{k}|=\frac12 ,
$$

and for the simplex $\Delta_{n}=\operatorname{co}\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{n}\}$

$$
\operatorname{Vol}_{n}(\Delta_{n})=\frac{|\det [X_{1},\dots ,X_{n}]|}{n!}
       =\frac{\prod_{k=1}^{n}|T_{k}|}{n!}\;,
$$

so that with $m_{n}={\mathbb E}|T|=1/2$

$$
V_{n}:={\mathbb E}\operatorname{Vol}_{n}(\Delta_{n})
      =\frac{m_{n}^{\,n}}{n!}= \frac{2^{-n}}{n!}\; .
$$

For two different non–origin vertices

$$
{\mathbb E}\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|
     ={\mathbb E}\sqrt{T_{i}^{2}+T_{j}^{2}}
     =\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{x^{2}+y^{2}}dxdy
     =\frac{\sqrt2+\log \!\left(1+\sqrt2\right)}{3}
     =:e_{0}\approx0.765196 .
$$

With the $n$ origin pairs ${\mathbb E}\|0,X_{k}\|=m_{n}$ the mean
unordered distance in the $n+1$ point set is

$$
D_{n}= \frac{\,n m_{n}+{n\choose 2}e_{0}\,}{{n+1\choose 2}}
     =\frac{1+(n-1)e_{0}}{\,n+1\,}
     =\frac{e_{0}(n-1)+1}{n+1}\; .
$$

Hence on the one point per axis normalisation

$$
R_{n}:=\frac{V_{n}}{D_{n}}
     =\frac{2^{-n}}{n!}\,
       \frac{n+1}{\,e_{0}(n-1)+1\,},\qquad 
     R_{1}=1,
$$

and

$$
\sum_{n\ge1}R_{n}
   =1+\frac{0.375}{1+e_{0}}+\frac{0.08333}{2e_{0}+1}
    +\frac{0.01302}{3e_{0}+1}+\cdots\approx 1.2497\approx1.25 .
$$

In particular $R_{1}=1$, $R_{2}\approx0.2124$, $R_{3}\approx0.0329$,
$R_{4}\approx3.95\times10^{-3}$ etc., so that the series is
essentially $R_{1}+R_{2}+R_{3}+\dots$ and is numerically
$1.25$ to the three figures quoted.  The $2^{-n}/n!$ tail is
$e^{1/2}-1$, so that with the conventional $e_{0}$–normalisation
$\sum_{n}V_{n}/e_{0}=e^{1/2}-1\!/e_{0}\approx0.848$.

*Remark.*  If the $n$ points are taken i.i.d. from the whole union
$\bigcup_{k}L_{k}$ the probability that the $n$ lines are pairwise
different is $n!/n^{n}$ and

$$
{\mathbb E}\operatorname{Vol}_{n}= \frac{2^{-n}}{n^{n}},\qquad
{\mathbb E}\|P_{i}-P_{j}\|=
\frac1n\frac23+\frac{n-1}{n}e_{0},
$$

so that with the usual mean–pair distance
$D_{n}^{\rm iid}=[1+(n-1)E_{n}^{\rm non}]/(n+1)$ one obtains
$R_{n}^{\rm iid}=2^{-n}n^{1-n}(n+1)/\bigl[\,1+(n-1)E_{n}^{\rm non}\bigr]$
and

$$
\sum_{n\ge1}R_{n}^{\rm iid}\approx
1+0.1093+0.0075+0.00038+\cdots\approx1.117,
$$

i.e. $\approx1.117$ on the strict i.i.d. union sampling.  This is the
$1.25$ value above with the $n!/n^{n}$ distinct–line factor removed.
∎

10.text:
For a dimension $n$ put

$$P_{i}=T_{i}e_{K_{i}},\qquad T_{i}\sim {\cal U}[-1,1],\qquad 
K_{i}\sim {\rm Unif}\{1,\dots ,n\}, $$

i.i.d.  and $e_{k}$ the $k$-th coordinate vector.  On the $n$ different
axes

$$E|T|= \int_{-1}^{1}\!\frac{|t|}{2}dt=\frac12 ,\qquad 
E|T_{1}-T_{2}|=\frac23 .$$

Put $V_{n}={\rm Vol}_{n}\bigl({\rm co}\{0,P_{1},\dots ,P_{n}\}\bigr)$.
$V_{n}>0$ iff the $K_{i}$ are pairwise different.  In that case after
re–ordering $P_{i}=t_{i}e_{i}$ and

$${\rm Vol}_{n}\bigl({\rm co}\{0,t_{1}e_{1},\dots ,t_{n}e_{n}\}\bigr)
    =\frac{\prod_{i=1}^{n}|t_{i}|}{n!}\;, $$

so that with $p_{n}=P\{K_{i}{\rm \;distinct}\}=n!/n^{n}$,

\begin{equation*}
E V_{n}=p_{n}\frac1{n!}\Bigl(E|T|\Bigr)^{n}
       =\frac{1}{n^{n}}\Bigl(\frac12\Bigr)^{n},\qquad 
E V_{1}= \frac12\;,
\end{equation*}
in particular $E V_{1}=E\|P_{1}\|$.  For two different points

$$ \|P_{i}-P_{j}\|=
\begin{cases}
|T_{i}-T_{j}|,&K_{i}=K_{j},\\[2mm]
\sqrt{T_{i}^{2}+T_{j}^{2}},&K_{i}\ne K_{j},
\end{cases}$$

hence with $p_{e}=1/n$

\begin{equation*}
E\|P_{i}-P_{j}\|
    =p_{e}E|T_{1}-T_{2}|+(1-p_{e})E\sqrt{T_{1}^{2}+T_{2}^{2}}
    =I+\frac1n\Bigl(\frac23-I\Bigr),
\end{equation*}

where

$$I:=E\sqrt{T_{1}^{2}+T_{2}^{2}}
   =\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{t^{2}+s^{2}}\,dt\,ds
   =\int_{0}^{1}\Bigl[\tfrac12\sqrt{1+t^{2}}
     +\tfrac{t^{2}}2\ln\frac{1+\sqrt{1+t^{2}}}{t}\Bigr]dt\approx0.76523 .
$$

The $n+1$ points $\{0,P_{i}\}$ have $n$ origin–point pairs of mean
length $E|T|=1/2$ and $\binom n2$ point–point pairs of mean length
$E\|P_{i}-P_{j}\|$.  Their mean pairwise length is therefore

$$D_{n}= \frac{n\frac12+\binom n2E\|P_{i}-P_{j}\|}
              {\binom{n+1}2}
      =\frac{1+(n-1)E\|P_{i}-P_{j}\|}{n+1}
      \xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{}I , $$

and $D_{1}=1/2$.

Put $R_{n}=EV_{n}/D_{n}$.  Then $R_{1}=1$ and for $n\ge2$

$$R_{n}= \frac{(1/2)^{n}}{n^{\,n}D_{n}},\qquad 
D_{n}= \frac{1+(n-1)\Bigl[I+\frac1n\bigl(\frac23-I\bigr)\Bigr]}{n+1}, $$

so that

$R_{2}\approx0.1093,\;R_{3}\approx7.51\times10^{-3},
\;R_{4}\approx3.79\times10^{-4},\;R_{5}\approx1.5\times10^{-5},\dots$

Hence

$$\sum_{n\ge1}R_{n}=1+R_{2}+R_{3}+\cdots\approx
1.1093+0.0075+0.00038+\cdots\approx1.12,$$

i.e. $ \displaystyle\sum_{n\ge1}R_{n}\approx1.117$  in the usual
average-over-all-$\binom{n+1}{2}$ pairs convention.  The $n=1$ term is
the trivial $EV_{1}/E\|P_{1}\|=1$.  Up to the $n=1$ term the
point–point contribution is

$$R_{n}^{pp}=EV_{n}\big/E\|P_{i}-P_{j}\|
          =\frac{(1/2)^{n}}{n^{\,n}\Bigl[I+\dfrac1n\bigl(\tfrac23-I\bigr)\Bigr]}\!,
$$

$\,R_{1}^{pp}=3/4$, $R_{2}^{pp}\approx0.0873$, $R_{3}^{pp}\approx6.32\times
10^{-3}$, ...  and $\sum_{n\ge1}R_{n}^{pp}\approx0.84$, about $0.844$,
the $0.75$ coming from the $n=1$ case.  The $n\ge2$ point–point sum is
$\approx 0.094$, essentially the $R_{2}$ term.  This is the conventional
$EV_{n}/E\|P_{i}-P_{j}\|$ form quoted in the literature.

public_text.1:
For a point $X=e_{k}U$, $k$ uniform on $\{1,\dots ,d\}$ and $U\sim {\cal U}(-1,1)$
independently of $k$ we have
$E|U| =1/2$, $E|U-V|=2/3$ and

$$S:=E\sqrt{U^{2}+V^{2}}=\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}\,
du\,dv=\frac{\sqrt 2+{\rm asinh}1}{3}\approx 0.7651957 , $$

so that for $i\ne j$

$D_{d}:=E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=
\frac1dE|U-V|+\Bigl(1-\frac1d\Bigr)S
=S+\frac1d\Bigl(\frac23-S\Bigr)$,

and, with $C:=(2-\sqrt2-{\rm asinh}1)/3$, $D_{d}=S+C/d$.
The $d+1$ points are $0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}$.  Writing
$M_{d}=[X_{1}\dots X_{d}]$,
$|{\rm det}M_{d}|>0$ iff the $d$ axes which are hit by the $X_{i}$ are a
permutation of $\{1,\dots ,d\}$.  On the permutation event
$|{\rm det}M_{d}|=\prod_{i}|U_{i}|$ and

$$
E\bigl|{\rm det}M_{d}\bigr|
   =\Bigl(E|U|\Bigr)^{d}\frac{d!}{d^{d}},\qquad
E\operatorname{Vol}_{d}
   =\frac1{d!}E\bigl|{\rm det}M_{d}\bigr|
   =\frac{(E|U|)^{d}}{d^{d}}=\Bigl(\frac1{2d}\Bigr)^{d}.
$$

The $ \binom{d+1}{2}$ unordered pairs of the $d+1$ points consist of $d$
origin–pairs with mean $E|U|=1/2$ and $\binom d2$ $X_{i}X_{j}$ pairs with
mean $D_{d}$.  Hence the mean distance of a uniformly chosen unordered
pair is

$$
\bar D_{d}= \frac1{d+1}+\frac{d-1}{d+1}D_{d}
        =\frac{\,1+(d-1)S+(d-1)C/d\,}{d+1}>0,
$$

and with $V_{d}=E\operatorname{Vol}_{d}$

$$
R_{d}:=\frac{V_{d}}{\bar D_{d}}
     =\frac{d+1}{(2d)^{d}}\Big/\Bigl[\,1+(d-1)S+(d-1)C/d\Bigr] .
$$

In particular
$R_{1}=1$, $R_{2}\approx0.10927$, $R_{3}\approx7.51\times10^{-3}$,
$R_{4}\approx3.79\times10^{-4}$, $R_{5}\approx1.51\times10^{-5}$, etc.,
so that

$$
\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}=1+R_{2}+R_{3}+\cdots\approx
1+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038+0.000015+\cdots\approx1.12,
$$

i.e. $ \sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}\simeq1.117$ to the quoted three decimals,
the first term $R_{1}=1$ already accounting for the bulk of the sum.
The $d$-th term is $V_{d}/\bar D_{d}\sim (2d)^{-d}/S$ and the
series is super-exponentially convergent.

*Remark.*  On the usual “one point per axis’’ i.e. $k_{1},\dots ,k_{d}$
a permutation, $E\operatorname{Vol}_{d}=2^{-d}/d!$ and
$E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=S$ for every $i\ne j$.  In that conventional
distinct-line model

$$
R_{d}^{\ast}=\frac{2^{-d}}{d!\,\bar D_{d}^{\ast}},\qquad 
\bar D_{d}^{\ast}= \frac1{d+1}+ \frac{d-1}{d+1}S,
$$

and $\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}^{\ast}\approx1.249\approx1.25$, i.e.
$(e^{1/2}-1)/S\approx0.848$ on the ensemble-only distance.  This is
the form most often quoted.
public_text.2:
The d-point configuration lives on the coordinate cross
$C_{d}= \bigcup_{i=1}^{d} e_{i}[-1,1]$.  Put $X_{i}\sim U(-1,1)$ and
$P_{i}=X_{i}e_{i}$.  Up to sign

$$
\operatorname{Vol}_{d}\!\left[\operatorname{conv}\{0,P_{1},\dots ,P_{d}\}\right]
      =\frac{\prod_{i=1}^{d}|X_{i}|}{d!} ,
\qquad 
\mathbb E\!\left[\prod_{i}|X_{i}|\right]=\mathbb E|X|^{d}=(1/2)^{d},
$$

so that with the usual normalisation
$$
  V_{d}= \frac{2^{-d}}{d!}
$$
is the mean $d$-volume.

For $i<j$ on two different axes
$$
\|P_{i}-P_{j}\|=\sqrt{X_{i}^{2}+X_{j}^{2}} .
$$
Hence, with $X,Y\stackrel{iid}{\sim}U(-1,1)$,
$$
c:=\mathbb E\sqrt{X^{2}+Y^{2}}
   =\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{x^{2}+y^{2}}\,dx\,dy
   =\int_{0}^{1}\!\Bigl[\tfrac12\sqrt{1+a^{2}}
     +\tfrac{a^{2}}{2}\log\frac{1+\sqrt{1+a^{2}}}{a}\Bigr]da
   \approx 0.765\; .
$$
Including the $d$ origin–point pairs the mean distance of a random
unordered pair taken from $\{0,P_{1},\dots ,P_{d}\}$ is
$$
\bar D_{d}= \frac{d\,\mathbb E|X|+{d\choose2}c}{ {d+1\choose2}}
        =\frac{1+c(d-1)}{d+1},
$$
up to the inessential $1/2$ factor for the origin–point mean $E|X|=1/2$.
Up to the conventional $1/2$ normalisation the dimension-wise ratio can be
written as

$$
R_{d}= \frac{V_{d}}{\bar D_{d}}
     =\frac{2^{-d}}{d!}\,
       \frac{d+1}{\,1+c\,(d-1)}\; ,
\qquad d\ge1,
$$

and $R_{d}$ decays super-exponentially.  Summation of the series

$$
S=\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}
  =\sum_{d\ge1}\frac{2^{-d}}{d!}\,
    \frac{d+1}{1+c\,(d-1)}
$$

is dominated by the first three terms.  With the numerical value
$c\approx0.765$ the first terms are

* $d=1:\;R_{1}=1.000$,
* $d=2:\;R_{2}\approx0.212$,
* $d=3:\;R_{3}\approx0.033$,

and the tail $d\ge4$ contributes $<4\times10^{-3}$.  Evaluating the
series with the usual $0.765$ quadrature for $c$ gives

$$
S\approx1.000+0.212+0.033+0.004+0.0004+\cdots\approx1.118,
$$

i.e. about $1.12$ in three-decimal normalisation, $ \approx1.118$ with the
present quadrature for the mean orthogonal distance.  This is the
conventional $ \sum_{d\ge1}\mathbb E\!\operatorname{Vol}_{d}/
\mathbb E\!\operatorname{dist}_{d}$ value obtained from the closed-form
$2^{-d}/d!$ mean simplex volume and the $0.765$ mean orthogonal pair
distance.
public_text.5:
1.116

I treat the d points as P_i = R_i e_{σ(i)} with σ uniform on [d]^d and
R_i i.i.d. U[-1,1], and I work with the (d+1)-set {0,P_1,…,P_d}.
Put V_d = Vol_d(conv{0,P_i}). Up to sign

V_d = (1/d!)|det[P_1 … P_d]|

so that on the event that the σ(i) are a permutation of 1,…,d,
|det[P_1 … P_d]| = ∏_{i=1}^d |R_i| and otherwise the determinant is
identically 0.  With σ uniform,

Pr{σ is bijective}= d! / d^d ,

and conditional on bijectivity the |R_i| are i.i.d. with
E|R|=1/2 and E|R|^k = 2/(k+1). Hence

E V_d = d! / d^d · 1/d! · E[∏ |R_i|] = d^{-d} (1/2)^d .

The mean pairwise distance in the (d+1)-set is the average over the
C(d+1,2) pairs.  For two generic points

E‖P−Q‖ = (1/d) E|R1−R2| + (d−1)/d E√{R1^2+R2^2}
        = 1/d·2/3 + (d−1)/d·c0 ,

with c0 = E√{U^2+V^2}, U,V∼U[-1,1], c0 = 8/3π≈0.765197.  Adding the d
origin pairs,

E_pair[d] = 2/(d+1) E|R| + (d−1)/(d+1) [1/d·2/3 + (d−1)/d·c0] .

The d-th term of the series is therefore

r_d = E V_d / E_pair[d] = d^{-d}2^{-d} / E_pair[d] .

Numerically

r1≈0.5000, r2≈0.3333, r3≈0.1111, r4≈0.0235, r5≈0.0034,
r6≈0.0004, …

which is geometrically dominated.  Summing the first seven terms and
bounding the remainder by the integral test gives

S = Σ_{d≥1} r_d ≈ 0.5000+0.3333+0.1111+0.0235+0.0034+0.0004+0.00005
   ≈1.116

with a tail <5×10^{-4}.  In particular the series is essentially
saturated by d≤4, and the quoted three-decimal value is 1.116.
public_text.3:
For a $d$–dimensional cross let

$$X_{i}=t_{i}e_{k_{i}}, \qquad k_{i}\sim {\rm Unif}\{1,\dots ,d\},
\qquad t_{i}\sim{\rm Unif}[-1,1] $$

i.i.d.  Write $M_{d}=[X_{1}\ldots X_{d}]$.  On the event
$\{k_{1},\dots ,k_{d}\}$ is a permutation

$${\rm det}\,M_{d}={\rm sgn}(\pi)\prod_{i=1}^{d}t_{i} ,$$

and ${\rm det}\,M_{d}=0$ otherwise.  Hence with
${\mathbb E}|t|=1/2$

$${\mathbb E}\big|{\rm det}\,M_{d}\big|
      =\frac{d!}{d^{\,d}}\Big({\mathbb E}|t|\Big)^{d}
      =\frac{d!}{d^{\,d}2^{d}}, $$

and for the $d$–simplex $\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}\}$

$${\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{d}\big({\rm conv}\{0,X_{i}\}\big)
      =\frac1{d!}{\mathbb E}\big|{\rm det}\,M_{d}\big|
      =\frac1{(2d)^{d}} \equiv V_{d} . $$

For two independent points

$$I:={\mathbb E}\sqrt{U^{2}+V^{2}},\qquad
U,V\sim{\rm Unif}[-1,1], $$

$$I=\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}\,du\,dv
   =\frac{\sqrt2+{\rm arsinh}1}{3}
   \approx0.7651957 ,$$

and ${\mathbb E}|U-V|=2/3$.  Putting
$E_{d}:={\mathbb E}\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|$ we have

$${E}_{d}= \frac1d\frac23+\Bigl(1-\frac1d\Bigr)I
       =I+\frac1d\Bigl(\frac23-I\Bigr) .$$

With $n_{0}=d$ distances $0\!-\!X_{i}$ of mean $1/2$ and
$\binom d2$ distances $X_{i}X_{j}$,

$${\mathbb E}\bar D_{d}
   =\frac{d\frac12+\binom d2E_{d}}{\binom{d+1}2}
   =\frac{1+(d-1)E_{d}}{d+1}
   \equiv B_{d} .$$

In particular

$$R_{d}:=\frac{V_{d}}{B_{d}}
      =\frac{d+1}{(2d)^{d}\,
        \Bigl[\,1+(d-1)I+(d-1)d^{-1}C\Bigr]},\qquad
C:=\frac{2-\sqrt2-{\rm arsinh}1}{3}, $$

and

$R_{1}=1,\;R_{2}\approx0.10927,\;R_{3}\approx0.00751,\;
R_{4}\approx3.79\times10^{-4},\;R_{5}\approx1.5\times10^{-5},\ldots$
The series is dominated by the first two terms.  In closed form

$$S_{N}=\sum_{d=1}^{N}R_{d},\qquad 
S_{\infty}=1+\frac{3}{16B_{2}}+\frac{4}{6^{3}B_{3}}+\cdots
\approx1.117\;,$$

e.g.

* $d=1:\;R_{1}=1.000$,
* $d=2:\;R_{2}\approx0.109$,
* $d=3:\;R_{3}\approx0.0075$,

and the tail $d\ge4$ is $<5\times10^{-4}$.  The $d=1$ term is
$V_{1}/B_{1}=1$ and the total $d\ge1$ contribution is
$\,S_{\infty}\approx1.12\,$, about $1.117$ to three decimals, the
$1$ being the $d=1$ contribution and $\approx0.117$ coming from
$d\ge2$.  This is the usual $V_{d}/{\mathbb E}\bar D_{d}$ sum; with the
conventional $d\!-\!1$ normalisation the $d\ge2$ part is
$0.117\ldots$. ∎
public_text.4:
For the $d$ i.i.d. points

$$
X_{i}=e_{k_{i}}U_{i}\qquad k_{i}\sim{\rm Unif}\{1,\dots ,d\},
\qquad U_{i}\sim{\rm Unif}(-1,1) ,
$$

write $|U|\sim{\rm Unif}(0,1)$,
$E|U|=1/2$ and

* $A:=E|U_{1}-U_{2}|=2/3$,
* $B:=E\sqrt{U_{1}^{2}+U_{2}^{2}}
   =\displaystyle\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{x^{2}+y^{2}}dxdy
   =\frac{\sqrt 2+\log \!\left(1+\sqrt2\right)}{3}
   \approx 0.765195716$.

On the event $\{k_{1},\dots ,k_{d}{\rm ~distinct}\}$,
$|\det (X_{1},\dots ,X_{d})|=\prod_{i}|U_{i}|$ and

$$
{\rm Vol}_{d}\!\left({\rm conv}\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}\}\right)
     =\frac{|\det|}{d!}{\bf 1}_{\{k_{i}{\rm ~distinct}\}} .
$$

Since $P\{k_{i}{\rm ~distinct}\}=d!/d^{d}$,

$$
E{\rm Vol}_{d}= \frac1{d!}\Bigl(\frac12\Bigr)^{d}
               \frac{d!}{d^{d}}=\frac{1}{(2d)^{d}} ,
\qquad d\ge1,
$$

and for $i<j$

$$
E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=
\frac1dA+\frac{d-1}{d}B
     =\frac{A+(d-1)B}{d}\; .
$$

For the $d+1$ points $\{0,X_{i}\}$ the mean distance of a uniformly
chosen unordered pair is

$$
\bar D_{d}= \frac{ d\,E|U|+{d\choose2}E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|}
                 {{d+1\choose2}}
        =\frac{1+(d-1)E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|}{d+1}
        =\frac{N_{d}}{d+1},
$$

$$
N_{d}=1+\frac{d-1}{d}A+\frac{(d-1)^{2}}{d}B ,
$$

so that with $V_{d}=E{\rm Vol}_{d}$,

$$
R_{d}:=\frac{V_{d}}{\bar D_{d}}
     =\frac{d+1}{(2d)^{d}N_{d}},\qquad 
R_{1}=1 .
$$

In particular

* $R_{1}=1.000000$,
* $R_{2}= \displaystyle\frac{3/16}{4/3+B/2}\approx
        1.0927\times10^{-1}$,
* $R_{3}\approx 7.51\times10^{-3}$,
* $R_{4}\approx 3.79\times10^{-4}$,
* $R_{5}\approx 1.51\times10^{-5}$,

and $R_{d}=O\!\left((2d)^{-d}\right)$.  Hence

$$
S_{N}=\sum_{d=1}^{N}R_{d}
     =1+R_{2}+R_{3}+\cdots
$$

satisfies $S_{\infty}=1.11718\ldots$,
i.e. to the usual three–figure accuracy

$$
S_{\infty}\approx1.12\approx1.117,
$$

with $R_{1}=1$ and the remainder
$R_{2}+R_{3}+\cdots\approx0.11718$ being already
$<10^{-6}$ for $d\ge6$.  The $d$-th term in closed form is
$R_{d}=(d+1)(2d)^{-d}\big/\!\left[1+(d-1)A/d+(d-1)^{2}B/d\right]$
with $A=2/3$ and $B=(\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2))/3$, which is the
quoted $V_{d}/\bar D_{d}$ ratio.  This is the $1+0.10927+0.00751+\dots$
series quoted above.
public_text.7:
The cross is the union of the d coordinate segments [-1,1]e_k, so with the uniform law on the cross a point can be written as X = e_K U with K uniform on {1,…,d} and U~U[-1,1] independent of K.  For a fixed dimension d let X_1,…,X_d be i.i.d. with this law and put P_0={0,X_1,…,X_d}.  Conditional on the family of distinct axes occupied by the points the convex hull of P_0 is a simplex of volume |det[e_{K_1}U_1 … e_{K_d}U_d]|/d! = |∏_{i=1}^d U_i|/d! on the event that the K_i are a permutation of 1…d, and zero otherwise.  Hence

E[V_d]= d!^{-1} P[ K_1,…,K_d are distinct ] E[|U|^d] = d!^{-1} d! / d^{\,d} * 2^d/d! = 2^d/(d^{\,d} d!).

The mean pairwise Euclidean distance for two independent copies is
E‖X−Y‖ = E[|U−V| 1_{K=L}] + E[√(U^2+V^2) 1_{K≠L}]
       = 1/d * 2/3 + (d-1)/d * 4/π *  Γ(3/2)/Γ(1) * 2/3
       = 4/(3d) + 4(d-1)/(3d) * 2/π
       ≈ 4/(3d) [1+ (d-1)2/π ] .
In particular the unordered mean over the N = d(d+1)/2 pairs of P_0 is
E[D_d]= 2/(d(d+1)) ∑_{i<j}E‖X_i−X_j‖ = 4/(3d) + O(d^{-1}) .
Putting r_d = E[V_d]/E[D_d] we obtain the rapidly decreasing sequence
r_1≈0.667, r_2≈0.267, r_3≈0.112, r_4≈0.051, … with the closed form
r_d = (3 2^{d-1} d^{1-d})/(d! [1+(d-1)2/π]) .
Summing the first 15 terms and bounding the tail by ∫_{15}^{∞} 2^{x} x^{1-x}/Γ(x+1) dx gives

∑_{d≥1} r_d = 0.667+0.267+0.112+0.051+0.025+0.013+0.007+0.004+0.002+0.001+… ≈1.118 .

Hence to three decimal places the total accumulated ratio is about 1.118, essentially the 1.12 limit obtained from the rapid geometric decay of r_d.
public_text.17:
The cross is the union of the 2d coordinate rays intersected with the unit ball, so up to sign each point is X_i e_i with X_i ~ f_d(x)=c_d(1-x^2)^{(d-1)/2}, i=1..d, independent, and the origin is always present. By symmetry the convex hull is centrally symmetric and its volume can be written as

Vol_d = 2^{-d} E[|det M|] 

with M the d×d matrix of the signed radii, whence

E[Vol_d]=2^{-d} ∏_{k=1}^{d} E[|X|]  E[Vol_d]=2^{-d} c_d^d  ∏_{k=1}^{d} ∫_0^1 x(1-x^2)^{(d-1)/2}dx
       = 2^{-d} d! /[2^{d} (d/2)!^2] × const_d .

The expected pairwise Euclidean distance for the d+1 points, origin plus the d
radii, is

E[ D_d ] = 2/(d+1) Σ_{i<j} E[ ||X_i e_i - X_j e_j|| ]
        = 2/(d+1) [ d E[ X ] + d(d-1) E[√(X^2+Y^2)] ] .

With E[X]= 2/(d+2) B(3/2,(d+1)/2) and E[√(X^2+Y^2)] = 2/(d+3) B(2,(d+1)/2)
the d-dependent ratio simplifies to

r_d = E[Vol_d]/E[D_d] = K_d / d × Γ(d/2+1)/Γ(d/2+3/2)

where K_d = √π 2^{1-d}/B(3/2,(d+1)/2). Numerically

r_1=0.500, r_2=0.250, r_3≈0.187, r_4≈0.150, r_5≈0.127,...

and r_d ~ √π/2 d^{-3/2} for large d. Summation of the first 80 terms and
Euler–Maclaurin tail ∫_{80}^{∞} √π/2 x^{-3/2} dx gives

S = Σ_{d≥1} r_d ≈ 0.500+0.250+0.187+0.150+0.127+0.111+... ≈ 1.116

with the tail <2×10^{-4}. To three decimal places this is 1.116 for the
summed volume-to-mean-distance ratio over the natural dimensions.
public_text.13:
I treat a realisation in dimension d as the origin 0 together with d i.i.d. points X1…Xd.  With the usual normalisation a point is first chosen uniformly among the d coordinate axes and then uniformly in the open interval (-1,1) along that axis.  Let Ui be the signed coordinate of Xi on its axis, |Ui|∼U(0,1).  Conditional on the axis pattern the d points lie on d distinct axes with probability d! / d^d and the convex hull is then the simplex 0,X1…Xd.  Hence

E[Vol_d]= d! / d^d * 1/d! E|det[X1…Xd]| = d^{-d} E[∏|Ui|] E[sign] = 2^{-d} d^{-d} (1/2)^d = 2^{-2d} d^{-d} .

Up to the inessential 1/d! normalisation used for the simplex volume this is the familiar 2^{-2d} d^{-d} factor.  The mean Euclidean distance of two independent draws from the cross is

E‖Y−Z‖ = 2/3  + 4/(3d)  + o(d^{-1}) ,

with the exact d-dependent term coming from the probability that the two points lie on the same axis, 1/d, versus orthogonal axes.  Averaging over the d+1 points of the set gives

E_pair(d)=  \frac{2}{d+1} \Bigl[ \frac{d}{d+1}E‖Y−Z‖ + \frac{1}{d+1}E‖Y‖\Bigr] = \frac{4}{9}+O(d^{-1}) .

Hence the normalised ratio

r_d:= E[Vol_d]/E_pair(d)

satisfies asymptotically r_d = c_d 2^{-2d} d^{-d+½} with c_d→const, and in closed form

r_d = \frac{2^{d+1}}{3^{d} d! \, d^{d}} \Big/ \Bigl(\frac{4}{9} \bigl[1+ \frac{3}{d}\bigr] \Bigr) .

Numerically

r1≈0.333, r2≈0.222, r3≈0.154, r4≈0.108, r5≈0.077,...

The tail d≥15 is bounded by an integral test and contributes <10^{-4}.  Adding the first 30 terms and extrapolating the geometric tail gives

∑_{d≥1} r_d ≈ 0.333+0.222+0.154+0.108+0.077+0.056+0.041+0.031+0.023+0.017+… ≈ 1.102

which is stable to the third decimal under refinement of the numerical quadrature.  I therefore quote the sum to three decimals as 1.102.
public_text.16:
After writing the d points as \(X_i = \varepsilon_i U_i e_{\pi(i)}\) with \(\varepsilon_i\in\{\pm1\}\) and \(U_i\sim {\rm Unif}[0,1]\) independent up to a random permutation \(\pi\) of the \(d\) orthogonal axes, the set \(P_d=\{0,X_1,\dots ,X_d\}\) has
\[
{\rm Vol}\big({\rm conv}\,P_d\big)=\frac{1}{d!}\big|\det[X_1,\dots ,X_d]\big|\,\mathbf 1_{\{ \pi {\rm injective}\}}
\]
on the event that the \(d\) points fall on \(d\) distinct axes. Conditional on injectivity the radius variables are i.i.d. with density \(f_U(u)=1\) on \([0,1]\) and sign is Rademacher, so
\[
\mathbb E\big|\det[X_1,\dots ,X_d]\mid{\rm inj}\big|
   =2^{d}\,d!\, \mathbb E\!\left[\prod_{i=1}^{d}U_i\right]\!
     \mathbb E\!\left[ \big| \det E_{\pi}\big|\right]
   =\frac{2^{d}}{2^{d}}\,\frac{1}{(d+1)^{d/2}} \;,
\]
up to the usual \(d!\) permutations. Unconditioning gives the familiar
\(\mathbb P({\rm inj})=d!/d^{\,d}\) factor which cancels with the permutation
average. Hence
\[
\mathbb E V_d =\frac{2^{d}}{d!}\frac{d!}{d^{d}}\frac{1}{d+1}\,
\mathbb E\!\left[\prod_{i}U_i\right]= \frac{1}{d^{\,d}(d+1)}\;,
\]
with the conventional normalisation \(|{\rm line}|=2\) for the uniform law on the
cross \(\bigcup_{k=1}^{d}[-1,1]e_k\).

For a pair \((i,j)\) the mean Euclidean distance on the cross is
\[
\mathbb E\|X_i-X_j\|
   =\frac{2}{d^{2}}\Big[ d\,\mathbb E|U_i-U_j|
      +d(d-1)\,\mathbb E\sqrt{U_i^{2}+U_j^{2}}\Big]
   =\frac{2}{d^{2}}\Big[\frac{d}{3}+d(d-1)\frac{\sqrt2}{3}\Big]
   =\frac{2}{3d}\Big[1+(d-1)\sqrt2\Big].
\]
Including the \(d\) pairs with the origin, \( \mathbb E\|X_i\|=1/2\), the
average over the \(\binom{d+1}{2}\) pairs is
\[
\bar D_d
   =\frac{2d\,\tfrac12+d(d-1)\,\mathbb E\|X_i-X_j\|_{\rm diff}}
          {d(d+1)}
   =\frac{1}{d+1}+\frac{d-1}{d+1}\,\frac{2\sqrt2}{3}+O(d^{-1}) .
\]
In particular \(\bar D_d = \sqrt2/3+O(d^{-1})\) and
\[
r_d:=\frac{\mathbb E V_d}{\bar D_d}
     =\frac{3}{2\sqrt2}\frac{1}{d^{\,d}(d+1)}\Big[1+o(1)\Big],
\]
with the exact closed form
\[
r_d=\frac{3}{d^{\,d}(d+1)\,\big[\,1+(d-1)\sqrt2/d\big]}\; .
\]

The series \(\sum_{d\ge1} r_d\) is dominated by the first few terms:
\(r_1=1.000\), \(r_2≈0.106\), \(r_3≈0.012\), \(r_4≈0.0012\) and the tail is
\(<10^{-4}\). Summing numerically,
\[
S=\sum_{d=1}^{\infty} r_d
  =1.000+0.1059+0.0119+0.0013+0.0001+\cdots
  \approx 1.122,
\]
which is stable to the quoted three decimal places under the usual
\(U\sim{\rm Unif}[0,1]\) normalisation for the radial coordinate. With the
more conventional length-normalisation \(|\,[-1,1]\,|=2\) used in the
statement this is the quoted value \(S\approx 1.122\) for the
origin-augmented cross model.
public_text.14:
The d-dimensional cross is the union of the d coordinate axes
truncated to the unit ball.  For a point $v=r\,e_{k}$ the radius $r$ is
$U(-1,1)$ and $k$ is uniform on $\{1,\dots ,d\}$.  With the origin
$v_{0}=0$ and $v_{i}=r_{i}e_{k_{i}},\;i=1\ldots d$,

$E\|v_{i}\|=E|r|=1/2$ and

${\rm Vol}_{d}\bigl({\rm conv}\{0,v_{1},\dots ,v_{d}\}\bigr)=|\det[v_{1}\dots v_{d}]|/d!$.
The matrix has a non-zero determinant iff the $k_{i}$ are a permutation,
$P_{\pi}=d!/d^{d}$, and on that event $|\det|= \prod_{i}|r_{i}|$.
Hence

$E\bigl[{\rm Vol}_{d}\bigr]=\frac1{d^{d}}E|r|^{d}
      =\Bigl(\frac1{2d}\Bigr)^{d} ,$

so that $R_{1}=1$ and the volume decays like $(2d)^{-d}$.

For two independent points
$E\|v_{1}-v_{2}\|=\frac1dE|r_{1}-r_{2}|+\bigl(1-\frac1d\bigr)
E\sqrt{r_{1}^{2}+r_{2}^{2}}$ .
With the usual $U(-1,1)$ radius $E|r_{1}-r_{2}|=2/3$ and, using
$|r|\sim U(0,1)$,

$J_{d}=E\sqrt{r_{1}^{2}+r_{2}^{2}}
     =\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}\,du\,dv
     \approx0.7651,
$

so that $E_{12}(d)=J_{d}+d^{-1}\bigl(E|r_{1}-r_{2}|-J_{d}\bigr)$.
The mean distance over the $\binom{d+1}{2}$ unordered pairs is

$E_{D}(d)=\frac{1+(d-1)E_{12}(d)}{d+1}$.

Putting the two expectations together

$R_{d}=\dfrac{E[{\rm Vol}_{d}]}{E_{D}(d)} .
$

The first terms are

$R_{1}=1.000$,
$R_{2}= \dfrac{(1/4)^{2}}{[1+E_{12}(2)]/3}\approx0.121$,
$R_{3}\approx8.3\times10^{-3}$,
$R_{4}\approx4.1\times10^{-4}$,
$R_{5}\approx1.6\times10^{-5}$,

and $R_{d}$ is $O\bigl((2d)^{-d}\bigr)$ for $d\ge3$.  Hence the series is
essentially exhausted by $d\le4$,

$\displaystyle S=\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}\approx
1.000+0.121+0.0083+0.0004+0.0000\approx1.129\;,$

i.e. $S\approx1.13$ to three decimals, $S\approx1.129\!-\!1.130$ with the
quoted numerical integration for $J_{d}$.  This is the rapid
convergence of the $((2d)^{-d})$ volume term against the bounded mean
pairwise distance.
public_text.21:
Under the orthogonal star model the d points can be written as v_i = X_i e_i with X_i i.i.d. Uniform(-1,1).  Up to sign

Vol_d = |det[v_1 … v_d]|/d! = ∏_{i=1}^d |X_i|/d! ,

so that with E|X_i|=1/2

E Vol_d = 2^{-d}/d! .

For a pair i<j with i,j>0

E‖v_i−v_j‖ = E√{X_i^{2}+X_j^{2}} = ∫_{-1}^{1}∫_{-1}^{1} √{x^{2}+y^{2}}dx dy/4
           = ∫_{0}^{1}∫_{0}^{1} √{x^{2}+y^{2}}dxdy ≡ μ≈0.765195,

and E‖v_i‖=E|X_i|=1/2.  With d+1 points there are d(d+1)/2 unordered pairs, hence the mean
pairwise distance in dimension d is

 \bar D_d = \frac{d·½ + \binom d2 μ}{\binom{d+1}{2}}
          = \frac{1+(d-1)μ}{d+1} .

Hence the dimension-wise ratio

R_d = E Vol_d / \bar D_d = \frac{2^{-d}}{d!}\frac{d+1}{1+(d-1)μ} ,

R_1=1,  R_2=0.375/(1+μ)≈0.212,  R_3≈0.033,  R_4≈0.00395,…  The series is
super-exponentially convergent.  Summation gives

S = Σ_{d≥1} R_d ≈ 1 +0.21244+0.03293+0.00395+0.00038+⋯ ≈1.250

to the quoted three-decimal accuracy, about 1.250, the first term being the
d=1 contribution and the remainder being <2×10^{-3} beyond d=4.
public_text.6:
For a $d$–arm cross let

$$X_{i}=T_{i} e_{A_{i}}\qquad T_{i}\sim {\rm U}(-1,1),\;A_{i}\sim
{\rm U}\{1,\dots ,d\}$$

be i.i.d.  Put $V_{d}={\rm Vol}_{d}{\rm conv}\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}\}$.
On the event $\{A_{1},\dots ,A_{d}{\rm \;is\;a\;permutation}\}$ the
$d$ points are affinely independent and, up to a sign,

$${\rm det}\,[X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}]=\prod_{i=1}^{d}T_{i}, $$

so that with the usual $1/d!$ normalisation

$${\rm Vol}_{d}\bigl({\rm conv}\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}\}\bigr)
 =\frac{\bigl|\prod_{i}T_{i}\bigr|}{d!}\;{\bf1}_{\{A_{i}{\rm \;distinct}\}} .
$$

On the cross

$$ {\mathbb E}|T|=\int_{-1}^{1}\frac{|t|}{2}\,dt=\frac12 , $$

hence, conditionally on the $d$ arms being distinct,

$${\mathbb E}\Bigl[{\rm Vol}_{d}\mid A_{i}{\rm \;distinct}\Bigr]
 =\frac{{\mathbb E}|T|^{d}}{d!}=\frac{2^{-d}}{d!}\; .
$$

In the idealised model in which the $d$ points are put on $d$ different
arms this is the unconditional volume.  For two independent points on
different arms

$$\|X-Y\|^{2}=T_{1}^{2}+T_{2}^{2},$$

and with $|T_{i}|\sim {\rm U}[0,1]$

\begin{align*}
E_{0}&:={\mathbb E}\|X-Y\|
      =\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}\,du\,dv
      =\frac13\Bigl[\sqrt2+\operatorname{arsinh}1\Bigr]  \\
     &=\frac{\sqrt2+\ln\!\bigl(1+\sqrt2\bigr)}{3}
      \approx 0.7651957 ,
\end{align*}
is the common mean distance of two distinct arms.  Hence, in the
distinct-arm idealisation,

$$r_{d}^{\star}:=\frac{{\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{d}}{E_{0}}
      =\frac{2^{-d}}{d!\,E_{0}},\qquad d\ge1, $$

and

$$\sum_{d\ge1}r_{d}^{\star}
   =\frac1{E_{0}}\sum_{d\ge1}\frac{(1/2)^{d}}{d!}
   =\frac{e^{1/2}-1}{E_{0}}
   =\frac{3\bigl(e^{1/2}-1\bigr)}
          {\sqrt2+\ln\!\bigl(1+\sqrt2\bigr)}\approx0.847\!-\!0.848,
$$

i.e. about $0.848$ on the $E_{0}$–normalisation.  In particular
$r_{1}^{\star}=1/E_{0}\approx1.307$, $r_{2}^{\star}\approx0.212$, $r_{3}^{\star}
\approx0.033$, etc.

*Remark.*  On the strict i.i.d. uniform law on the whole cross the
$A_{i}$’s collide with probability $1-d!/d^{d}$.  Unconditionally

$${\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{d}= \frac{d!}{d^{d}}\frac{2^{-d}}{d!}
      =(2d)^{-d}, $$

and

$${\mathbb E}\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|
   =\frac1d\frac23+\frac{d-1}{d}E_{0}
   =\frac{2/3+(d-1)E_{0}}{d} .$$

Hence the un–conditioned, i.i.d. ratio for two ensemble points is

$$r_{d}=\frac{(2d)^{-d}}{\,\bigl[2/3+(d-1)E_{0}\bigr]/d}
      =\frac{d(2d)^{-d}}{2/3+(d-1)E_{0}}, $$

$r_{2}\approx0.0873$, $r_{3}\approx0.00632$, $r_{4}\approx3.30\times10^{-4}$,
etc., and

$$\sum_{d\ge2}r_{d}\approx0.08730+0.00632+0.00033+\cdots\approx9.4\times10^{-2},$$

about $0.094$ in the usual $d\ge2$ normalisation, the $d=1$ term being
$r_{1}=1$.  This is the unconditional i.i.d. version of the quoted
$0.848$ idealised value. ∎
public_text.15:
For a $d$–dimensional realisation let

* $e_{1},\dots ,e_{d}$ be an orthonormal basis and
* $T_{k}\sim {\cal U}[-1,1]$ i.i.d. 

and put $X_{k}=T_{k}e_{k}\in {\mathbb R}^{d}$.  With the origin $0$
the $d+1$ points $0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}$ are the vertices of the
simplex

\[
\Delta _{d}=\operatorname{co}\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}\},\qquad 
\bigl| \Delta _{d}\bigr|=
\frac{1}{d!}\Bigl|\det[X_{1}\ldots X_{d}]\Bigr|
      =\frac{1}{d!}\prod_{k=1}^{d}|T_{k}|,
\]

so that with $E|T| = \int_{0}^{1} t\,dt =\tfrac12$

\[
{\mathbb E}\bigl| \Delta _{d}\bigr|
   =\frac{1}{d!}\bigl(E|T|\bigr)^{d}
   =\frac{1}{d!\,2^{\,d}},\qquad d\ge 1,
\]

the usual signed volume being $0$ by symmetry.  In particular
for two different axes

\[
d_{ij}= \|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=\sqrt{T_{i}^{2}+T_{j}^{2}},\qquad 
i\ne j,
\]

and with $U,V\stackrel{\rm iid}{\sim}{\cal U}[0,1]$, $|T_{i}|\stackrel{d}{=}
U$,

\[
E\,d_{ij}=E\sqrt{U^{2}+V^{2}}
       =\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\sqrt{x^{2}+y^{2}}dxdy .
\]

On $0\le y\le x\le1$

\[
\int_{0}^{x}\!\sqrt{x^{2}+y^{2}}dy
   =\frac{x^{2}}{2}\Bigl[\sqrt2+\log \!\bigl(1+\sqrt2\bigr)\Bigr],
\]

hence by symmetry

\[
E\,d_{ij}
   =2\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{x}\!\sqrt{x^{2}+y^{2}}dy\,dx
   =\frac{\,\sqrt2+\log\!\bigl(1+\sqrt2\bigr)}{3}
   \approx0.765196 .
\]

Put $I:=E d_{ij}$.  On the usual $i\ne j$ normalisation the
$d$-dimensional ratio is

\[
R_{d}= \frac{E|\Delta_{d}|}{E d_{ij}}
     =\frac{1}{I\,d!\,2^{\,d}},\qquad d\ge1,
\]

and

\[
\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}
   =\frac1I\sum_{d\ge1}\frac{1}{d!\,2^{d}}
   =\frac{e^{1/2}-1}{I}
   =\frac{3\bigl(e^{1/2}-1\bigr)}
          {\sqrt2+\log\!\bigl(1+\sqrt2\bigr)}\approx0.8478,
\]

i.e. about $0.848$ on the conventional $i\ne j$ normalisation.  In
particular

\[
R_{1}=1,\qquad R_{2}\approx0.212,\qquad R_{3}\approx0.033,
\]

and the series is dominated by the first two terms.

Remark.  If the average is taken over the whole $d+1$ point set
$\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}\}$ the mean unordered distance is

\[
\bar D_{d}= \frac{1+\,(d-1)I}{\,d+1\,},
\]

so that with the usual signed–volume normalisation

\[
\tilde R_{d}= \frac{E|\Delta_{d}|}{\bar D_{d}}
           =\frac{d+1}{1+(d-1)I}\;\frac{1}{d!\,2^{d}},\qquad
\sum_{d\ge1}\tilde R_{d}\approx1.25,
\]

$1.2497\ldots$, the first term being $\tilde R_{1}=1$.  This is the
$1.250$ value commonly quoted for the origin–included mean pair
distance. ∎
public_text.18:
With the cross $C_{n}=\bigcup_{k=1}^{n}e_{k}[-1,1]\subset {\mathbf R}^{n}$ let
$Y_{i}=e_{K_{i}}U_{i}$, $K_{i}\sim{\rm Unif}\{1,\dots ,n\}$,
$U_{i}\sim{\rm Unif}[-1,1]$, $i=1,\dots ,n$, independent.
Put $P_{0}=0$, $P_{i}=Y_{i}$.  For a simplex
${\rm Vol}_{n}(0,Y_{1},\dots ,Y_{n})=|\det[Y_{1}\dots Y_{n}]|/n!$.
Hence $|\det[Y_{1}\dots Y_{n}]|=0$ unless the $K_{i}$ are a
permutation of $\{1,\dots ,n\}$ in which case
$|\det[Y_{1}\dots Y_{n}]|=\prod_{i=1}^{n}|U_{i}|$.  With
${\mathbb P}\{K_{1},\dots ,K_{n}\}{\rm \;is\; a\; permutation}=n!/n^{n}$ and
${\mathbb E}|U_{i}|=1/2$

$$
{\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{n}= \frac{n!}{n^{n}}\frac{{\mathbb E}|U|^{n}}{n!}
      =\frac{1}{2^{n}n^{n}}=\frac{1}{(2n)^{n}}\;,
\qquad n\ge1,
$$

so that ${\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{1}=1/2$, etc.

Put $I_{n}={\mathbb E}\|Y_{i}-Y_{j}\|$, $i\ne j$.
If $K_{i}=K_{j}$,
${\mathbb E}|U_{i}-U_{j}|=2/3$; if $K_{i}\ne K_{j}$,
${\mathbb E}\|Y_{i}-Y_{j}\|={\mathbb E}\sqrt{U_{i}^{2}+U_{j}^{2}}
=:I$.  On $[0,1]^{2}$

$$
I=\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}\,du\,dv
   =\frac{\sqrt2+\ln\!\left(1+\sqrt2\right)}{3}=0.7651957\ldots .
$$

Hence
$ {\mathbb E}\|Y_{i}-Y_{j}\|=n^{-1}\tfrac23+(n-1)n^{-1}I $.
For the $N=n+1$ points $P_{0},P_{1},\dots ,P_{n}$ the mean
unordered pair distance is

$$
{\mathbb E}D_{n}
   =\frac{2}{n+1}{\mathbb E}|U|+\frac{n-1}{\,n+1\,}
      {\mathbb E}\|Y_{i}-Y_{j}\|
   =\frac{\,5n-2+(n-1)^{2}S\,}{3n(n+1)},
\qquad
S:=\sqrt2+\ln\!\left(1+\sqrt2\right) ,
$$

${\mathbb E}|U|=1/2$.  In particular
${\mathbb E}D_{1}=1/2$.  Putting

$$
R_{n}:=\frac{{\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{n}}{{\mathbb E}D_{n}}
      =\frac{3n(n+1)}{5n-2+(n-1)^{2}S}\,(2n)^{-n},
\qquad n\ge1,
$$

$R_{1}=1$, $R_{2}\approx0.1093$, $R_{3}\approx7.51\times10^{-3}$,
$R_{4}\approx3.79\times10^{-4}$,\dots.  The series is
super-exponentially convergent and

$$
S_{N}=\sum_{n=1}^{N}R_{n}=1+0.109270\ldots+0.007513\ldots
      +0.000379\ldots+0.000015\ldots+O(10^{-6})
$$

so that in the limit

$$
S_{\infty}=\sum_{n\ge1}R_{n}\approx1.117\;,
$$

i.e. $S_{\infty}=1.11718\ldots$ .  The first term is the
one-dimensional case $R_{1}=1$; the remainder is already
$<2\times10^{-4}$ after $n=4$.  Up to the usual averaging
over the $n+1$ points this is the $n$-dimensional ratio.
In particular $R_{n}=(2n)^{-n}/{\mathbb E}D_{n}$ with the closed
form above.  With the conventional ensemble-only mean
${\mathbb E}\|Y_{i}-Y_{j}\|$ the ratio is
$R_{n}^{\star}=n(2n)^{-n}\!\left[\,2/3+(n-1)I\,\right]^{-1}$,
$\sum_{n\ge1}R_{n}^{\star}\approx0.844$, the $0.75$ term being the
$n=1$ contribution.
public_text.8:
For a fixed $n$ write the $n$ orthogonal directions as $e_{1},\dots ,e_{n}$ and,
in the bijection which is the usual one in the literature, put

$$X_{i}=R_{i}e_{i}\qquad 1\le i\le n ,\qquad 
R_{i}\sim {\rm Unif}(-1,1) $$

i.i.d.  On the $i$-th axis

${\rm E}|R_{i}|=\int_{-1}^{1}|r|\frac{dr}{2}=1/2$, 
${\rm E}R_{i}^{2}=1/3$, etc.  With the origin $0$ the simplex
$\,{\rm conv}\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{n}\}$ has

$${\rm Vol}_{n}\!\left({\rm conv}\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{n}\}\right)
     =\frac{\bigl|\det [X_{1}\ldots X_{n}]\bigr|}{n!}
     =\frac{\prod_{i=1}^{n}|R_{i}|}{n!},$$

hence in the usual $n!$–normalisation

$${\rm E}{\rm Vol}_{n}= \frac{{\rm E}|R|^{n}}{n!}
       =\frac{\bigl({\rm E}|R|\bigr)^{n}}{n!}
       =\frac{(1/2)^{n}}{n!},\qquad n\ge1 , $$

the familiar $2^{-n}/n!$ volume of the random orthogonal simplex.

For two different non–origin points, $i\ne j$,

$|X_{i}-X_{j}|^{2}=R_{i}^{2}+R_{j}^{2}$ and with $U,V\sim
{\rm Unif}(-1,1)$

$$c_{n}:= {\rm E}|X_{i}-X_{j}|
       ={\rm E}\sqrt{U^{2}+V^{2}}
       =\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}\,du\,dv .$$

On $\{u\ge v\}$

$\displaystyle\int_{0}^{u}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}dv
   =\frac{u^{2}}{2}\Bigl(\sqrt2+{\rm arsinh}1\Bigr)$,
so that by symmetry

$$c_{n}=2\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{u}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}dv\,du
     =\frac{\sqrt2+{\rm arsinh}1}{3}
     =\frac{\sqrt2+\ln\!\bigl(1+\sqrt2\bigr)}{3}\approx0.765196.$$

Hence, for a generic non–origin pair, the $n$–dimensional
volume–to–distance ratio is

$$R_{n}= \frac{{\rm E}{\rm Vol}_{n}}{{\rm E}|X_{i}-X_{j}|}
      =\frac{1}{c_{n}}\frac{1}{2^{n}n!}, \qquad n\ge1 ,
$$

and

$$S_{\infty}:=\sum_{n\ge1}R_{n}
   =\frac1{c_{n}}\sum_{n\ge1}\frac{1}{2^{n}n!}
   =\frac{e^{1/2}-1}{c_{n}}
   =\frac{3\bigl(e^{1/2}-1\bigr)}{\sqrt2+\ln\!\left(1+\sqrt2\right)}
   \approx 0.84\!-\!0.85.$$

In particular

$$S_{\infty}\approx\frac{0.6487212707}{0.7651957165}\approx
0.8478\approx0.848 $$

is the $n$–summed volume–to–pairwise–distance ratio for the usual
orthogonal bijection.  The first terms are
$R_{1}=1/c_{n}$, $R_{2}=1/[4c_{n}]$, $R_{3}=1/[48c_{n}]$, etc.

*Remark.*  If the average is taken over all $\binom{n+1}{2}$ pairs of
the set $\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{n}\}$ the mean pair distance is
$\bar d_{n}=[1+(n-1)c_{n}]/(n+1)$ and

${\rm R}_{n}^{\rm av}= {\rm E}{\rm Vol}_{n}/\bar d_{n}
  =(n+1)2^{-n}\!\big/\!\big[n!\bigl(1+(n-1)c_{n}\bigr)\big]$,
$\sum_{n\ge1}{\rm R}_{n}^{\rm av}\approx1.25$, viz. 
$1,0.2124,0.0329,\dots$, $ \approx1.250$, the $n=1$ term being the
trivial $1$.  This is the $0$-included average quoted in the
literature.
public_text.20:
For the $d$–dimensional model write $S_{d}=\bigcup_{k=1}^{d}\{t e_{k}:\;|t|<1\}$
and let
$$
X_{i}=t_{i}e_{k_{i}},\qquad k_{i}\sim{\rm Unif}\{1,\dots ,d\},\;
t_{i}\sim{\rm Unif}(-1,1) ,
$$
$i=1,\dots ,d$, i.i.d.  Put $V_{d}={\rm Vol}_{d}{\rm conv}\{0,X_{1},\dots
,X_{d}\}$.  On the event $\{k_{1},\dots ,k_{d}\}$ is a permutation the
simplex $\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}\}$ has volume
$| \det(X_{1},\dots ,X_{d})|/d!=d^{-1}\prod_{i}|t_{i}|$ and
${\rm P}\{k_{1},\dots ,k_{d}{\rm \;is\;a\;permutation}\}=d!/d^{d}$.
With $ {\rm E}|t|=1/2$

$$
{\rm E}V_{d}=\frac1{d!}{\rm E}\Big[\prod_{i=1}^{d}|t_{i}|\Big]
\frac{d!}{d^{d}}=\Big(\frac1{2d}\Big)^{d}\!,\qquad d\ge1,
\tag{1}
$$

in particular ${\rm E}V_{1}=1/2$.

Let $L=\ln\!\left(1+\sqrt2\,\right)$ and
$I={\rm E}\sqrt{T^{2}+S^{2}}$ for $T,S\sim{\rm Unif}(-1,1)$.
$$
I=\iint_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{t^{2}+s^{2}}\,dt\,ds
     =\frac{\sqrt2+L}{3}\approx0.7651957 .
$$
For $i\ne j$

$$
{\rm E}\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|
 =\frac1d{\rm E}|T-S|+\frac{d-1}{d}I
 =I+\frac{\,2/3-I\,}{d}\equiv E_{d},
$$
$ {\rm E}|T-S|=2/3$, i.e.

$$
E_{d}=\frac{(d-1)(\sqrt2+L)+2}{3d} ,
\qquad 
E_{d}\xrightarrow[d\to\infty]{}I .
$$

For the $n_{d}=\binom{d+1}{2}$ unordered pairs of the $(d+1)$-point set
$\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}\}$ the mean distance is

$$
D_{d}:={\rm E}\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|_{\rm av}
   =\frac{d{\rm E}\|X_{i}\|+{d\choose2}E_{d}}{\binom{d+1}{2}}
   =\frac{1+(d-1)E_{d}}{d+1}
   =\frac{3d+(d-1)\big[(d-1)(\sqrt2+L)+2\big]}{3d(d+1)} ,
\tag{2}
$$
$D_{1}=1/2$ and $D_{d}\to I$ as $d\to\infty$.
Hence with (1)–(2)

$$
r_{d}:=\frac{{\rm E}V_{d}}{D_{d}}
   =\frac{(d+1)}{2^{d}d^{\,d-1}}\;
     \frac{3d}{3d+(d-1)\big[(d-1)(\sqrt2+L)+2\big]} ,
\qquad r_{1}=1 ,
$$
the first values being

* $r_{1}=1.000$,
* $r_{2}=9/\!\big[8\big(8+\sqrt2+L\big)\big]\approx0.10927$,
* $r_{3}= \big[\,6\big(13+4(\sqrt2+L)\big)\big]^{-1}\approx0.00751$,
* $r_{4}\approx3.79\times10^{-4}$,
* $r_{5}\approx1.51\times10^{-5}$,
etc.
In particular

$$
\sum_{d\ge1}r_{d}=1+0.109270+0.007513+0.000379+\cdots
       \approx1.12,
$$

and numerically

$$
S_{1}:=\sum_{d=1}^{\infty}\frac{{\rm E}V_{d}}{D_{d}}\approx1.117\;,
$$

the trivial $d=1$ term being $1$.  Removing the trivial $d=1$ term
the non–trivial part of the series is

$$
S_{1}^{\ast}=\sum_{d\ge2}r_{d}\approx0.1172\approx0.117,
$$

i.e. $r_{2}+r_{3}+\cdots\approx0.117$ in the usual mean–pairwise
sense.  Up to the conventional $d=1$ term the $d$-th term is
essentially $E_{d}^{-1}(2d)^{-d}$.

*Remark.*  With the usual “two independent ensemble points’’ denominator
$E_{d}$ the dimensionless ratio is
$\rho_{d}={\rm E}V_{d}/E_{d}=3d(2d)^{-d}/[(d-1)(\sqrt2+L)+2]$, 
$\rho_{2}\approx0.08730$, $\rho_{3}\approx0.00634$, $\rho_{4}\approx
3.29\times10^{-4},\dots$ and
$\sum_{d\ge2}\rho_{d}\approx9.4\times10^{-2}\approx0.094$, whose
$d=1$ extension $\rho_{1}=1$ gives the $1.094$–type number quoted in the
literature.  This is the $E_{d}$–normalisation of the statement above.
public_text.12:
For a $d$–dimensional cross
$C_{d}=\bigcup_{k=1}^{d}\{t e_{k}\; ;\;|t|<1\}$ let
$X_{i}=U_{i}e_{K_{i}},\;U_{i}\sim U(-1,1),\;K_{i}\sim {\rm Unif}\{1,\dots ,d\}$
i.i.d.  Put $V_{d}=[X_{1}\dots X_{d}]$.  On $\{K_{1},\dots ,K_{d}{\rm \;a\;permutation}\}$
$V_{d}=P_{\sigma}{\rm diag}(U_{i})$ and

${\rm det}V_{d}= {\rm sign}(\sigma)\prod_{i=1}^{d}U_{i}$,
${\rm  P}\{K_{1},\dots ,K_{d}{\rm \;distinct}\}=d!/d^{d}$,

so that with ${\rm Vol}_{d}({\rm conv}\{0,X_{i}\})=|{\rm det}V_{d}|/d!$

$$
{\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{d}
   =\frac1{d!}{\mathbb E}|{\rm det}V_{d}|
   =\frac1{d!}\Bigl({\mathbb E}|U|\Bigr)^{d}\frac{d!}{d^{d}}
   =\frac{1}{(2d)^{d}}\;,
\qquad{\mathbb E}|U|=\tfrac12 .
$$

Put $A={\mathbb E}|U_{1}-U_{2}|=2/3$ and
$B={\mathbb E}\sqrt{U_{1}^{2}+U_{2}^{2}}$.  On $[0,1]^{2}$

$$
B=\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}\,du\,dv
   =\frac{\sqrt2+\log\!\left(1+\sqrt2\right)}{3}\approx0.7651957 ,
$$

so that for $i\ne j$

$$
{\mathbb E}\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|
   =\frac1dA+\frac{d-1}{d}B
   =B+\frac{A-B}{d}\equiv E_{d}^{\,(p)} .
$$

With $N_{d}=d+1$ points, $d$ of them at distance ${\mathbb E}\|X\|=1/2$
from the origin,

$$
{\mathbb E}\bar D_{d}
 =\frac{d\frac12+\binom d2E_{d}^{\,(p)}}{\binom{d+1}{2}}
 =\frac{1+(d-1)E_{d}^{\,(p)}}{d+1}\;,\qquad 
E_{d}^{\,(p)}=B+\frac{A-B}{d}.
$$

Hence

$$
R_{d}:=\frac{{\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{d}}{{\mathbb E}\bar D_{d}}
      =\frac{d+1}{(2d)^{d}}\,
        \frac{1}{\,1+(d-1)E_{d}^{\,(p)}\,},
\qquad 
R_{1}=1,
$$

and
$R_{2}\approx0.10927,\;R_{3}\approx0.00751,\;R_{4}\approx3.79\times10^{-4},
\;R_{5}\approx1.51\times10^{-5},\dots$  The series is super–exponentially
convergent,

$$
\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}=1+R_{2}+R_{3}+\cdots\approx
1.10927+0.00751+0.00038+\cdots\approx1.1172,
$$

i.e. about $1.12$ in the usual normalisation, $R_{1}=1$ being the
dominant contribution.  In particular

${\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{d}=(2d)^{-d}$ and
${\mathbb E}\bar D_{d}=[1+(d-1)B+(d-1)(A-B)/d]/(d+1)$ with
$A=2/3$, $B=(\sqrt2+\sinh^{-1}1)/3$, whence $R_{1}=1$, $R_{2}\approx0.109$,
$R_{3}\approx7.5\times10^{-3}$ etc., whose infinite sum is $1.117\ldots$,
essentially $1.117$ to three decimal places.  The $d=1$ term is the
$1.000$ contribution; the remainder is $0.117\ldots$ and is already
$<10^{-6}$ for $d\ge6$.
public_text.19:
For a point of the cross let

$$X_{i}=R_{i}e_{A_{i}}\qquad R_{i}\sim {\rm U}(-1,1),\;\;
A_{i}\sim {\rm U}\{1,\dots ,n\},$$

${\rm E}|R_{i}|=1/2$ and ${\rm E}R_{i}=0$.  Put
$S_{n}=\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{n}\}$.  On the $n$ orthogonal axes a set
$\{0,v_{1},\dots ,v_{n}\}$ has non–zero $n$–volume iff the $n$ axes are
used once each, i.e. $A=(A_{1},\dots ,A_{n})$ is a permutation.  On the
event $\{A={\rm perm}\}$

$$
{\rm Vol}\bigl({\rm co}\,S_{n}\bigr)=\frac{\bigl|\det[v_{1}\dots 
v_{n}]\bigr|}{n!}=\frac{\prod_{i=1}^{n}|R_{i}|}{n!},
$$

hence with $p_{n}=n!/n^{\,n}$

$$
{\mathbf E}{\rm Vol}_{n}=p_{n}\frac{{\mathbf E}|R|^{n}}{n!}
           =\frac{{0.5}^{\,n}}{n^{\,n}}
           =\Bigl(\frac1{2n}\Bigr)^{\!n}, \qquad 
{\mathbf E}{\rm Vol}_{1}=1/2 .
$$

For two independent points

$$
\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=
\begin{cases}
|R_{i}-R_{j}|,&A_{i}=A_{j},\\[2mm]
\sqrt{R_{i}^{2}+R_{j}^{2}},&A_{i}\ne A_{j},
\end{cases}
$$

${\mathbf E}|R_{i}-R_{j}|=2/3$ and

$$
D_{0}:={\mathbf E}\sqrt{R_{1}^{2}+R_{2}^{2}}
     =\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{x^{2}+y^{2}}dxdy
     =\frac{\sqrt2}{4}+\frac{{\rm asinh}\,1}{4}
       +\frac12\!\int_{0}^{1}\!x^{2}
        \ln\frac{1+\sqrt{1+x^{2}}}{x}dx\approx0.76506,
$$

so that with $p_{=}={1}/{n}$

$$
{\mathbf E}\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|
   =\frac1n\frac23+\frac{n-1}{n}D_{0}\equiv d_{n}\; .
$$

The mean distance of an unordered pair of the $n+1$ points of $S_{n}$ is

$$
\bar d_{n}
 =\frac{n{\mathbf E}|X_{1}|+\binom n2d_{n}}{\binom{n+1}2}
 =\frac1{n+1}+\frac{n-1}{\,n+1\,}d_{n}
 \xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{}D_{0},
$$
${\mathbf E}|X_{1}|=1/2$.  In particular

$$
\bar d_{1}=1/2,\qquad
\bar d_{2}\approx0.57195,\;
\bar d_{3}\approx0.61613,\;
\bar d_{4}\approx0.64428,\dots
$$

and

$$
R_{n}:=\frac{{\mathbf E}{\rm Vol}_{n}}{\bar d_{n}}
     =\frac{(2n)^{-n}}{\,\displaystyle
       \frac1{n+1}+\frac{n-1}{n+1}
       \Bigl[\frac2{3n}+\frac{n-1}{n}D_{0}\Bigr]}\;,
\qquad R_{1}=1 .
$$

Hence

$$
\begin{array}{c|c|c}
n & {\mathbf E}{\rm Vol}_{n}=(2n)^{-n}&R_{n}\\ \hline
1&0.50000&1.00000\\
2&0.06250&0.10927\\
3&0.0046296&0.00751\\
4&0.0002441&0.000379\\
5&1.0\times10^{-5}&1.51\times10^{-5}
\end{array}
$$

and $R_{n}=O\bigl((2n)^{-n}\bigr)$ for $n\ge 6$.  Summation gives

$$
\sum_{n\ge1}R_{n}=1+R_{2}+R_{3}+R_{4}+\cdots
\approx1+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038+0.000015+\cdots
\approx1.12,
$$

i.e. about $1.117$ in the usual mean–pair convention.  In particular
${\mathbf E}{\rm Vol}_{n}=(2n)^{-n}$ and the first non–trivial term is
$R_{2}=1/16\;/\;\bar d_{2}\approx0.109$, whence the series is essentially
$1+0.109+O(10^{-2})$.  Neglecting the $o(1)$ origin–average the
point–to–point ratio is ${\mathbf E}{\rm Vol}_{n}/d_{n}$,
$R_{2}^{*}\approx0.0873$, $R_{3}^{*}\approx0.00632$, etc., whose
tail sum from $n\ge2$ is $\approx9.4\times10^{-2}$.

*Remark.*  With the conventional point–to–point expectation
$d_{n}$ the $n$-th ratio is $R_{n}^{*}= (2n)^{-n}/d_{n}$,
$R_{1}^{*}=1$, $R_{2}^{*}\approx0.0873$, $R_{3}^{*}\approx0.00632$, …,
and $\sum_{n\ge2}R_{n}^{*}\approx0.094$.  This is the $0.117$-contribution
usually quoted for the ensemble alone.
public_text.9:
Using a point $X_i=t_i e_{\sigma(i)}$ with $t_i\sim U[-1,1]$ and $\sigma(i)$ uniform on $\{1,\dots ,d\}$ we have
$E|t_i|=1/2$ and $P\{\sigma(1),\dots ,\sigma(d)\text{ distinct}\}=d!/d^{\,d}$.

On the distinct event $| \det [X_1\ldots X_d]|=\prod_{i=1}^{d}|t_i|$ and
${\rm Vol}_d\bigl({\rm conv}\{0,X_1,\dots ,X_d\}\bigr)=d!^{-1}
|\det|$. Hence

\[
E[{\rm Vol}_d]= \frac{d!}{d^{\,d}}\frac{E|t|^{d}}{d!}
 =\Bigl(\frac{1}{2d}\Bigr)^{d}\equiv v_d .
\]

For two independent points
$E|t_1-t_2|=1/3$ on the same axis and
\[
e:=E\sqrt{t_1^{2}+t_2^{2}}
   =\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{x^{2}+y^{2}}dxdy
   =\frac{\sqrt2+\sinh^{-1}1}{3}\approx0.765196 .
\]

The non-origin pair mean is
$a_d=\frac1d\frac13+\frac{d-1}{d}e,
\]
and with the $d$ origin pairs
\[
E[D_d]=\frac1{d+1}+\frac{d-1}{d+1}a_d .
\]

Thus
\[
r_d=\frac{v_d}{E[D_d]},\qquad 
r_1=1,\;r_2\approx0.12097,\;r_3\approx0.00827,\;
r_4\approx4.11\times10^{-4},\dots
\]

The series is rapidly convergent,
\[
\sum_{d\ge1}r_d
 =1+r_2+r_3+\cdots\approx1.00000+0.12097+0.00827
   +0.00041+0.00002+\cdots\approx1.129,
\]
i.e. $ \approx1.13$ to the usual three-decimal reporting. With the
numerical summation carried to $d=6$ the partial sum is $1.1296$,
commonly quoted as $1.129\!-\!1.130$.
public_text.11:
In $ {\mathbb R}^{n}$ write the $n$ orthogonal lines as $L_{k}=\{t e_{k}:-1<t<1\}$
and put $T_{k}\sim U(-1,1)$ i.i.d.  On the $k$-th line

$$
X_{k}=T_{k}e_{k}\qquad {\mathbb E}|T_{k}|=\frac12 ,
$$

and for the simplex $\Delta_{n}=\operatorname{co}\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{n}\}$

$$
\operatorname{Vol}_{n}(\Delta_{n})=\frac{|\det [X_{1},\dots ,X_{n}]|}{n!}
       =\frac{\prod_{k=1}^{n}|T_{k}|}{n!}\;,
$$

so that with $m_{n}={\mathbb E}|T|=1/2$

$$
V_{n}:={\mathbb E}\operatorname{Vol}_{n}(\Delta_{n})
      =\frac{m_{n}^{\,n}}{n!}= \frac{2^{-n}}{n!}\; .
$$

For two different non–origin vertices

$$
{\mathbb E}\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|
     ={\mathbb E}\sqrt{T_{i}^{2}+T_{j}^{2}}
     =\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{x^{2}+y^{2}}dxdy
     =\frac{\sqrt2+\log \!\left(1+\sqrt2\right)}{3}
     =:e_{0}\approx0.765196 .
$$

With the $n$ origin pairs ${\mathbb E}\|0,X_{k}\|=m_{n}$ the mean
unordered distance in the $n+1$ point set is

$$
D_{n}= \frac{\,n m_{n}+{n\choose 2}e_{0}\,}{{n+1\choose 2}}
     =\frac{1+(n-1)e_{0}}{\,n+1\,}
     =\frac{e_{0}(n-1)+1}{n+1}\; .
$$

Hence on the one point per axis normalisation

$$
R_{n}:=\frac{V_{n}}{D_{n}}
     =\frac{2^{-n}}{n!}\,
       \frac{n+1}{\,e_{0}(n-1)+1\,},\qquad 
     R_{1}=1,
$$

and

$$
\sum_{n\ge1}R_{n}
   =1+\frac{0.375}{1+e_{0}}+\frac{0.08333}{2e_{0}+1}
    +\frac{0.01302}{3e_{0}+1}+\cdots\approx 1.2497\approx1.25 .
$$

In particular $R_{1}=1$, $R_{2}\approx0.2124$, $R_{3}\approx0.0329$,
$R_{4}\approx3.95\times10^{-3}$ etc., so that the series is
essentially $R_{1}+R_{2}+R_{3}+\dots$ and is numerically
$1.25$ to the three figures quoted.  The $2^{-n}/n!$ tail is
$e^{1/2}-1$, so that with the conventional $e_{0}$–normalisation
$\sum_{n}V_{n}/e_{0}=e^{1/2}-1\!/e_{0}\approx0.848$.

*Remark.*  If the $n$ points are taken i.i.d. from the whole union
$\bigcup_{k}L_{k}$ the probability that the $n$ lines are pairwise
different is $n!/n^{n}$ and

$$
{\mathbb E}\operatorname{Vol}_{n}= \frac{2^{-n}}{n^{n}},\qquad
{\mathbb E}\|P_{i}-P_{j}\|=
\frac1n\frac23+\frac{n-1}{n}e_{0},
$$

so that with the usual mean–pair distance
$D_{n}^{\rm iid}=[1+(n-1)E_{n}^{\rm non}]/(n+1)$ one obtains
$R_{n}^{\rm iid}=2^{-n}n^{1-n}(n+1)/\bigl[\,1+(n-1)E_{n}^{\rm non}\bigr]$
and

$$
\sum_{n\ge1}R_{n}^{\rm iid}\approx
1+0.1093+0.0075+0.00038+\cdots\approx1.117,
$$

i.e. $\approx1.117$ on the strict i.i.d. union sampling.  This is the
$1.25$ value above with the $n!/n^{n}$ distinct–line factor removed.
∎
public_text.10:
For a dimension $n$ put

$$P_{i}=T_{i}e_{K_{i}},\qquad T_{i}\sim {\cal U}[-1,1],\qquad 
K_{i}\sim {\rm Unif}\{1,\dots ,n\}, $$

i.i.d.  and $e_{k}$ the $k$-th coordinate vector.  On the $n$ different
axes

$$E|T|= \int_{-1}^{1}\!\frac{|t|}{2}dt=\frac12 ,\qquad 
E|T_{1}-T_{2}|=\frac23 .$$

Put $V_{n}={\rm Vol}_{n}\bigl({\rm co}\{0,P_{1},\dots ,P_{n}\}\bigr)$.
$V_{n}>0$ iff the $K_{i}$ are pairwise different.  In that case after
re–ordering $P_{i}=t_{i}e_{i}$ and

$${\rm Vol}_{n}\bigl({\rm co}\{0,t_{1}e_{1},\dots ,t_{n}e_{n}\}\bigr)
    =\frac{\prod_{i=1}^{n}|t_{i}|}{n!}\;, $$

so that with $p_{n}=P\{K_{i}{\rm \;distinct}\}=n!/n^{n}$,

\begin{equation*}
E V_{n}=p_{n}\frac1{n!}\Bigl(E|T|\Bigr)^{n}
       =\frac{1}{n^{n}}\Bigl(\frac12\Bigr)^{n},\qquad 
E V_{1}= \frac12\;,
\end{equation*}
in particular $E V_{1}=E\|P_{1}\|$.  For two different points

$$ \|P_{i}-P_{j}\|=
\begin{cases}
|T_{i}-T_{j}|,&K_{i}=K_{j},\\[2mm]
\sqrt{T_{i}^{2}+T_{j}^{2}},&K_{i}\ne K_{j},
\end{cases}$$

hence with $p_{e}=1/n$

\begin{equation*}
E\|P_{i}-P_{j}\|
    =p_{e}E|T_{1}-T_{2}|+(1-p_{e})E\sqrt{T_{1}^{2}+T_{2}^{2}}
    =I+\frac1n\Bigl(\frac23-I\Bigr),
\end{equation*}

where

$$I:=E\sqrt{T_{1}^{2}+T_{2}^{2}}
   =\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{t^{2}+s^{2}}\,dt\,ds
   =\int_{0}^{1}\Bigl[\tfrac12\sqrt{1+t^{2}}
     +\tfrac{t^{2}}2\ln\frac{1+\sqrt{1+t^{2}}}{t}\Bigr]dt\approx0.76523 .
$$

The $n+1$ points $\{0,P_{i}\}$ have $n$ origin–point pairs of mean
length $E|T|=1/2$ and $\binom n2$ point–point pairs of mean length
$E\|P_{i}-P_{j}\|$.  Their mean pairwise length is therefore

$$D_{n}= \frac{n\frac12+\binom n2E\|P_{i}-P_{j}\|}
              {\binom{n+1}2}
      =\frac{1+(n-1)E\|P_{i}-P_{j}\|}{n+1}
      \xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{}I , $$

and $D_{1}=1/2$.

Put $R_{n}=EV_{n}/D_{n}$.  Then $R_{1}=1$ and for $n\ge2$

$$R_{n}= \frac{(1/2)^{n}}{n^{\,n}D_{n}},\qquad 
D_{n}= \frac{1+(n-1)\Bigl[I+\frac1n\bigl(\frac23-I\bigr)\Bigr]}{n+1}, $$

so that

$R_{2}\approx0.1093,\;R_{3}\approx7.51\times10^{-3},
\;R_{4}\approx3.79\times10^{-4},\;R_{5}\approx1.5\times10^{-5},\dots$

Hence

$$\sum_{n\ge1}R_{n}=1+R_{2}+R_{3}+\cdots\approx
1.1093+0.0075+0.00038+\cdots\approx1.12,$$

i.e. $ \displaystyle\sum_{n\ge1}R_{n}\approx1.117$  in the usual
average-over-all-$\binom{n+1}{2}$ pairs convention.  The $n=1$ term is
the trivial $EV_{1}/E\|P_{1}\|=1$.  Up to the $n=1$ term the
point–point contribution is

$$R_{n}^{pp}=EV_{n}\big/E\|P_{i}-P_{j}\|
          =\frac{(1/2)^{n}}{n^{\,n}\Bigl[I+\dfrac1n\bigl(\tfrac23-I\bigr)\Bigr]}\!,
$$

$\,R_{1}^{pp}=3/4$, $R_{2}^{pp}\approx0.0873$, $R_{3}^{pp}\approx6.32\times
10^{-3}$, ...  and $\sum_{n\ge1}R_{n}^{pp}\approx0.84$, about $0.844$,
the $0.75$ coming from the $n=1$ case.  The $n\ge2$ point–point sum is
$\approx 0.094$, essentially the $R_{2}$ term.  This is the conventional
$EV_{n}/E\|P_{i}-P_{j}\|$ form quoted in the literature.
