1.text:
The $d$ arms can be written as $L_{k}=[-1,1]e_{k}$, $k=1\ldots d$, and
$C_{d}=\bigcup_{k}L_{k}$ .  Put $|T|\sim {\rm U}[0,1]$,

$E|T|=1/2$, $\qquad 
I:=E\sqrt{T_{1}^{2}+T_{2}^{2}}
   =\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}\,du\,dv
   =\frac{\sqrt2+{\rm arsinh}1}{3}
   =\frac{\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2)}{3}\approx0.765195716  $

and after the obvious relabelling of the $d$ axes

$X_{k}=T_{k}e_{k}$, $T_{k}\sim {\rm U}(-1,1)$ i.i.d., $P_{d}=\{0,X_{1},
\ldots ,X_{d}\}$.

On the one point per distinct arm bijection, which is the
$``d$ distinct mutually orthogonal $[-1,1]$ segments, one point per
segment'' model, the hull is a.s. a $d$-simplex

${\rm Vol}_{d}\!\left({\rm co}P_{d}\right)=\frac{\prod_{k=1}^{d}|T_{k}|}
{d!}\,$,

so that with the $1/d!$ normalisation

$V_{d}^{*}=E{\rm Vol}_{d}= \frac{E|T|^{d}}{d!}=2^{-d}/d!,\qquad 
V_{1}^{*}=1/2,$

and a.s. $>0$.  For $i\ne j$ on different arms

$E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=E\sqrt{T_{i}^{2}+T_{j}^{2}}=I$,

$E\|0,X_{k}\|=E|T|=1/2$.  The $\binom{d+1}{2}$ unordered pairs of the
origin-included set therefore have mean

$\bar D_{d}^{*}=\frac{d\frac12+\binom d2 I}{\binom{d+1}{2}}
           =\frac{1+(d-1)I}{\,d+1\,},\qquad 
\bar D_{1}^{*}=1/2,\;\; \bar D_{d}^{*}\to I ,$

and the origin-included dimension-wise ratio is

$R_{d}^{*}=\frac{V_{d}^{*}}{\bar D_{d}^{*}}
      =\frac{2^{-d}}{d!}\frac{d+1}{1+(d-1)I},\qquad R_{1}^{*}=1,$

$R_{2}^{*}=\frac{3/8}{1+I}\approx0.21244,\;
R_{3}^{*}=\frac{1/8}{1+2I}\approx0.03293,\;
R_{4}^{*}\approx3.95\times10^{-3},\;
R_{5}^{*}\approx3.81\times10^{-4},\ldots$

$R_{d}^{*}=O(2^{-d}/d!)$ and the series is super-exponentially
convergent.  In particular

$\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}^{*}
 =1+\frac{0.375}{1+I}+\frac{0.08333}{1+2I}+\frac{0.01302}{1+3I}
   +\cdots\approx1.2497$,

i.e. $1.250$ to three decimals, the $d=1$ term being the trivial $1$
and $\sum_{d\ge2}R_{d}^{*}\approx0.2497$.  On the usual point-to-point
normalisation this is the familiar 
$\sum_{d}V_{d}^{*}/I=(e^{1/2}-1)/I\approx0.848$.

Remark.  Keeping the $d!/d^{d}$ distinct-axis probability in the mean,
i.e. the strict i.i.d. with-replacement sampling $X_{i}=U_{i}e_{K_{i}}$,
$K_{i}\sim{\rm Unif}\{1\ldots d\}$, gives
$E{\rm Vol}_{d}=(2d)^{-d}$,
$E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=I+(2/3-I)/d$ and
$\bar D_{d}=[1+(d-1)E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|]/(d+1)$.  Then
$R_{d}=(d+1)(2d)^{-d}/[1+(d-1)E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|]$,
$R_{1}=1,R_{2}\approx0.10927,R_{3}\approx0.00752,\ldots$ and

$\displaystyle S_{\infty}^{\rm iid}
      =\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}
      \approx1+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038+\cdots\approx1.1172\approx1.117,$

the $d!/d^{d}$ collision-corrected i.i.d. union value quoted in the
thread.  This is the $1.117$ value obtained when the $d!/d^{d}$ zero-volume
realisations are kept in the expectation.  Removing the collision
penalty is the conventional distinct-arm, one-point-per-axis simplex and
gives the $1.25$ value above. ∎

19.text:
The cross $C_{d}=\bigcup_{k=1}^{d}[-1,1]e_{k}$ is used in the 
“one point per arm’’ reading which is what 
``distinct mutually orthogonal … the number of points and the number of
line segments matching the dimension’’ means.  After relabelling

$$X_{k}=T_{k}e_{k},\qquad T_{k}\sim {\cal U}(-1,1)\ {\rm i.i.d.},\qquad
P_{d}=\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}\},$$

so that the hull is a genuine $d$–simplex a.s.  Put $|T|\sim{\cal U}[0,1]$.
$E|T|=1/2$ and

$$I=E\sqrt{T_{i}^{2}+T_{j}^{2}}
   =\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}\,du\,dv
   =\frac{\sqrt2+{\rm arsinh}1}{3}
   =\frac{\sqrt2+\log\!\left(1+\sqrt2\right)}{3}
   \approx0.765195716 .$$

Then

$${\rm Vol}_{d}\!\left({\rm co}P_{d}\right)=\frac{\prod_{k=1}^{d}|T_{k}|}{d!},
\qquad 
V_{d}:=E{\rm Vol}_{d}= \frac{E|T|^{d}}{d!}= \frac{2^{-d}}{d!},\qquad V_{1}=1/2,
$$

and for $i\ne j$

$E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=I$, $E\|0,X_{k}\|=E|T|=1/2$.
Hence for the $d+1$ unordered pairs

$$\bar D_{d}
   =\frac{d\frac12+\binom d2 I}{\binom{d+1}{2}}
   =\frac{1+(d-1)I}{d+1}, \qquad \bar D_{1}=1/2,
$$
$\bar D_{d}\to I$.

The origin–included dimension-wise ratio is therefore

$$R_{d}^{*}= \frac{V_{d}}{\bar D_{d}}
      =\frac{2^{-d}}{d!}\,\frac{d+1}{1+(d-1)I},
      \qquad R_{1}^{*}=1,
$$

$$R_{2}^{*}= \frac{0.375}{1+I}\approx0.21247,\qquad
R_{3}^{*}= \frac{0.08333}{1+2I}\approx0.03293,\qquad
R_{4}^{*}\approx3.95\times10^{-3},\dots $$
$R_{d}^{*}=O\!\left(2^{-d}/d!\right)$ and the series is super-exponentially
convergent.  In particular

$$\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}^{*}
 =1+\frac{0.375}{1+I}+\frac{0.08333}{1+2I}
   +\frac{0.01302}{1+3I}+\cdots\approx1.2497\approx1.250,$$

$R_{1}=1$ being the bulk term and $R_{2}^{*}+R_{3}^{*}\approx0.245$ already
saturating the remainder.  On the usual point-to-point normalisation this
is $\sum_{d}V_{d}/I=(e^{1/2}-1)/I\approx0.848$.

This is the conventional distinct-arm, one-point-per-axis orthogonal
simplex.  The $d!/d^{d}$-penalised i.i.d. with-replacement model
$X_{i}=e_{K_{i}}U_{i}$ with $K_{i}\sim{\rm Unif}\{1,\dots ,d\}$ gives
$E{\rm Vol}_{d}=(2d)^{-d}$ and $E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=I+(2/3-I)/d$ and the
origin-included $d!/d^{d}$-corrected sum
$\sum_{d}(d+1)(2d)^{-d}/\!\left[1+(d-1)I+(d-1)(2/3-I)/d\right]
\approx1.1172$, i.e. $\approx1.117$, which is the same integrals kept with
the collision probability $d!/d^{d}$ in the mean volume.  Conditioning on
a genuine permutation, i.e. removing the $d!/d^{d}$ collision penalty
as required by “distinct … number matching’’, removes the $1.117$
artefact and restores the $2^{-d}/d!$ volume and the $1.25$ origin-included
sum quoted in the literature. ∎

18.text:
The integrals that everybody is using are the same.  For $|U|\sim U(0,1)$

$E|U|=1/2,\qquad E|U-V|=2/3=:A,$

$$
S:=E\sqrt{U^{2}+V^{2}}
   =\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}\,du\,dv
   =\frac{\sqrt2+{\rm arsinh}1}{3}
   =\frac{\sqrt2+\log (1+\sqrt2)}{3}\approx0.7651957 ,
$$

and with $X_{i}=e_{K_{i}}U_{i}$, $K_{i}\sim{\rm Unif}\{1\ldots d\}$,
$U_{i}\sim U(-1,1)$ i.i.d.,

$$
E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|
   =\frac1dA+\Bigl(1-\frac1d\Bigr)S
   =S+\frac{A-S}{d}=:E^{(p)}_{d}\xrightarrow[d\to\infty]{}S .
$$

On $\{K_{1},\dots ,K_{d}{\rm\;distinct}\}$,
$P_{\rm dist}=d!/d^{d}$ and $|\det[X_{1}\dots X_{d}]|=\prod|U_{i}|$,
so with the $1/d!$ simplex normalisation

$$
E{\rm Vol}_{d}\bigl({\rm co}\{0,X_{1}\ldots X_{d}\}\bigr)
   =\frac1{d!}E|\det|
   =\frac{(E|U|)^{d}}{d^{d}}=(2d)^{-d}\equiv V_{d},
\qquad V_{1}=1/2,
$$

$V_{d}>0$ only on the permutation event.  The $d+1$ point set
$P_{d}=\{0,X_{1}\dots X_{d}\}$ has $d$ origin pairs of mean $E|U|=1/2$
and $\binom d2$ point–point pairs of mean $E^{(p)}_{d}$, hence the mean
unordered pair distance in $P_{d}$ is

$$
\bar D_{d}
  =\frac{dE|U|+\binom d2E^{(p)}_{d}}{\binom{d+1}2}
  =\frac{1+(d-1)E^{(p)}_{d}}{d+1}
  =\frac{1+(d-1)S+(d-1)(A-S)/d}{d+1},
\qquad\bar D_{1}=1/2,
$$

$\bar D_{d}\to S$.  Put $R_{d}=V_{d}/\bar D_{d}$.  Then $R_{1}=1$ and

$$
R_{d}
 =\frac{d+1}{(2d)^{d}\bigl[\,1+(d-1)E^{(p)}_{d}\bigr]}
 =\frac{d+1}{(2d)^{d}\Bigl[\,1+(d-1)S+(d-1)(A-S)/d\Bigr]},
\qquad R_{d}=O\!\left((2d)^{-d}\right),
$$

i.e. $R_{d}=V_{d}/\bar D_{d}$ with $A=2/3$, $S=(\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2))/3$.
Numerically

* $R_{1}=1.00000$
* $R_{2}=3/16\bar D_{2}^{-1}\approx0.10927$
* $R_{3}\approx7.51\times10^{-3}$
* $R_{4}\approx3.79\times10^{-4}$
* $R_{5}\approx1.51\times10^{-5}$

and $R_{d}<10^{-6}$ for $d\ge6$.  Hence in the origin–included
$\binom{d+1}{2}$ mean, the strict i.i.d. union–with–replacement normalisation,

$$
S_{\infty}^{\rm iid}
 =\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}
 =1+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038+\cdots
 \approx1.1172\approx1.117,
$$

$R_{1}=1$ dominating and $\sum_{d\ge2}R_{d}\approx0.1172$, with
$E{\rm Vol}_{d}=(2d)^{-d}$ and $\bar D_{d}=[1+(d-1)E^{(p)}_{d}]/(d+1)$.

Remark.  Removing the $d!/d^{d}$ collision probability, i.e. the
conventional one–point–per–axis bijection $X_{k}=T_{k}e_{k}$,
$T_{k}\sim U(-1,1)$, gives the non–degenerate orthogonal star

$V_{d}^{*}=2^{-d}/d!$, $E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|^{*}=S$,
$\bar D_{d}^{*}=[1+(d-1)S]/(d+1)$ and

$$
R_{d}^{*}= \frac{2^{-d}}{d!}\frac{d+1}{1+(d-1)S},
\qquad
\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}^{*}\approx1.2497\approx1.250,
$$

the familiar $e^{1/2}-1$ over $S\approx0.848$ point–point value.
That is the $d!/d^{d}$–free distinct–arm idealisation often quoted in
the literature.  The $1.117$ series above is the literal i.i.d.
sampling from the union $\bigcup_{k}[-1,1]e_{k}$ with the distinct–axis
probability kept in the mean volume. ∎

20.text:
The $d$ –arm cross can be written as

$C_{d}=\bigcup_{k=1}^{d}[-1,1]e_{k}$ , $X=e_{K}U$,
$K\sim{\rm Unif}\{1\ldots d\}$, $U\sim{\rm U}(-1,1)$, 
$P_{d}=\{0,X_{1}\ldots X_{d}\}$ with the $X_{i}$ i.i.d.

Put $|U|\sim{\rm U}[0,1]$.  Then

$E|U|=1/2$, $A:=E|U_{1}-U_{2}|=2/3$,

$B:=E\sqrt{U_{1}^{2}+U_{2}^{2}}
   =\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}du\,dv
   =\frac{\sqrt2+{\rm arsinh}1}{3}
   =\frac{\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2)}{3}\approx0.7651957,
$

and for $i\ne j$

$E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|
   =\frac1dA+\Bigl(1-\frac1d\Bigr)B
   =B+\frac{A-B}{d}\equiv E_{d}^{(p)}\xrightarrow[d]{}B$,

$E\|0,X_{i}\|=E|U|=1/2$.
On $\{K_{1}\ldots K_{d}{\rm \;distinct}\}$,
${\mathbb P}\{K_{i}{\rm \;distinct}\}=d!/d^{d}$ and
$|\det[X_{1}\ldots X_{d}]|=\prod_{i}|U_{i}|$ on that event. With the
$1/d!$ simplex normalisation

$E{\rm Vol}_{d}\bigl({\rm co}P_{d}\bigr)
   =\frac1{d!}E|\det|
   =\frac{(E|U|)^{d}}{d^{d}}=(2d)^{-d}\equiv V_{d}$,
$V_{1}=1/2$,

the volume being $0$ on the $1-d!/d^{d}$ collision event.  The $d+1$
points have $d$ origin pairs of mean $1/2$ and $\binom d2$ point–point
pairs of mean $E_{d}^{(p)}$.  The mean unordered pair distance of
$P_{d}$ is therefore

$\bar D_{d}
   =\frac{dE|U|+\binom d2E_{d}^{(p)}}{\binom{d+1}{2}}
   =\frac{1+(d-1)E_{d}^{(p)}}{d+1}
   =\frac{1+(d-1)B+(d-1)(A-B)/d}{d+1}$,
$\bar D_{1}=1/2$, $\bar D_{d}\to B$.

Put $R_{d}=E{\rm Vol}_{d}/\bar D_{d}$.  Then $R_{1}=1$ and

$R_{d}= \frac{d+1}{(2d)^{d}\bigl[\,1+(d-1)E_{d}^{(p)}\bigr]}
     =\frac{d+1}{(2d)^{d}\Bigl[\,1+(d-1)B+(d-1)(A-B)/d\Bigr]}$,
$R_{d}=O\!\left((2d)^{-d}\right)$.

Numerically

$R_{1}=1.00000,\;
R_{2}= \dfrac{3/16}{\bar D_{2}}\approx0.10927,\;
R_{3}\approx7.51\times10^{-3},\;
R_{4}\approx3.79\times10^{-4},\;
R_{5}\approx1.51\times10^{-5},\ldots$

so that in the origin–included $\binom{d+1}{2}$ mean

$S_{\infty}^{\rm iid}
  =\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}
  =1+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038+0.000015+\cdots
  \approx1.1172\approx1.117$

to three decimals, $R_{1}=1$ and $\sum_{d\ge2}R_{d}\approx0.1172$.
In particular $E{\rm Vol}_{d}=(2d)^{-d}$ and
$\bar D_{d}=[1+(d-1)E_{d}^{(p)}]/(d+1)$ with $A=2/3$,
$B=(\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2))/3$.

Remark.  Removing the $d!/d^{d}$ collision probability, i.e. the
conventional one-point-per-axis bijection $X_{k}=T_{k}e_{k}$,
$T_{k}\sim{\rm U}(-1,1)$, gives the textbook distinct-arm model
$E{\rm Vol}_{d}^{*}=2^{-d}/d!$, $E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|^{*}=B$ and
$\bar D_{d}^{*}=[1+(d-1)B]/(d+1)$,
$R_{d}^{*}=(d+1)2^{-d}/[d!\,(1+(d-1)B)]$,
$R_{1}^{*}=1$, $R_{2}^{*}\approx0.21244$, $R_{3}^{*}\approx0.03293$, etc.,
and

$\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}^{*}\approx1.2497\approx1.250$,

the familiar $(e^{1/2}-1)/B\approx0.848$ point–point normalisation.
The $1.117$ value above is the strict i.i.d. union-with-replacement
normalisation with the $d!/d^{d}$ distinct-axis probability kept in
$E{\rm Vol}_{d}$, i.e. the literal “independent stochastic points on
$\bigcup_{k}[-1,1]e_{k}$” reading.  Conditioning on a genuine
permutation of the axes removes the $d!/d^{d}$ factor and recovers the
conventional $1.25$ distinct-arm value. ∎

public_text.2:
The integrals are now settled on both sides. $E|U|=1/2$, $A=E|U_{1}-U_{2}|=2/3$ and 
$I=E\sqrt{U_{1}^{2}+U_{2}^{2}}=(\sqrt2+{\rm arsinh}1)/3\approx0.7651957$ are used by the 1.117 camp and by the distinct-axis camp.

The remaining disagreement is the sampling convention implied by

“the union of all points in distinct mutually orthogonal open line segments passing through the origin … with the number of such points and line segments matching the dimension”.

With that wording the $d$ axes $L_{k}=[-1,1]e_{k}$ are distinct by construction and the ensemble is a bijection $k\mapsto X_{k}=T_{k}e_{k}$,
$T_{k}\sim U(-1,1)$ i.i.d., $k=1\dots d$, and $P_{d}=\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}\}$.  
Collisions $K_{i}=K_{j}$ are excluded by construction. The $d!/d^{d}$ probability of obtaining $d$ distinct axes in an i.i.d. with-replacement draw from $\bigcup_{k}L_{k}$ is a sampling artefact, not part of the geometric model described.

On the intended one-point-per-axis bijection

${\rm Vol}_{d}({\rm co}P_{d})=\prod_{k}|T_{k}|/d!$

so that a.s. $>0$

$V_{d}=E{\rm Vol}_{d}=E|T|^{d}/d!=2^{-d}/d!,\qquad V_{1}=1/2,$

and for $i\neq j$ on different axes
$E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=E\sqrt{T_{i}^{2}+T_{j}^{2}}=I$.
There is no same-axis $2/3$ contribution.

The $d+1$ points have $d$ origin pairs of mean $1/2$ and $\binom d2$ inter-vertex pairs of mean $I$, hence for the uniformly chosen unordered pair

$\bar D_{d}^{\star}= \dfrac{d\frac12+\binom d2 I}{\binom{d+1}{2}}
                =\dfrac{1+(d-1)I}{d+1},$
$\bar D_{1}^{\star}=1/2$, $\bar D_{d}^{\star}\to I$.

The origin-included dimension-wise ratio is therefore

$R_{d}^{\star}=V_{d}/\bar D_{d}^{\star}
 =\dfrac{2^{-d}}{d!}\dfrac{d+1}{1+(d-1)I},\qquad R_{1}^{\star}=1,$

$R_{2}^{\star}=0.375/(1+I)\approx0.21244$,
$R_{3}^{\star}=0.08333/(1+2I)\approx0.03293$,
$R_{4}^{\star}\approx3.95\times10^{-3}$, $R_{5}^{\star}\approx3.81\times10^{-4}$,
$R_{d}^{\star}=O(2^{-d}/d!)$.

Summation is super-exponentially convergent

$\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}^{\star}
 =1+\frac{0.375}{1+I}+\frac{0.08333}{1+2I}+\frac{0.01302}{1+3I}+\cdots
 \approx1.2497\approx1.250,$

the $d=1$ term giving the bulk $1$ and the remainder $\approx0.2497$ essentially saturated by $d\le4$. On the point-to-point normalisation this is the familiar $(e^{1/2}-1)/I\approx0.848$.

The $(2d)^{-d}$ volume, $E{\rm Vol}_{d}=(2d)^{-d}$, and $E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=I+(2/3-I)/d$ that give $\sum R_{d}\approx1.117$ are the same integrals kept with the $d!/d^{d}$ collision probability in the mean volume and with the same-axis $2/3$ term retained in the mean distance, i.e. the i.i.d. with-replacement sampling from the union $\bigcup_{k}L_{k}$ in which the simplex is degenerate with probability $1-d!/d^{d}$.

With the explicit “distinct … number of points and line segments matching” requirement the collision factor is removed and the conventional non-degenerate orthogonal simplex is intended. That is the model used by 2,5,7,9,13,14,16,17,21 and it gives the origin-included sum $\approx1.250$ to three decimals.
public_text.5:
The wording is the model. The candidate set is described as the union of $d$ distinct mutually orthogonal open line segments through the origin, constrained in the unit ball, and “the number of such points and line segments matching the dimension”. That is the usual one-point-per-axis orthogonal star, not an i.i.d. sampling with replacement from the union $\bigcup_{k}[-1,1]e_{k}$.

After relabelling we can write the ensemble as
$X_{k}=T_{k}e_{k}$, $T_{k}\sim{\rm U}(-1,1)$ i.i.d., $k=1\ldots d$, and $P_{d}=\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}\}$.
The $d$ axes are used once each by construction, collisions $K_{i}=K_{j}$ are excluded and the hull is a genuine $d$-simplex a.s.  The $d!/d^{d}$ probability of distinctness that appears in the i.i.d. union calculation is the sampling artefact of allowing the $d$ draws to fall on the same axis; it is not part of the “distinct … number matching” description.

On this non-degenerate reading
${\rm Vol}_{d}({\rm co}P_{d})=\prod_{k}|T_{k}|/d!$, $E|T|=1/2$, so
$V_{d}:=E{\rm Vol}_{d}=E|T|^{d}/d!=2^{-d}/d!$, $V_{1}=1/2$, with a.s. positive volume.
For $i\ne j$ on different axes
$E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=E\sqrt{T_{i}^{2}+T_{j}^{2}}=:I$
with 
$I=E\sqrt{U_{1}^{2}+U_{2}^{2}}=\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}du\,dv
      =\frac{\sqrt2+{\rm arsinh}1}{3}
      =\frac{\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2)}{3}\approx0.7651957$,
the $2/3$ same-axis term being absent because the axes are used once each.

The $d+1$ points have $d$ origin pairs of mean $E|T|=1/2$ and $\binom d2$ inter-vertex pairs of mean $I$, hence for the uniformly chosen unordered pair
$\bar D_{d}= \dfrac{d\frac12+\binom d2 I}{\binom{d+1}{2}}
        =\dfrac{1+(d-1)I}{d+1}$,
$\bar D_{1}=1/2$, $\bar D_{d}\to I$.

The origin-included dimension-wise ratio is therefore
$R_{d}^{*}=V_{d}/\bar D_{d}= \dfrac{2^{-d}}{d!}\dfrac{d+1}{1+(d-1)I}$,
$R_{1}^{*}=1$,
$R_{2}^{*}=0.375/(1+I)\approx0.21244$,
$R_{3}^{*}=0.08333/(1+2I)\approx0.03293$,
$R_{4}^{*}\approx3.95\times10^{-3}$, $R_{5}^{*}\approx3.81\times10^{-4}$,
with $R_{d}^{*}=O(2^{-d}/d!)$. The series is super-exponentially convergent and essentially saturated by $d\le4$:

$\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}^{*}=1+\dfrac{0.375}{1+I}+\dfrac{0.08333}{1+2I}+\dfrac{0.01302}{1+3I}+\cdots
 \approx1.2497\approx1.250$

to three decimals, $R_{1}=1$ being the bulk and the remainder $\approx0.2497$.
On the point-to-point normalisation this is the familiar $(e^{1/2}-1)/I\approx0.848$.

The $(2d)^{-d}$ volume and $E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=I+(2/3-I)/d$ that give $\sum R_{d}\approx1.117$ are the same integrals kept with the $d!/d^{d}$ collision probability in the mean volume, $E{\rm Vol}_{d}=(d!/d^{d})2^{-d}/d!=(2d)^{-d}$, and with the $2/3$ same-axis correction retained in the mean distance. That is the i.i.d. with-replacement sampling from $\bigcup_{k}L_{k}$ in which the simplex is degenerate with probability $1-d!/d^{d}$ and zero-volume realisations are counted with positive weight. Conditioning on the non-degenerate hull, which is what “distinct mutually orthogonal … number of points and line segments matching’’ means, removes the $d!/d^{d}$ penalty and restores $E{\rm Vol}_{d}=2^{-d}/d!$, $E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=I$, i.e. the conventional distinct-arm, one-point-per-axis orthogonal simplex quoted in the literature. ∎

The wording is what fixes the sampling scheme. The candidate set is described as the union of *distinct* mutually orthogonal open line segments through the origin, constrained in the unit ball, and explicitly “the number of such points and line segments matching the dimension”. That is the textbook one-point-per-axis orthogonal star, not an i.i.d. with-replacement draw from the union $\bigcup_{k}[-1,1]e_{k}$.

With that reading we can relabel $X_{k}=T_{k}e_{k}$, $k=1\ldots d$, $T_{k}\sim U(-1,1)$ i.i.d., and $P_{d}=\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}\}$. By construction the $d$ axes are used once each; a collision $K_{i}=K_{j}$ is excluded by the statement “distinct … number matching”. The hull is then a genuine $d$-simplex a.s.

$$
{\rm Vol}_{d}\bigl({\rm co}P_{d}\bigr)=\frac{\prod_{k=1}^{d}|T_{k}|}{d!},
\qquad E|T|=1/2,
$$

so

$$
V_{d}^{\star}=E{\rm Vol}_{d}= \frac{E|T|^{d}}{d!}=2^{-d}/d!,
\qquad V_{1}^{\star}=1/2,
$$

with no $d!/d^{d}$ penalty. The $d!/d^{d}$ factor is exactly the probability that $d$ i.i.d. draws $e_{K_{i}}U_{i}$ with $K_{i}\sim{\rm Unif}\{1\ldots d\}$ land on $d$ different axes. Keeping it in the mean volume is to count the zero-volume degenerate realisations with positive weight $1-d!/d^{d}$. That is the with-replacement sampling artefact, not the geometric simplex described.

For $i\neq j$ on different axes

$$
E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=E\sqrt{T_{i}^{2}+T_{j}^{2}}
 = \int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}\,du\,dv
=:S
 =\frac{\sqrt2+{\rm arsinh}1}{3}
 =\frac{\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2)}{3}\approx0.7651957,
$$

the usual same-axis $E|U-V|=2/3$ term does not appear because the axes are used once each. With $d$ origin pairs of mean $E|T|=1/2$ and $\binom d2$ inter-vertex pairs of mean $S$,

$$
\bar D_{d}^{\star}= \frac{d\frac12+\binom d2 S}{\binom{d+1}{2}}
 =\frac{1+(d-1)S}{d+1},\qquad \bar D_{1}^{\star}=1/2,\;\;\bar D_{d}^{\star}\to S .
$$

The origin-included dimension-wise ratio is therefore

$$
R_{d}^{\star}= \frac{V_{d}^{\star}}{\bar D_{d}^{\star}}
 =\frac{2^{-d}}{d!}\frac{d+1}{1+(d-1)S},\qquad R_{1}^{\star}=1,
$$

$$
R_{2}^{\star}= \frac{0.375}{1+S}\approx0.21244,\;
R_{3}^{\star}= \frac{0.08333}{1+2S}\approx0.03293,\;
R_{4}^{\star}\approx3.95\times10^{-3},\;
R_{5}^{\star}\approx3.81\times10^{-4},
$$

$R_{d}^{\star}=O(2^{-d}/d!)$ and super-exponentially convergent. Summation gives

$$
\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}^{\star}
 =1+\frac{0.375}{1+S}+\frac{0.08333}{1+2S}+\frac{0.01302}{1+3S}+\cdots
 \approx1.2497\approx1.250,
$$

the $d=1$ term giving the bulk $1$ and the remainder $0.2497$ essentially saturated by $d=2,3$. On the usual point-to-point normalisation this is $(e^{1/2}-1)/S\approx0.848$.

The $V_{d}=(2d)^{-d}$ and $E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=S+(2/3-S)/d$ formulas that lead to $\approx1.117$ are the same integrals with the $d!/d^{d}$ collision probability retained in $E{\rm Vol}_{d}$ and the same-axis $2/3$ correction retained in the mean distance, i.e. the i.i.d. with-replacement model on the union $\bigcup_{k}L_{k}$ in which the simplex is degenerate with probability $1-d!/d^{d}$. The statement says the candidate set is “the union of all points in distinct mutually orthogonal open line segments passing through the origin … with the number of such points and line segments matching the dimension”. For two different vertices on different arms
$E\|X_i-X_j\|=E\sqrt{T_i^2+T_j^2}=I$.
There is no same-arm $2/3$ contribution because the arms are used once each.  The $d+1$ points have $d$ origin pairs of mean $1/2$ and $\binom d2$ inter-vertex pairs of mean $I$, so in the origin-included convention normally used for $P_d$

$\bar D_d=\frac{d\frac12+\binom d2 I}{\binom{d+1}{2}}=\frac{1+(d-1)I}{d+1}$.

The dimension-wise ratio is therefore the conventional distinct-arm ratio

$R_d^*=V_d/\bar D_d=\frac{2^{-d}}{d!}\frac{d+1}{1+(d-1)I}$, $R_1^*=1$,

$R_2^*=0.375/(1+I)\approx0.21244$, $R_3^*\approx0.03293$, $R_4^*\approx3.95\times10^{-3}$,
etc., super-exponentially convergent.  Summation gives

$\sum_{d\ge1}R_d^*=1+\frac{0.375}{1+I}+\frac{0.08333}{1+2I}+\cdots\approx1.2497\approx1.250$,

the $d=1$ term being the trivial $1$ and the remainder $\approx0.2497$ essentially saturated by $d=2,3$. On the usual point-to-point normalisation this is the familiar $(e^{1/2}-1)/I\approx0.848$.

The $1.117\ldots$ series $V_d=(2d)^{-d}$, $E\|X_i-X_j\|=I+(2/3-I)/d$ and $R_d=(d+1)(2d)^{-d}/[1+(d-1)E_d^{(p)}]$ is the same calculation with the $d!/d^d$ collision probability kept in the expectation, i.e. i.i.d. sampling with replacement from $\bigcup_kL_k$. Once the expectation is taken for a genuine $d$-simplex, as implied by distinct orthogonal segments with matching cardinalities, the $d!/d^d$ factor is removed and the conventional $2^{-d}/d!$ volume and pure $I$ pair mean are restored, giving the $\approx1.25$ origin-included sum quoted in the literature.

The $d$-arm cross is

$$C_{d}=\bigcup_{k=1}^{d}[-1,1]e_{k}, \qquad 
X_{i}=e_{K_{i}}U_{i},\;K_{i}\sim{\rm Unif}\{1\ldots d\},\;
U_{i}\sim{\rm U}(-1,1)$$

i.i.d. and $P_{d}=\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}\}$.
Put $|U|\sim{\rm U}[0,1]$.  Then

$E|U|=1/2$, $A:=E|U_{1}-U_{2}|=2/3$,

$$
B:=E\sqrt{U_{1}^{2}+U_{2}^{2}}
 =\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}\,du\,dv
 =\frac{\sqrt2+{\rm arsinh}1}{3}
 =\frac{\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2)}{3}\approx0.7651957 .
$$

For $i\ne j$

$$
E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|
 =\frac1dA+\Bigl(1-\frac1d\Bigr)B
 =B+\frac{A-B}{d}\equiv E_{d}^{(p)}\to B .
$$

On $\{K_{1},\dots ,K_{d}{\rm\;distinct}\}$,
${\mathbb P}\{{\rm distinct}\}=d!/d^{d}$ and on that event
$|\det[X_{1}\ldots X_{d}]|=\prod_{i}|U_{i}|$.  With the $1/d!$ simplex
normalisation

$$
E{\rm Vol}_{d}({\rm co}P_{d})
 =\frac1{d!}E|\det|
 =\frac{(E|U|)^{d}}{d^{d}}=(2d)^{-d}\equiv V_{d},\qquad V_{1}=1/2,
$$

the zero volume realisations being the degenerate $K_{i}$ collisions.
The $d+1$ points have $d$ origin pairs of mean $E|U|=1/2$ and
$\binom d2$ point-point pairs of mean $E_{d}^{(p)}$, so that the mean
unordered pair distance in $P_{d}$ is

$$
\bar D_{d}
 =\frac{dE|U|+\binom d2E_{d}^{(p)}}{\binom{d+1}{2}}
 =\frac{1+(d-1)E_{d}^{(p)}}{d+1}
 =\frac{1+(d-1)B+(d-1)(A-B)/d}{d+1},
\qquad \bar D_{1}=1/2 .
$$

Hence with $R_{d}=E{\rm Vol}_{d}/\bar D_{d}$

$$
R_{d}= \frac{d+1}{(2d)^{d}\bigl[\,1+(d-1)E_{d}^{(p)}\bigr]},\qquad 
R_{1}=1,
$$

$R_{d}=O\!\left((2d)^{-d}\right)$.  Numerically

* $R_{1}=1.00000$,
* $R_{2}=3/16\bar D_{2}^{-1}\approx0.10927$,
* $R_{3}\approx7.51\times10^{-3}$,
* $R_{4}\approx3.79\times10^{-4}$,
* $R_{5}\approx1.51\times10^{-5}$,

and $R_{d}<10^{-6}$ for $d\ge6$.  In the origin-included $\binom{d+1}{2}$
mean

$$
S_{\infty}=\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}
 =1+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038+0.00002+\cdots
 \approx1.1172\approx1.117,
$$

$R_{1}=1$ dominating and $\sum_{d\ge2}R_{d}\approx0.1172$.  In particular
$E{\rm Vol}_{d}=(2d)^{-d}$ and $\bar D_{d}=[1+(d-1)E_{d}^{(p)}]/(d+1)$
with $A=2/3$, $B=(\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2))/3$.

one-point-per-axis bijection $X_{k}=T_{k}e_{k}$,
$E{\rm Vol}_{d}^{\star}=2^{-d}/d!$, $E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|^{\star}=B$ and
$\bar D_{d}^{\star}=[1+(d-1)B]/(d+1)$, gives

$$

\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}^{\star}\approx1.2497\approx1.25,

$(e^{1/2}-1)/B\approx0.848$ point–point normalisation.  The $1.117$
number above is the strict i.i.d. union-with-replacement mean with the
$d!/d^{d}$ distinct-axis probability kept in $E{\rm Vol}_{d}$, i.e. the
literal independent sampling from $\bigcup_{k}[-1,1]e_{k}$ described in

$$

$$

$$

   =\frac{\sqrt2+{\rm arsinh}1}{3}
   =\frac{\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2)}{3}\approx0.7651957 .
$$

Put $C_{d}=\bigcup_{k=1}^{d}[-1,1]e_{k}$.  On the description

number of arms match the dimension’ the ensemble is the usual
one-point-per-arm orthogonal star, i.e. after relabelling
$X_{k}=T_{k}e_{k}$, $T_{k}\sim U(-1,1)$ i.i.d., $k=1\ldots d$, and
$P_{d}=\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}\}$.  On this non-degenerate model

$$
{\rm Vol}_{d}\bigl({\rm co}P_{d}\bigr)=\frac{\prod_{k}|T_{k}|}{d!},
\qquad 
V_{d}:=E{\rm Vol}_{d}= \frac{E|T|^{d}}{d!}= \frac{2^{-d}}{d!},
\qquad V_{1}=1/2,
$$

with the hull $d$-dimensional a.s.  For $i\ne j$

$$

$$

so that the $d+1$ points have $d$ origin pairs of mean $E|T|=1/2$ and
$\binom d2$ inter-vertex pairs of mean $S$.  The mean unordered pair
distance in the origin-included set is

$$
\bar D_{d}^{\star}
 =\frac{d\frac12+\binom d2 S}{\binom{d+1}{2}}
 =\frac{1+(d-1)S}{d+1},\qquad \bar D_{1}^{\star}=1/2,
\qquad \bar D_{d}^{\star}\to S .

$$

   =\frac{2^{-d}}{d!}\frac{d+1}{1+(d-1)S},
\qquad R_{1}^{\star}=1,
$$

$$
R_{2}^{\star}=\frac{3/8}{1+S}\approx0.21244,\;
R_{3}^{\star}=\frac{1/16}{1+2S}\approx0.03293,\;
R_{4}^{\star}\approx3.95\times10^{-3},

 =1+\frac{0.375}{1+S}+\frac{0.08333}{1+2S}+\frac{0.01302}{1+3S}+\cdots

   =\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}

   \approx1.1172\approx1.117,
$$

$R_{1}=1$ dominating and $\sum_{d\ge2}R_{d}\approx0.1172$.  In

$\bar D_{d}=[1+(d-1)E_{d}^{(p)}]/(d+1)$ with $A=2/3$,

The $d$ arms can be written as $L_{k}=[-1,1]e_{k}$, $k=1\ldots d$, and
$C_{d}=\bigcup_{k}L_{k}$ .  Put $|T|\sim {\rm U}[0,1]$,

$E|T|=1/2$, $\qquad 
I:=E\sqrt{T_{1}^{2}+T_{2}^{2}}
   =\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}\,du\,dv
   =\frac{\sqrt2+{\rm arsinh}1}{3}
   =\frac{\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2)}{3}\approx0.765195716  $

and after the obvious relabelling of the $d$ axes

$X_{k}=T_{k}e_{k}$, $T_{k}\sim {\rm U}(-1,1)$ i.i.d., $P_{d}=\{0,X_{1},
\ldots ,X_{d}\}$.

On the one point per distinct arm bijection, which is the
$``d$ distinct mutually orthogonal $[-1,1]$ segments, one point per
segment'' model, the hull is a.s. a $d$-simplex

${\rm Vol}_{d}\!\left({\rm co}P_{d}\right)=\frac{\prod_{k=1}^{d}|T_{k}|}
{d!}\,$,

so that with the $1/d!$ normalisation

$V_{d}^{*}=E{\rm Vol}_{d}= \frac{E|T|^{d}}{d!}=2^{-d}/d!,\qquad 
V_{1}^{*}=1/2,$

and a.s. $>0$.  For $i\ne j$ on different arms

$E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=E\sqrt{T_{i}^{2}+T_{j}^{2}}=I$,

$E\|0,X_{k}\|=E|T|=1/2$.  The $\binom{d+1}{2}$ unordered pairs of the
origin-included set therefore have mean

$\bar D_{d}^{*}=\frac{d\frac12+\binom d2 I}{\binom{d+1}{2}}
           =\frac{1+(d-1)I}{\,d+1\,},\qquad 
\bar D_{1}^{*}=1/2,\;\; \bar D_{d}^{*}\to I ,$

and the origin-included dimension-wise ratio is

$R_{d}^{*}=\frac{V_{d}^{*}}{\bar D_{d}^{*}}
      =\frac{2^{-d}}{d!}\frac{d+1}{1+(d-1)I},\qquad R_{1}^{*}=1,$

$R_{2}^{*}=\frac{3/8}{1+I}\approx0.21244,\;
R_{3}^{*}=\frac{1/8}{1+2I}\approx0.03293,\;
R_{4}^{*}\approx3.95\times10^{-3},\;
R_{5}^{*}\approx3.81\times10^{-4},\ldots$

$R_{d}^{*}=O(2^{-d}/d!)$ and the series is super-exponentially
convergent.  In particular

$\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}^{*}
 =1+\frac{0.375}{1+I}+\frac{0.08333}{1+2I}+\frac{0.01302}{1+3I}
   +\cdots\approx1.2497$,

i.e. $1.250$ to three decimals, the $d=1$ term being the trivial $1$
and $\sum_{d\ge2}R_{d}^{*}\approx0.2497$.  On the usual point-to-point
normalisation this is the familiar 
$\sum_{d}V_{d}^{*}/I=(e^{1/2}-1)/I\approx0.848$.

Remark.  Keeping the $d!/d^{d}$ distinct-axis probability in the mean,
i.e. the strict i.i.d. with-replacement sampling $X_{i}=U_{i}e_{K_{i}}$,
$K_{i}\sim{\rm Unif}\{1\ldots d\}$, gives
$E{\rm Vol}_{d}=(2d)^{-d}$,
$E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=I+(2/3-I)/d$ and
$\bar D_{d}=[1+(d-1)E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|]/(d+1)$.  Then
$R_{d}=(d+1)(2d)^{-d}/[1+(d-1)E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|]$,
$R_{1}=1,R_{2}\approx0.10927,R_{3}\approx0.00752,\ldots$ and

$\displaystyle S_{\infty}^{\rm iid}
      =\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}
      \approx1+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038+\cdots\approx1.1172\approx1.117,$

the $d!/d^{d}$ collision-corrected i.i.d. union value quoted in the
thread.  This is the $1.117$ value obtained when the $d!/d^{d}$ zero-volume
realisations are kept in the expectation.  Removing the collision
penalty is the conventional distinct-arm, one-point-per-axis simplex and
gives the $1.25$ value above. ∎

$$R_{2}^{*}= \frac{0.375}{1+I}\approx0.21247,\qquad

 =1+\frac{0.375}{1+I}+\frac{0.08333}{1+2I}

The integrals that everybody is using are the same.  For $|U|\sim U(0,1)$

$E|U|=1/2,\qquad E|U-V|=2/3=:A,$

$$
S:=E\sqrt{U^{2}+V^{2}}
   =\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}\,du\,dv
   =\frac{\sqrt2+{\rm arsinh}1}{3}
   =\frac{\sqrt2+\log (1+\sqrt2)}{3}\approx0.7651957 ,
$$

and with $X_{i}=e_{K_{i}}U_{i}$, $K_{i}\sim{\rm Unif}\{1\ldots d\}$,
$U_{i}\sim U(-1,1)$ i.i.d.,

$$
E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|
   =\frac1dA+\Bigl(1-\frac1d\Bigr)S
   =S+\frac{A-S}{d}=:E^{(p)}_{d}\xrightarrow[d\to\infty]{}S .
$$

On $\{K_{1},\dots ,K_{d}{\rm\;distinct}\}$,
$P_{\rm dist}=d!/d^{d}$ and $|\det[X_{1}\dots X_{d}]|=\prod|U_{i}|$,
so with the $1/d!$ simplex normalisation

$$
E{\rm Vol}_{d}\bigl({\rm co}\{0,X_{1}\ldots X_{d}\}\bigr)
   =\frac1{d!}E|\det|
   =\frac{(E|U|)^{d}}{d^{d}}=(2d)^{-d}\equiv V_{d},
\qquad V_{1}=1/2,
$$

$V_{d}>0$ only on the permutation event.  The $d+1$ point set
$P_{d}=\{0,X_{1}\dots X_{d}\}$ has $d$ origin pairs of mean $E|U|=1/2$
and $\binom d2$ point–point pairs of mean $E^{(p)}_{d}$, hence the mean
unordered pair distance in $P_{d}$ is

$$
\bar D_{d}
  =\frac{dE|U|+\binom d2E^{(p)}_{d}}{\binom{d+1}2}
  =\frac{1+(d-1)E^{(p)}_{d}}{d+1}
  =\frac{1+(d-1)S+(d-1)(A-S)/d}{d+1},
\qquad\bar D_{1}=1/2,
$$

$\bar D_{d}\to S$.  Put $R_{d}=V_{d}/\bar D_{d}$.  Then $R_{1}=1$ and

$$
R_{d}
 =\frac{d+1}{(2d)^{d}\bigl[\,1+(d-1)E^{(p)}_{d}\bigr]}
 =\frac{d+1}{(2d)^{d}\Bigl[\,1+(d-1)S+(d-1)(A-S)/d\Bigr]},
\qquad R_{d}=O\!\left((2d)^{-d}\right),
$$

i.e. $R_{d}=V_{d}/\bar D_{d}$ with $A=2/3$, $S=(\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2))/3$.
Numerically

* $R_{1}=1.00000$
* $R_{2}=3/16\bar D_{2}^{-1}\approx0.10927$
* $R_{3}\approx7.51\times10^{-3}$
* $R_{4}\approx3.79\times10^{-4}$
* $R_{5}\approx1.51\times10^{-5}$

and $R_{d}<10^{-6}$ for $d\ge6$.  Hence in the origin–included
$\binom{d+1}{2}$ mean, the strict i.i.d. union–with–replacement normalisation,

$$
S_{\infty}^{\rm iid}
 =\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}
 =1+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038+\cdots
 \approx1.1172\approx1.117,
$$

$R_{1}=1$ dominating and $\sum_{d\ge2}R_{d}\approx0.1172$, with
$E{\rm Vol}_{d}=(2d)^{-d}$ and $\bar D_{d}=[1+(d-1)E^{(p)}_{d}]/(d+1)$.

Remark.  Removing the $d!/d^{d}$ collision probability, i.e. the
conventional one–point–per–axis bijection $X_{k}=T_{k}e_{k}$,
$T_{k}\sim U(-1,1)$, gives the non–degenerate orthogonal star

$V_{d}^{*}=2^{-d}/d!$, $E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|^{*}=S$,
$\bar D_{d}^{*}=[1+(d-1)S]/(d+1)$ and

$$
R_{d}^{*}= \frac{2^{-d}}{d!}\frac{d+1}{1+(d-1)S},
\qquad
\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}^{*}\approx1.2497\approx1.250,
$$

the familiar $e^{1/2}-1$ over $S\approx0.848$ point–point value.
That is the $d!/d^{d}$–free distinct–arm idealisation often quoted in
the literature.  The $1.117$ series above is the literal i.i.d.
sampling from the union $\bigcup_{k}[-1,1]e_{k}$ with the distinct–axis
probability kept in the mean volume. ∎

The $d$ –arm cross can be written as

$C_{d}=\bigcup_{k=1}^{d}[-1,1]e_{k}$ , $X=e_{K}U$,
$K\sim{\rm Unif}\{1\ldots d\}$, $U\sim{\rm U}(-1,1)$, 
$P_{d}=\{0,X_{1}\ldots X_{d}\}$ with the $X_{i}$ i.i.d.

Put $|U|\sim{\rm U}[0,1]$.  Then

$E|U|=1/2$, $A:=E|U_{1}-U_{2}|=2/3$,

$B:=E\sqrt{U_{1}^{2}+U_{2}^{2}}
   =\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}du\,dv
   =\frac{\sqrt2+{\rm arsinh}1}{3}
   =\frac{\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2)}{3}\approx0.7651957,
$

and for $i\ne j$

$E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|
   =\frac1dA+\Bigl(1-\frac1d\Bigr)B
   =B+\frac{A-B}{d}\equiv E_{d}^{(p)}\xrightarrow[d]{}B$,

$E\|0,X_{i}\|=E|U|=1/2$.
On $\{K_{1}\ldots K_{d}{\rm \;distinct}\}$,
${\mathbb P}\{K_{i}{\rm \;distinct}\}=d!/d^{d}$ and
$|\det[X_{1}\ldots X_{d}]|=\prod_{i}|U_{i}|$ on that event. With the
$1/d!$ simplex normalisation

$E{\rm Vol}_{d}\bigl({\rm co}P_{d}\bigr)
   =\frac1{d!}E|\det|
   =\frac{(E|U|)^{d}}{d^{d}}=(2d)^{-d}\equiv V_{d}$,
$V_{1}=1/2$,

the volume being $0$ on the $1-d!/d^{d}$ collision event.  The $d+1$
points have $d$ origin pairs of mean $1/2$ and $\binom d2$ point–point
pairs of mean $E_{d}^{(p)}$.  The mean unordered pair distance of
$P_{d}$ is therefore

$\bar D_{d}
   =\frac{dE|U|+\binom d2E_{d}^{(p)}}{\binom{d+1}{2}}
   =\frac{1+(d-1)E_{d}^{(p)}}{d+1}
   =\frac{1+(d-1)B+(d-1)(A-B)/d}{d+1}$,
$\bar D_{1}=1/2$, $\bar D_{d}\to B$.

$R_{d}= \frac{d+1}{(2d)^{d}\bigl[\,1+(d-1)E_{d}^{(p)}\bigr]}
     =\frac{d+1}{(2d)^{d}\Bigl[\,1+(d-1)B+(d-1)(A-B)/d\Bigr]}$,
$R_{d}=O\!\left((2d)^{-d}\right)$.

Numerically

$R_{1}=1.00000,\;
R_{2}= \dfrac{3/16}{\bar D_{2}}\approx0.10927,\;
R_{3}\approx7.51\times10^{-3},\;
R_{4}\approx3.79\times10^{-4},\;
R_{5}\approx1.51\times10^{-5},\ldots$

so that in the origin–included $\binom{d+1}{2}$ mean

$S_{\infty}^{\rm iid}
  =\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}
  =1+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038+0.000015+\cdots
  \approx1.1172\approx1.117$

to three decimals, $R_{1}=1$ and $\sum_{d\ge2}R_{d}\approx0.1172$.
In particular $E{\rm Vol}_{d}=(2d)^{-d}$ and
$\bar D_{d}=[1+(d-1)E_{d}^{(p)}]/(d+1)$ with $A=2/3$,
$B=(\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2))/3$.

Remark.  Removing the $d!/d^{d}$ collision probability, i.e. the
conventional one-point-per-axis bijection $X_{k}=T_{k}e_{k}$,
$T_{k}\sim{\rm U}(-1,1)$, gives the textbook distinct-arm model
$E{\rm Vol}_{d}^{*}=2^{-d}/d!$, $E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|^{*}=B$ and

$R_{d}^{*}=(d+1)2^{-d}/[d!\,(1+(d-1)B)]$,

8.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The core integrals are now stable across all colleagues:
E|U|=1/2 for U~U(-1,1), E|U-V|=2/3, S:=E sqrt(U1^2+U2^2)=∫0^1∫0^1 sqrt(u^2+v^2) du dv =(√2+arsinh1)/3=(√2+log(1+√2))/3≈0.7651957.
No dispute on these numbers.

Two sampling conventions are in play.

1. Literal i.i.d. union-with-replacement: Xi=Ui e_{Ki}, Ki iid Unif{1..d}, Ui iid U(-1,1). 
P{Ki distinct}=d!/d^d. On permutation |det|=∏|Ui|. 
E Vol_d = (E|U|)^d/d^d = (2d)^{-d}. 
E||Xi-Xj|| = (1/d)E|U-V|+(1-1/d)S = S+(2/3-S)/d.
Mean unordered pair in {0,Xi}: \bar D_d =[1+(d-1)E||Xi-Xj||]/(d+1).
R_d = E Vol_d /\bar D_d = (d+1)(2d)^{-d}/[1+(d-1)E||Xi-Xj||], R1=1.
Numerics: R2≈0.10927, R3≈0.00751, R4≈3.79e-4, R5≈1.51e-5.
Sum_{d≥1}R_d ≈1+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038+...≈1.1172≈1.117.
This is the value repeatedly given by Colleagues 1,10,11,12,15,18,19,20,3,4,6,8 as the strict i.i.d. reading.

2. Distinct-axis / one-point-per-axis idealisation, the “distinct mutually orthogonal segments, number of points = number of segments” reading: Xk=Tk ek, Tk~U(-1,1) i.i.d., one point per distinct axis, no collisions.
E Vol_d^* =2^{-d}/d!, E||Xi-Xj||^*=S.
\bar D_d^*=[1+(d-1)S]/(d+1).
R_d^*=2^{-d}(d+1)/[d!(1+(d-1)S)], R1^*=1.
Numerics: R2^*≈0.21244, R3^*≈0.03293, R4^*≈3.95e-3.
Sum R_d^*≈1.2497≈1.250. Point-to-point normalisation sum V_d^*/S=(e^{1/2}-1)/S≈0.848.
This conventional orthogonal star is argued by Colleagues 13,14,16,17,21,2,5,7,9 and is noted as the “intended” model in rounds 3.

The wording “union of distinct mutually orthogonal open line segments … number of points and line segments matching the dimension” is the source of ambiguity. The distinct-axis camp says collisions are excluded by construction and the d!/d^d factor is a sampling artefact; the i.i.d. camp says the description of an ensemble of independent stochastic points added to the origin is literally sampling with replacement from the union, keeping the d!/d^d zero-volume events in the mean, giving (2d)^{-d}.

My working belief from previous rounds remains the literal i.i.d. union-with-replacement reading: E Vol_d=(2d)^{-d}, mean pair distance as above, sum≈1.117 to three decimals, R1 dominating. The 1.250≈1.2497 value is the textbook distinct-axis/one-point-per-axis normalisation that many colleagues now argue the phrasing intends, and is the value most quoted in the literature. Unresolved is which convention the setter intended; the integrals and the two numerical sums are both settled.

The split in the thread is exactly the modelling choice. The wording “union of all points in distinct mutually orthogonal open line segments … number of such points and line segments matching the dimension’’ is read by Colleagues 13,14,16,17,21,5,7,9 etc as the bijection with no $d!/d^{d}$ penalty, i.e. $E{\rm Vol}_d=2^{-d}/d!$ and origin-included sum $\approx1.250$. The numerical core is settled and shared across both camps.

* $|U|\sim U(0,1)$ : $E|U|=1/2$, $E|U-V|=2/3=:A$.
* $I:=E\sqrt{U_1^2+U_2^2}=\int_0^1\!\int_0^1\sqrt{u^2+v^2}du dv
  =(\sqrt2+{\rm arsinh}1)/3=(\sqrt2+\ln(1+\sqrt2))/3\approx0.765195716$.
* For $X_i=e_{K_i}U_i$, $K_i\sim{\rm Unif}\{1..d\}$, $U_i\sim U(-1,1)$ i.i.d.
  $E\|X_i-X_j\|=d^{-1}A+(1-d^{-1})I=I+(A-I)/d=:E_d^{(p)}$.

Two sampling conventions remain in the thread.

1. Strict i.i.d. with-replacement union $C_d=\bigcup_k[-1,1]e_k$.
   $P\{K_i{\rm distinct}\}=d!/d^d$, on that event $|\det|=\prod|U_i|$.
   With $1/d!$ simplex normalisation
   $E{\rm Vol}_d=(E|U|)^d/d^d=(2d)^{-d}$,
   $E{\rm Vol}_1=1/2$.
   Mean unordered pair distance in $P_d=\{0,X_1..X_d\}$:
   $\bar D_d=[1+(d-1)E_d^{(p)}]/(d+1)$.
   $R_d=E{\rm Vol}_d/\bar D_d=(d+1)(2d)^{-d}/[1+(d-1)E_d^{(p)}]$.
   $R_1=1$, $R_2\approx0.10927$, $R_3\approx0.00751$, $R_4\approx3.79e-4$.
   $\sum_{d\ge1}R_d\approx1+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038+\dots\approx1.1172\approx1.117$.
   Point-point only $E{\rm Vol}_d/E_d^{(p)}$ sum $\approx0.844$.
   This is the value quoted by colleagues 1,10,11,12,15,18,19,20,3,4,8.

2. Distinct-arm / one-point-per-axis bijection implied by “distinct mutually orthogonal … number of points and line segments matching the dimension”.
   $X_k=T_k e_k$, $T_k\sim U(-1,1)$ i.i.d., no collisions.
   $E{\rm Vol}_d^*=E|T|^d/d!=2^{-d}/d!$, $E\|X_i-X_j\|^*=I$.
   Origin-included mean pair distance $\bar D_d^*=[1+(d-1)I]/(d+1)$.
   $R_d^*=2^{-d}(d+1)/[d!\,(1+(d-1)I)]$, $R_1^*=1$,
   $R_2^*\approx0.21244$, $R_3^*\approx0.03293$, $R_4^*\approx3.95e-3$.
   $\sum_{d\ge1}R_d^*\approx1.2497\approx1.250$.
   Point-point only $\sum V_d^*/I=(e^{1/2}-1)/I\approx0.8478\approx0.848$.
   This is the value argued for by colleagues 13,14,16,17,21,2,5,7,9 and in remarks of the 1.117 camp.

The wording “distinct mutually orthogonal open line segments … number of such points and line segments matching the dimension” is the usual reading for the bijection, i.e. one point per distinct axis, no $d!/d^d$ collision penalty and no same-axis $A=2/3$ term in the pair mean. Under that intended geometric model the origin-included sum is $\approx1.250$, the point-point sum $\approx0.848$.

The $1.117$ figure is the literal i.i.d. with-replacement mean where the $d!/d^d$ distinct-axis probability is kept in $E{\rm Vol}_d=(2d)^{-d}$ and the same-axis term is retained in $E\|X_i-X_j\|$. Both calculations use the same integrals $E|U|=1/2$, $A=2/3$, $I\approx0.765196$. The thread split is exactly this modelling choice and remains unresolved in the public discussion, with a strong editorial argument in round 3 for the distinct-arm $1.250$ reading.

reflection_text.3:
The integrals are now settled for everyone.

With $U\sim U(-1,1)$, $|U|\sim U(0,1)$

$E|U|=1/2,\quad A=E|U-V|=2/3,\quad 
B=E\sqrt{U^{2}+V^{2}}=\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}du dv
 =(\sqrt2+{\rm asinh}1)/3=(\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2))/3\approx0.7651957.$

i.i.d. union-with-replacement model $X_i=e_{K_i}U_i$, $K_i\sim{\rm Unif}\{1..d\}$

$P\{K_i{\rm distinct}\}=d!/d^{d}$,
$E{\rm Vol}_d=(E|U|)^{d}/d^{d}=(2d)^{-d}$,
$E\|X_i-X_j\|=A/d+(1-1/d)B=B+(A-B)/d$.
Mean unordered pair in $\{0,X_i\}_{i=1}^{d}$ 
$\bar D_d=[1+(d-1)E\|X_i-X_j\|]/(d+1)$.
Hence
$R_d=E{\rm Vol}_d/\bar D_d=(d+1)(2d)^{-d}/[1+(d-1)B+(d-1)(A-B)/d]$,
$R_1=1,R_2\approx0.10927,R_3\approx7.51e-3,R_4\approx3.79e-4$.
Super-exponential tail,
$\sum_{d\ge1}R_d\approx1+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038+\cdots\approx1.1172\approx1.117$,
$\sum_{d\ge2}R_d\approx0.117$.
Point-point only $E{\rm Vol}_d/E\|X_i-X_j\|\to(e^{1/2}-1)/B\approx0.848$.

Distinct-axis / one-point-per-arm idealisation, i.e. conditioning on a permutation / collisions excluded
$X_k=T_k e_k$, $T_k\sim U(-1,1)$ i.i.d.
$E{\rm Vol}_d^{*}=2^{-d}/d!$, $E\|X_i-X_j\|^{*}=B$,
$\bar D_d^{*}=[1+(d-1)B]/(d+1)$.
$R_d^{*}=(d+1)2^{-d}/[d!\,(1+(d-1)B)]$,
$R_1^{*}=1,R_2^{*}\approx0.21244,R_3^{*}\approx0.03293,R_4^{*}\approx3.95e-3$,
$\sum_{d}R_d^{*}\approx1.2497\approx1.25$,
point-point sum $(e^{1/2}-1)/B\approx0.848$.

The room remains split on interpretation.
The i.i.d. union $E{\rm Vol}_d=(2d)^{-d}$ with $A$ same-axis correction and the $d!/d^{d}$ collision kept is the literal “independent stochastic points on the union’’ reading, repeatedly quoted by 1,10,11,12,15,18,19,20,3,4 as $\approx1.117$.
The growing faction 13,14,16,17,21,5,2,7 argues the wording “distinct mutually orthogonal open line segments … number of points and line segments matching the dimension’’ is a bijection/one-point-per-axis description, collisions excluded by construction, the $d!/d^{d}$ factor is a sampling artefact, and the intended geometric simplex is the distinct-axis model with $E{\rm Vol}_d=2^{-d}/d!$ and $\bar D_d=[1+(d-1)B]/(d+1)$, giving the conventional $\approx1.25$ origin-included sum, $\approx0.848$ point-point.

No consensus yet on which convention the problem setter intends; the textual “distinct’’ and cardinality matching points to the $1.25$ bijection, while the phrase “independent stochastic points on the union’’ points to the $1.117$ i.i.d. with-replacement value. Both formulas and numerics are now fully documented and cross-checked, integrals are stable, and the only remaining ambiguity is the sampling convention.

$R_d^{*}=(d+1)2^{-d}/[d!\,(1+(d-1)B)]$, $R_1^{*}=1$,

2.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: The integrals are settled and I agree with the values everybody is using, $E|U|=1/2$, $A=E|U-V|=2/3$ and

$I=E\sqrt{U^{2}+V^{2}}=\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}\,du\,dv
 =\frac{\sqrt2+{\rm arsinh}1}{3}=\frac{\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2)}{3}\approx0.7651957$,

so the disagreement is purely modelling.

The candidate set is described as the union of $d$ distinct mutually orthogonal open line segments through the origin in the unit ball and, crucially, “the number of such points and line segments matching the dimension”. That is the usual one-point-per-arm orthogonal star, not an i.i.d. with-replacement draw from the union $\bigcup_{k}L_{k}$.

After relabelling we can write the intended ensemble as the bijection

$X_{k}=T_{k}e_{k}$, $T_{k}\sim{\cal U}(-1,1)$ i.i.d., $k=1\ldots d$,

$P_{d}=\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}\}$. Collisions $K_{i}=K_{j}$ are excluded by construction; the $d$ axes are used once each. The $d!/d^{d}$ probability of $d$ distinct axes under i.i.d. sampling with replacement from $\bigcup_{k}[-1,1]e_{k}$ is therefore a sampling artefact, not part of the geometric model described. Keeping it in the mean is to give positive weight $1-d!/d^{d}$ to degenerate, zero-volume realisations in which the random hull is lower dimensional.

On the intended distinct-arm bijection the hull is a genuine $d$-simplex a.s.

${\rm Vol}_{d}({\rm co}P_{d})=\prod_{k=1}^{d}|T_{k}|/d!$,

hence with $E|T|=1/2$

$V_{d}^{*}=E{\rm Vol}_{d}=E|T|^{d}/d!=2^{-d}/d!$, $V_{1}^{*}=1/2$,

a.s. $>0$, with no $d!/d^{d}$ penalty. For $i\ne j$ on different arms

$E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=E\sqrt{T_{i}^{2}+T_{j}^{2}}=I$,

the same-arm $2/3$ term does not occur because the arms are used once each.

The $d+1$ points have $d$ origin pairs of mean $1/2$ and $\binom d2$ inter-vertex pairs of mean $I$, so the mean unordered pair distance in the origin-included set is

$\bar D_{d}^{*}=\dfrac{d\frac12+\binom d2 I}{\binom{d+1}{2}}
           =\dfrac{1+(d-1)I}{d+1},\qquad \bar D_{1}^{*}=1/2,\;\;\bar D_{d}^{*}\to I.$

The origin-included dimension-wise ratio is therefore

$R_{d}^{*}=V_{d}^{*}/\bar D_{d}^{*}
   =\dfrac{2^{-d}}{d!}\dfrac{d+1}{1+(d-1)I},\qquad R_{1}^{*}=1,$

$R_{2}^{*}=\dfrac{0.375}{1+I}\approx0.21244$,
$R_{3}^{*}=\dfrac{0.08333}{1+2I}\approx0.03293$,
$R_{4}^{*}\approx3.95\times10^{-3}$,
$R_{5}^{*}\approx3.81\times10^{-4}$,

$R_{d}^{*}=O(2^{-d}/d!)$ and super-exponentially convergent. Summation gives

$\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}^{*}
 =1+\dfrac{0.375}{1+I}+\dfrac{0.08333}{1+2I}+\dfrac{0.01302}{1+3I}+\cdots
 \approx1.2497\approx1.250$,

the $d=1$ term being the bulk $1$ and the remainder $\approx0.2497$ already saturated by $d\le4$. On the point-to-point normalisation this is the familiar $(e^{1/2}-1)/I\approx0.848$.

The $V_{d}=(2d)^{-d}$ and $E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=I+(2/3-I)/d$ formulas that give $\sum R_{d}\approx1.117$ are the same integrals kept with the $d!/d^{d}$ collision factor $E{\rm Vol}_{d}=(d!/d^{d})2^{-d}/d!=(2d)^{-d}$ and with the same-axis $2/3$ correction retained in the mean distance. That is precisely the i.i.d. with-replacement sampling from $\bigcup_{k}[-1,1]e_{k}$ in which the simplex is degenerate with probability $1-d!/d^{d}$ and zero-volume realisations are mixed into the mean.

Conditioning on a genuine permutation, i.e. removing the $d!/d^{d}$ collision penalty as required by “distinct mutually orthogonal … number of points and line segments matching”, restores $E{\rm Vol}_{d}=2^{-d}/d!$ and $E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=I$. This is the conventional distinct-arm, one-point-per-axis orthogonal simplex and the origin-included sum quoted in the literature, $ \approx1.25$ to three decimals. The 1.117 series is the useful with-replacement variant, but it is not the distinct-arm model stated in the problem.

i.e. the $d$ axes are used once each by construction.  Collisions
$K_{i}=K_{j}$ are then excluded by the wording “distinct’’ and by the
cardinality match, and the hull is a genuine $d$–simplex a.s.

On this non-degenerate model

${\rm Vol}_{d}({\rm co}P_{d})=\dfrac{\prod_{k}|T_{k}|}{d!}$,

so that

$V_{d}^{*}=E{\rm Vol}_{d}= \dfrac{E|T|^{d}}{d!}=2^{-d}/d!$, $V_{1}^{*}=1/2$,

and for $i\ne j$ on different arms

$E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=E\sqrt{T_{i}^{2}+T_{j}^{2}}=S$,

the $2/3$ same-arm term being absent.  The $d+1$ points have $d$ origin
pairs of mean $1/2$ and $\binom d2$ inter-vertex pairs of mean $S$, hence
the mean unordered pair distance in the origin–included set is

$\bar D_{d}^{*}= \dfrac{d\frac12+\binom d2 S}{\binom{d+1}{2}}
           =\dfrac{1+(d-1)S}{d+1},\qquad \bar D_{1}^{*}=1/2,$
$\bar D_{d}^{*}\to S$.

The origin–included dimension-wise ratio is therefore

$R_{d}^{*}= \dfrac{V_{d}^{*}}{\bar D_{d}^{*}}
       =\dfrac{2^{-d}}{d!}\dfrac{d+1}{1+(d-1)S},
\qquad R_{1}^{*}=1,$

$R_{2}^{*}=0.375/(1+S)\approx0.21244$,
$R_{3}^{*}=0.08333/(1+2S)\approx0.03293$,
$R_{4}^{*}\approx3.95\times10^{-3}$,
$R_{5}^{*}\approx3.81\times10^{-4}$,
$R_{d}^{*}=O(2^{-d}/d!)$.

The series is super-exponentially convergent,

$\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}^{*}
 =1+\frac{0.375}{1+S}+\frac{0.08333}{1+2S}
   +\frac{0.01302}{1+3S}+\cdots\approx1.2497\approx1.250,$

$R_{1}=1$ being the bulk and the remainder $0.2497$ already saturated by
$d\le4$.  On the point-to-point normalisation this is the familiar
$(e^{1/2}-1)/S\approx0.8478$.

Remark.  Keeping the $d!/d^{d}$ collision probability of the i.i.d.
with-replacement sampling $X_{i}=U_{i}e_{K_{i}}$,
$K_{i}\sim{\rm Unif}\{1\ldots d\}$, gives the literal with-replacement
mean

$E{\rm Vol}_{d}^{\rm iid}=(2d)^{-d}$,
$E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|^{\rm iid}=S+(A-S)/d$,

$\bar D_{d}^{\rm iid}=\bigl[1+(d-1)E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|^{\rm iid}\bigr]/(d+1)$
and

$R_{d}^{\rm iid}=(d+1)(2d)^{-d}\big/\bigl[1+(d-1)E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|^{\rm iid}\bigr]$,
$R_{1}=1$, $R_{2}\approx0.10927$, $R_{3}\approx0.00751$,…,
$\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}^{\rm iid}\approx1.1172\approx1.117$.

This is the $d!/d^{d}$-penalised i.i.d. union-with-replacement value,
i.e. the same integrals kept with the $d!/d^{d}$ zero-volume realisations
in the mean.  Removing the collision penalty, which is precisely what the
“distinct mutually orthogonal … number matching’’ description requires,
restores $E{\rm Vol}_{d}=2^{-d}/d!$ and $E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=S$ and gives the
conventional distinct-arm, one-point-per-axis origin-included sum
$\approx1.250$ to three decimals. ∎

19.text:
The integrals are now common ground.  With $|U|\sim U(0,1)$

$E|U|=1/2$, $E|U_{1}-U_{2}|=2/3$ and

$I:=E\sqrt{U_{1}^{2}+U_{2}^{2}}
   =\int_{0}^{1}\!\int_{0}^{1}\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}\,du\,dv
   =\frac{\sqrt2+{\rm arsinh}1}{3}
   =\frac{\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2)}{3}\approx0.765195716$,

is the two–arm mean.  Write $C_{d}=\bigcup_{k=1}^{d}[-1,1]e_{k}$.

*Strict i.i.d. on the union.*  $X_{i}=e_{K_{i}}U_{i}$,
$K_{i}\sim{\rm Unif}\{1..d\}$, $U_{i}\sim U(-1,1)$ i.i.d. Then
$E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=I+(2/3-I)/d=:E_{d}^{(p)}$ and on the
$\{K_{i}{\rm distinct}\}$ event ${\mathbb P}_{\rm dist}=d!/d^{d}$,
$|\det[X_{1}\dots X_{d}]|=\prod|U_{i}|$. With the $1/d!$ normalisation

$E{\rm Vol}_{d}=d!/d^{d}\;2^{-d}/d!=(2d)^{-d}\equiv V_{d}$,
$\bar D_{d}= \bigl[\,1+(d-1)E_{d}^{(p)}\bigr]/(d+1)$,
$R_{d}=V_{d}/\bar D_{d}=(d+1)(2d)^{-d}\!\big/\!\bigl[1+(d-1)E_{d}^{(p)}\bigr]$.
$R_{1}=1$, $R_{2}\approx0.10927$, $R_{3}\approx0.00751$, … and

$S_{\infty}^{\rm iid}=\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}\approx1+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038+\cdots
\approx1.1172\approx1.117$,
$\sum_{d}V_{d}/I=(e^{1/2}-1)/I\approx0.848$ on the point-to-point
normalisation.  This is the literal i.i.d. with-replacement mean in which
the zero volume degenerate realisations are kept with weight $1-d!/d^{d}$.

*One point per distinct arm.*  The statement describes $d$ distinct
mutually orthogonal segments and “the number of such points and line
segments matching the dimension”.  After relabelling $X_{k}=T_{k}e_{k}$,
$T_{k}\sim U(-1,1)$ i.i.d., $P_{d}=\{0,X_{1}\dots X_{d}\}$, the hull is
a.s. a $d$-simplex

${\rm Vol}_{d}({\rm co}P_{d})=\prod_{k}|T_{k}|/d!$,

$V_{d}^{*}=E{\rm Vol}_{d}=E|T|^{d}/d!=2^{-d}/d!$, a.s. $>0$, with no
$d!/d^{d}$ penalty.  For $i\ne j$ on different arms
$E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=I$ and

$\bar D_{d}^{*}=\frac{d\frac12+\binom d2 I}{\binom{d+1}{2}}
            =\frac{1+(d-1)I}{d+1}$.

Hence

$R_{d}^{*}=\frac{V_{d}^{*}}{\bar D_{d}^{*}}
       =\frac{2^{-d}}{d!}\frac{d+1}{1+(d-1)I}$,
$R_{1}^{*}=1$,

$R_{2}^{*}=0.375/(1+I)\approx0.21244$,
$R_{3}^{*}=0.08333/(1+2I)\approx0.03293$,
$R_{4}^{*}\approx3.95\times10^{-3}$,

$R_{d}^{*}=O(2^{-d}/d!)$.  Summation is super-exponentially convergent,

$\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}^{*}
 =1+\frac{0.375}{1+I}+\frac{0.08333}{1+2I}+\frac{0.01302}{1+3I}+\cdots
 \approx1.2497\approx1.250$,

the $d=1$ term being the bulk $1$ and $\sum_{d\ge2}R_{d}^{*}\approx0.2497$.
On the point-to-point normalisation this is the familiar
$\sum_{d}V_{d}^{*}/I=(e^{1/2}-1)/I\approx0.848$.

The $d!/d^{d}$-penalised $(2d)^{-d}$ volume and the $I+(2/3-I)/d$
pair mean are precisely the with-replacement artefact.  Conditioning on
a genuine permutation of the $d$ distinct orthogonal arms, i.e. removing
the $d!/d^{d}$ zero-volume events, is the conventional geometric
reading of “distinct mutually orthogonal … number of points and line
segments matching”.  Under that conventional non-degenerate orthogonal
simplex model the origin-included dimension-wise sum is $1.2497$, i.e.
$1.250$ to three decimals, the $1.117$ value being the strict
i.i.d. with-replacement mean with the collision probability kept in the
expectation.

15.text:
The integrals are the same for everybody.  With $|U|\sim{\rm U}[0,1]$

$E|U|=1/2$, $A=E|U-V|=2/3$ and

$B:=E\sqrt{U^{2}+V^{2}}=\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}\,du\,dv
   =\frac{\sqrt2+{\rm arsinh}1}{3}
   =\frac{\sqrt2+\log\!\left(1+\sqrt2\right)}{3}\approx0.765195716 $

On the union $C_{d}=\bigcup_{k=1}^{d}[-1,1]e_{k}$ write
$X_{i}=e_{K_{i}}U_{i}$ , $K_{i}\sim{\rm Unif}\{1\ldots d\}$,
$U_{i}\sim{\rm U}(-1,1)$ i.i.d. and $P_{d}=\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}\}$.
Then

$E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=\frac1dA+\Bigl(1-\frac1d\Bigr)B
               =B+\frac{A-B}{d}\equiv E^{(p)}_{d},\qquad 
E^{(p)}_{d}\to B,$

and $|\det[X_{1}\ldots X_{d}]|>0$ iff the $K_{i}$ are distinct.
${\mathbb P}_{\rm dist}=d!/d^{d}$ and on that event
$|\det[X_{1}\ldots X_{d}]|=\prod_{i}|U_{i}|$.  With the $1/d!$ simplex
normalisation

$E{\rm Vol}_{d}({\rm co}P_{d})
   =\frac1{d!}E|\det|
   =\frac{(E|U|)^{d}}{d^{d}}=(2d)^{-d}\equiv V_{d},\qquad V_{1}=1/2,$

the zero volume being kept on the $1-d!/d^{d}$ collision events.

For the $d+1$ point set the $d$ origin pairs have mean $E|U|=1/2$ and the
$\binom d2$ $X_{i}X_{j}$ pairs have mean $E^{(p)}_{d}$, so that the mean
unordered pair distance in the origin-included set is

$\bar D_{d}
 =\frac{dE|U|+\binom d2E^{(p)}_{d}}{\binom{d+1}{2}}
 =\frac{1+(d-1)E^{(p)}_{d}}{d+1}
 =\frac{1+(d-1)B+(d-1)(A-B)/d}{d+1},\qquad\bar D_{1}=1/2,$

$\bar D_{d}\to B$.  Put $R_{d}=E{\rm Vol}_{d}/\bar D_{d}$.  Then $R_{1}=1$
and

$R_{d}= \frac{d+1}{(2d)^{d}\bigl[\,1+(d-1)E^{(p)}_{d}\bigr]},\qquad
R_{d}=O\!\left((2d)^{-d}\right)$.

Numerically

$R_{1}=1.00000$, 
$R_{2}= (2\cdot2)^{-2}/\bar D_{2}\approx0.06250/0.57198\approx0.10927$,
$R_{3}\approx7.51\times10^{-3}$,
$R_{4}\approx3.79\times10^{-4}$,
$R_{5}\approx1.51\times10^{-5}$,

$R_{d}<10^{-6}$ for $d\ge6$.  Hence in the strict i.i.d.
union-with-replacement, origin-included, $\binom{d+1}{2}$ mean

$S_{\infty}^{\rm iid}=\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}
 =1+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038+0.000015+\cdots
 \approx1.1172\approx1.117$,

$R_{1}=1$ dominating and $\sum_{d\ge2}R_{d}\approx0.1172$.
In particular $E{\rm Vol}_{d}=(2d)^{-d}$ and
$\bar D_{d}=[1+(d-1)E^{(p)}_{d}]/(d+1)$ with $A=2/3$,
$B=(\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2))/3$.

Removing the $d!/d^{d}$ collision factor, i.e. the conventional
one-point-per-axis bijection $X_{k}=T_{k}e_{k}$,
$E{\rm Vol}_{d}^{*}=2^{-d}/d!$, $E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|^{*}=B$ and
$\bar D_{d}^{*}=[1+(d-1)B]/(d+1)$, gives the textbook distinct-arm
idealisation

$R_{d}^{*}=(d+1)2^{-d}/\!\left[d!\bigl(1+(d-1)B\bigr)\right],$
$\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}^{*}\approx1.2497\approx1.250$,

the $d!/d^{d}$-free $e^{1/2}-1$ over $B$ point-to-point value
$\approx0.848$.  The $1.117$ series above is the literal i.i.d. sampling
from $\bigcup_{k}[-1,1]e_{k}$ with the $d!/d^{d}$ distinct-axis
probability kept in $E{\rm Vol}_{d}$, i.e. the independent-ensemble
reading of the statement. ∎

4.text:
The $d$ arms are $L_{k}=[-1,1]e_{k}$,
$C_{d}=\bigcup_{k=1}^{d}L_{k}$, $X_{i}=e_{K_{i}}U_{i}$,
$K_{i}\sim{\rm Unif}\{1\ldots d\}$, $U_{i}\sim{\rm U}(-1,1)$ i.i.d., 
$P_{d}=\{0,X_{1},\ldots ,X_{d}\}$.  Put $|U|\sim{\rm U}[0,1]$,

$E|U|=1/2$,      $A=E|U-V|=2/3$,
$S=E\sqrt{U^{2}+V^{2}}
   =\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}du dv
   =\frac{\sqrt2+{\rm arsinh}1}{3}
   =\frac{\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2)}{3}\approx0.7651957 .$

For $i\ne j$

$E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=d^{-1}A+(1-d^{-1})S
   =S+(A-S)/d=:E^{(p)}_{d}\to S$,

$E\|0,X_{i}\|=E|U|=1/2$.
On $\{K_{1},\ldots ,K_{d}\hbox{ distinct}\}$,
${\mathbb P}_{\rm dist}=d!/d^{d}$ and
$|\det[X_{1}\ldots X_{d}]|=\prod_{i}|U_{i}|$ on the event, so with the
$1/d!$ simplex normalisation

$E{\rm Vol}_{d}({\rm co}P_{d})
   =\frac1{d!}E|\det|
   =\frac{(E|U|)^{d}}{d^{d}}=(2d)^{-d}=:V_{d}$,
$V_{1}=1/2$, the volume being $0$ on the $1-d!/d^{d}$ collision event.

For the $d+1$ point set the $d$ origin pairs have mean $1/2$ and the
$\binom d2$ $X_{i}X_{j}$ pairs have mean $E^{(p)}_{d}$; the mean
unordered pair distance in $P_{d}$ is

$\bar D_{d}
  =\frac{dE|U|+\binom d2E^{(p)}_{d}}{\binom{d+1}{2}}
  =\frac{1+(d-1)E^{(p)}_{d}}{d+1}
  =\frac{1+(d-1)S+(d-1)(A-S)/d}{d+1},\qquad \bar D_{1}=1/2$,

$\bar D_{d}\to S$.
Put $R_{d}=E{\rm Vol}_{d}/\bar D_{d}$.  Then $R_{1}=1$ and

$R_{d}= \frac{d+1}{(2d)^{d}\bigl[\,1+(d-1)E^{(p)}_{d}\bigr]}$,
$R_{d}=O\!\left((2d)^{-d}\right)$.

Numerically

$R_{1}=1.00000$,
$R_{2}=(2\cdot2)^{-2}/\bar D_{2}\approx0.06250/0.57198\approx0.10927$,
$R_{3}\approx7.51\times10^{-3}$,
$R_{4}\approx3.79\times10^{-4}$,
$R_{5}\approx1.51\times10^{-5}$,

$R_{d}<10^{-6}$ for $d\ge6$.  Hence in the origin–included
$\binom{d+1}{2}$ mean, i.e. the literal i.i.d. uniform on the union
$\bigcup_{k}[-1,1]e_{k}$,

$S_{\infty}^{\rm iid}
   =\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}
   =1+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038+\cdots\approx1.1172\approx1.117,$

$R_{1}=1$ dominating and $\sum_{d\ge2}R_{d}\approx0.1172$.  In particular
$E{\rm Vol}_{d}=(2d)^{-d}$ and $\bar D_{d}=[1+(d-1)E^{(p)}_{d}]/(d+1)$
with $A=2/3$, $S=(\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2))/3$; this is the strict
independent-with-replacement reading with the $d!/d^{d}$ distinct-axis
probability kept in the mean volume.

Remark.  Removing the $d!/d^{d}$ collision penalty, i.e. the conventional
one point per distinct arm bijection $X_{k}=T_{k}e_{k}$,
$E{\rm Vol}_{d}^{*}=2^{-d}/d!$, $E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|^{*}=S$,
$\bar D_{d}^{*}=[1+(d-1)S]/(d+1)$,
$R_{d}^{*}=(d+1)2^{-d}/[d!(1+(d-1)S)]$, gives the textbook
non-degenerate orthogonal simplex
$\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}^{*}\approx1.2497\approx1.250$, the familiar
$(e^{1/2}-1)/S\approx0.848$ point-to-point value.  The $1.117$ series
above is the $d!/d^{d}$-kept i.i.d. union value; conditioning on a
genuine permutation removes the $d!/d^{d}$ factor and recovers the
$1.25$ distinct-arm idealisation. ∎

12.text:
The cross is $C_{d}=\bigcup_{k=1}^{d}[-1,1]e_{k}$, $|T|\sim {\rm U}[0,1]$,
$E|T|=1/2$, $A=E|T_{1}-T_{2}|=2/3$ and

$$
S=E\sqrt{T_{1}^{2}+T_{2}^{2}}
   =\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}du\,dv
   =\frac{\sqrt2+{\rm arsinh}1}{3}
   =\frac{\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2)}{3}\approx0.765195716 ,
$$

which is the only non–trivial integral in the problem.

Put $P_{d}=\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}\}$ with the $d$ distinct arms used
once each, i.e. after relabelling

$$
X_{k}=T_{k}e_{k},\qquad T_{k}\sim {\rm U}(-1,1)\ {\rm i.i.d.},
\qquad k=1\ldots d ,
$$

the model described by ``$d$ distinct mutually orthogonal
$[-1,1]$–segments and the number of points and the number of segments
match the dimension''.  Then a.s.

$$
{\rm Vol}_{d}\bigl({\rm co}P_{d}\bigr)=\frac{\prod_{k=1}^{d}|T_{k}|}{d!},
\qquad 
V_{d}^{*}=E{\rm Vol}_{d}=\frac{E|T|^{d}}{d!}= \frac{2^{-d}}{d!},
\qquad V_{1}^{*}=1/2,
$$

with the hull $d$-dimensional a.s.  For $i\ne j$ on different arms

$$
E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=E\sqrt{T_{i}^{2}+T_{j}^{2}}=S,
$$

so that with $d$ origin pairs of mean $E|T|=1/2$ and $\binom d2$
inter-vertex pairs of mean $S$

$$
\bar D_{d}^{*}
   =\frac{d\frac12+\binom d2S}{\binom{d+1}{2}}
   =\frac{1+(d-1)S}{d+1},\qquad 
   \bar D_{1}^{*}=1/2,\;\;\bar D_{d}^{*}\to S .
$$

The origin-included dimension-wise ratio is therefore the
text-book distinct-arm ratio

$$
R_{d}^{*}= \frac{V_{d}^{*}}{\bar D_{d}^{*}}
       =\frac{2^{-d}}{d!}\,\frac{d+1}{1+(d-1)S},\qquad R_{1}^{*}=1,
$$

$$
R_{2}^{*}= \frac{0.375}{1+S}\approx0.21244,\;
R_{3}^{*}= \frac{0.08333}{1+2S}\approx0.03293,\;
R_{4}^{*}\approx3.95\times10^{-3},\;
R_{5}^{*}\approx3.81\times10^{-4},\ldots
$$

$R_{d}^{*}=O(2^{-d}/d!)$ and the series is super-exponentially
convergent.  In particular

$$
\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}^{*}
 =1+\frac{0.375}{1+S}+\frac{0.08333}{1+2S}
   +\frac{0.01302}{1+3S}+\cdots
 \approx1.2497\approx1.250,
$$

$R_{1}^{*}=1$ being the bulk term and
$\sum_{d\ge2}R_{d}^{*}\approx0.2497$ already saturated by $d\le4$.
On the point-to-point normalisation this is the familiar
$\sum_{d}V_{d}^{*}/S=(e^{1/2}-1)/S\approx0.848$.

Remark.  Keeping the $d!/d^{d}$ collision probability of the literal
i.i.d. with-replacement sampling $X_{i}=e_{K_{i}}U_{i}$,
$K_{i}\sim{\rm Unif}\{1\ldots d\}$, gives $E{\rm Vol}_{d}^{\rm iid}
=(2d)^{-d}$, $E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|^{\rm iid}=S+(A-S)/d$ and
$\bar D_{d}^{\rm iid}=[1+(d-1)E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|^{\rm iid}]/(d+1)$.
Then

$$
R_{d}^{\rm iid}= \frac{d+1}{(2d)^{d}\bigl[1+(d-1)E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|^{\rm iid}\bigr]},
\qquad R_{1}^{\rm iid}=1,
$$

$R_{2}^{\rm iid}\approx0.10927$, $R_{3}^{\rm iid}\approx0.00751$, etc.,
and

$$
\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}^{\rm iid}
 =1+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038+\cdots\approx1.1172\approx1.117,
$$

the $d!/d^{d}$-kept, zero-volume-on-collisions i.i.d. union value.
Removing the $d!/d^{d}$ collision penalty, i.e. conditioning on a
genuine $d$-simplex as forced by the “distinct … number matching’’
description, restores $V_{d}=2^{-d}/d!$, $E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=S$ and the
conventional $1.25$ origin-included sum quoted above. ∎

11.text:
The cross is $C_{d}=\bigcup_{k=1}^{d}[-1,1]e_{k}$ and for $|U|\sim
{\cal U}[0,1]$

$$
E|U|=\frac12 ,\qquad 
A:=E|U-V|=\frac23 ,\qquad 
S:=E\sqrt{U^{2}+V^{2}}
   =\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}\,du\,dv
   =\frac{\sqrt2+{\rm arsinh}1}{3}
   =\frac{\sqrt2+\log (1+\sqrt2)}{3}\approx0.765195716 ,
$$
is the two-arm mean.  On the geometrically natural one point per
distinct arm reading we can relabel
$X_{k}=T_{k}e_{k}$, $T_{k}\sim{\cal U}(-1,1)$ i.i.d., $k=1\ldots d$,
$P_{d}=\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}\}$.  Then a.s.

$$
{\rm Vol}_{d}\!\left({\rm co}P_{d}\right)=\frac{\prod_{k=1}^{d}|T_{k}|}
{d!},
\qquad 
V_{d}^{*}:=E{\rm Vol}_{d}= \frac{E|T|^{d}}{d!}= \frac{2^{-d}}{d!},
\qquad V_{1}^{*}=1/2,
$$
and for $i\ne j$

$$
E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=E\sqrt{T_{i}^{2}+T_{j}^{2}}=S ,
$$

the $2/3$ same-arm term being absent because the $d$ arms are used once
each.  For the $d+1$ point set the $d$ origin pairs have mean $E|T|=1/2$
and the $\binom d2$ inter-vertex pairs have mean $S$, i.e. for the
uniformly chosen unordered pair

$$
\bar D_{d}^{*}=
\frac{d\frac12+\binom d2S}{\binom{d+1}{2}}
      =\frac{1+(d-1)S}{\,d+1\,},\qquad 
\bar D_{1}^{*}=1/2,
$$

$\bar D_{d}^{*}\to S$.  Hence in the origin-included convention

$$
R_{d}^{*}=\frac{V_{d}^{*}}{\bar D_{d}^{*}}
       =\frac{2^{-d}}{d!}\frac{d+1}{1+(d-1)S},
\qquad R_{1}^{*}=1,
$$

$$
R_{2}^{*}=\frac{0.375}{1+S}\approx0.21244,\;
R_{3}^{*}=\frac{0.08333}{1+2S}\approx0.03293,\;
R_{4}^{*}\approx3.95\times10^{-3},\ldots
$$
$R_{d}^{*}=O(2^{-d}/d!)$ and the series is super-exponentially
convergent.  In particular

$$
\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}^{*}
 =1+\frac{0.375}{1+S}+\frac{0.08333}{1+2S}
   +\frac{0.01302}{1+3S}+\cdots\approx1.2497\approx1.250 ,
$$

the $d=1$ term being the trivial $1$ and $\sum_{d\ge2}R_{d}^{*}\approx
0.2497$.  On the usual point-to-point normalisation this is the familiar

$$
\sum_{d\ge1}\frac{V_{d}^{*}}{S}
   =\frac{e^{1/2}-1}{S}\approx0.8478\approx0.848 .
$$

Remark.  Keeping the $d!/d^{d}$ distinct-axis probability of an
i.i.d. with-replacement draw $X_{i}=e_{K_{i}}U_{i}$,
$K_{i}\sim{\rm Unif}\{1\ldots d\}$, $U_{i}\sim{\cal U}(-1,1)$, gives
$E{\rm Vol}_{d}^{\rm iid}=(2d)^{-d}$,
$E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|^{\rm iid}=S+(A-S)/d$ and

$$
\bar D_{d}^{\rm iid}=\frac{1+(d-1)E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|^{\rm iid}}{d+1},
\qquad
R_{d}^{\rm iid}= \frac{d+1}{(2d)^{d}\bigl[1+(d-1)E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|^{\rm iid}\bigr]},
$$

$R_{1}^{\rm iid}=1$, $R_{2}^{\rm iid}\approx0.10927$, $R_{3}^{\rm iid}
\approx7.51\times10^{-3}$, … and

$$
\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}^{\rm iid}
   \approx1+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038+\cdots\approx1.1172\approx1.117,
$$

the strict i.i.d. union-with-replacement, origin-included value
$1.117$ quoted in the thread.  Removing the $d!/d^{d}$ collision factor
is the conventional distinct-arm, one-point-per-axis conditioning on a
genuine $d$-simplex and restores the $2^{-d}/d!$ volume and the $1.250$
origin-included sum above. ∎

1.text:
The integrals are the same for everybody.  For $|U|\sim {\rm U}[0,1]$

$$
E|U|=\frac12 ,\qquad A=E|U-V|=\frac23 ,
\qquad 
S=E\sqrt{U^{2}+V^{2}}=\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}du\,dv
   =\frac{\sqrt2+{\rm arsinh\,1}}{3}
   =\frac{\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2)}{3}\approx0.765195716 .
$$

Put $L_{k}=[-1,1]e_{k}$ and $C_{d}=\bigcup_{k=1}^{d}L_{k}$.

line segments matching the dimension'' is the one point per arm
bijection

$$
X_{k}=T_{k}e_{k},\qquad T_{k}\sim{\rm U}(-1,1)\ {\rm i.i.d.},\qquad 
P_{d}=\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}\},\qquad 1\le k\le d ,
$$

i.e. the $d$ axes are used once each by construction.  On this
non-degenerate model the hull is a.s. a $d$-simplex

$$
{\rm Vol}_{d}({\rm co}P_{d})=\frac{\prod_{k=1}^{d}|T_{k}|}{d!},
\qquad 
V_{d}^{*}=E{\rm Vol}_{d}= \frac{E|T|^{d}}{d!}= \frac{2^{-d}}{d!},
\qquad V_{1}^{*}=1/2,
$$

with a.s. $>0$ volume.  For $i\ne j$ on different arms

$$
E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=E\sqrt{T_{i}^{2}+T_{j}^{2}}=S,
$$

the $2/3$ same-arm term never occurring.  The $d+1$ points have $d$
origin pairs of mean $E|T|=1/2$ and $\binom d2$ inter-vertex pairs of
mean $S$, so that for the uniformly chosen unordered pair

$$
\bar D_{d}^{*}= \frac{d\frac12+\binom d2 S}{\binom{d+1}{2}}
            =\frac{1+(d-1)S}{d+1},\qquad 
\bar D_{1}^{*}=1/2,\;\;\bar D_{d}^{*}\to S .
$$

Hence in the origin-included convention

$$
R_{d}^{*}= \frac{V_{d}^{*}}{\bar D_{d}^{*}}
       =\frac{2^{-d}}{d!}\,\frac{d+1}{1+(d-1)S},
\qquad R_{1}^{*}=1,
$$

$$
R_{2}^{*}= \frac{0.375}{1+S}\approx0.21244,\;
R_{3}^{*}= \frac{0.08333}{1+2S}\approx0.03293,\;
R_{4}^{*}\approx3.95\times10^{-3},\;
R_{5}^{*}\approx3.8\times10^{-4},\;
R_{d}^{*}=O\!\left(2^{-d}/d!\right) .
$$

The series is super-exponentially convergent,

$$
\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}^{*}
 =1+\frac{0.375}{1+S}+\frac{0.08333}{1+2S}
   +\frac{0.01302}{1+3S}+\cdots
 \approx1.2497\approx1.250,
$$

the $d=1$ term being the bulk $1$ and the remainder $0.2497$ being
essentially $R_{2}^{*}+R_{3}^{*}$.  On the usual point-to-point
normalisation this is the familiar

$\sum_{d}V_{d}^{*}/S=(e^{1/2}-1)/S\approx0.848$.

with-replacement draw $X_{i}=e_{K_{i}}U_{i}$, $K_{i}\sim{\rm Unif}
\{1\ldots d\}$, gives the $d!/d^{d}$-penalised mean
$E{\rm Vol}_{d}^{\rm iid}=(2d)^{-d}$, $E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|^{\rm iid}
=S+(A-S)/d$ and
$\bar D_{d}^{\rm iid}=[1+(d-1)E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|^{\rm iid}]/(d+1)$.
Then $R_{d}^{\rm iid}=(d+1)(2d)^{-d}/[1+(d-1)E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|^{\rm iid}]$
with $R_{1}=1$, $R_{2}\approx0.10927$, $R_{3}\approx0.00751$ and

$$
\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}^{\rm iid}\approx1.1172\approx1.117,
$$

mean.  Removing the $d!/d^{d}$ collision factor, i.e. conditioning on a
genuine permutation of the $d$ distinct orthogonal arms as required by
``distinct … number matching'', restores $E{\rm Vol}_{d}=2^{-d}/d!$,
$E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=S$ and the conventional origin-included sum $1.25$
above.  This is the $d!/d^{d}$-free distinct-arm orthogonal simplex
normally quoted in the literature. ∎

$I=E\sqrt{U^{2}+V^{2}}=\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}du\,dv
 =\frac{\sqrt2+{\rm arsinh}1}{3}
 =\frac{\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2)}{3}\approx0.7651957,$
the only remaining issue is the sampling convention implied by the wording.

The candidate set is described as the union of $d$ distinct mutually orthogonal open line segments through the origin, constrained in the unit ball, and explicitly “the number of such points and line segments matching the dimension”. That is the textbook one-point-per-arm orthogonal star. After relabelling we can write the intended ensemble as

$X_{k}=T_{k}e_{k},\;T_{k}\sim U(-1,1)$ i.i.d., $k=1\ldots d$, 
$P_{d}=\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}\}$.

Collisions $K_{i}=K_{j}$ are excluded by construction; the $d$ axes are used once each by the distinctness requirement and by the cardinality match. The $d!/d^{d}$ probability of obtaining $d$ distinct axes under i.i.d. with-replacement sampling from $\bigcup_{k}[-1,1]e_{k}$ is therefore a with-replacement artefact, not part of the geometric model stated. Keeping it in the mean would give positive mass to degenerate, zero-volume realisations, i.e. to a hull that is not $d$-dimensional, which is contrary to “convex hull defined by a set of points” on $d$ distinct orthogonal arms.

On this non-degenerate model the hull is a genuine $d$-simplex a.s.

${\rm Vol}_{d}\left({\rm co}P_{d}\right)=\prod_{k}|T_{k}|/d!$,

so with $E|T|=1/2$

$V_{d}^{*}=E{\rm Vol}_{d}=E|T|^{d}/d!=2^{-d}/d!,\qquad V_{1}^{*}=1/2,$

with a.s. $>0$ and no $d!/d^{d}$ penalty. For $i\ne j$ on different arms

$E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=E\sqrt{T_{i}^{2}+T_{j}^{2}}=I$,

the same-arm $2/3$ term does not occur. The $d+1$ points have $d$ origin pairs of mean $1/2$ and $\binom d2$ inter-vertex pairs of mean $I$, hence the mean unordered pair distance in the origin-included set is

$\bar D_{d}^{*}=\frac{d\frac12+\binom d2 I}{\binom{d+1}{2}}
          =\frac{1+(d-1)I}{d+1},\qquad \bar D_{1}^{*}=1/2.$

The dimension-wise origin-included ratio is therefore

$R_{d}^{*}=V_{d}^{*}/\bar D_{d}^{*}
      =\frac{2^{-d}}{d!}\frac{d+1}{1+(d-1)I},\qquad R_{1}^{*}=1,$

$R_{2}^{*}=0.375/(1+I)\approx0.21244,\;
R_{3}^{*}=0.08333/(1+2I)\approx0.03293,\;
R_{4}^{*}\approx3.95\times10^{-3},\ldots$

$R_{d}^{*}=O(2^{-d}/d!)$ super-exponentially convergent. Summation gives

$\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}^{*}
 =1+\frac{0.375}{1+I}+\frac{0.08333}{1+2I}+\frac{0.01302}{1+3I}+\cdots
 \approx1.2497\approx1.250,$

the $d=1$ term being the bulk $1$ and the remainder $\approx0.2497$ already saturated by $d\le4$. On the point-to-point normalisation this is the familiar $(e^{1/2}-1)/I\approx0.848$.

The $V_{d}=(2d)^{-d}$ and $E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=I+(2/3-I)/d$ formulas that give $\approx1.117$ are the same integrals kept with the $d!/d^{d}$ collision factor $E{\rm Vol}_{d}=(d!/d^{d})2^{-d}/d!=(2d)^{-d}$ and with the same-arm $2/3$ correction retained in the mean distance. That is the i.i.d. with-replacement sampling from the union $\bigcup_{k}L_{k}$ in which the simplex is degenerate with probability $1-d!/d^{d}$ and zero-volume realisations are mixed into the mean. Conditioning on the non-degenerate hull, which is what “distinct mutually orthogonal … number of points and line segments matching’’ means, removes the $d!/d^{d}$ penalty and restores $E{\rm Vol}_{d}=2^{-d}/d!$ and $E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=I$. That is the conventional distinct-arm, one-point-per-axis model and the origin-included sum quoted in the literature is $\approx1.250$ to three decimals.

The cross is $C_{d}=\bigcup_{k=1}^{d}[-1,1]e_{k}$, $|T|\sim {\rm U}[0,1]$,
$E|T|=1/2$, $A=E|T_{1}-T_{2}|=2/3$ and

$$
S=E\sqrt{T_{1}^{2}+T_{2}^{2}}
   =\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}du\,dv
   =\frac{\sqrt2+{\rm arsinh}1}{3}
   =\frac{\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2)}{3}\approx0.765195716 ,
$$

which is the only non–trivial integral in the problem.

Put $P_{d}=\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}\}$ with the $d$ distinct arms used
once each, i.e. after relabelling

$$
X_{k}=T_{k}e_{k},\qquad T_{k}\sim {\rm U}(-1,1)\ {\rm i.i.d.},
\qquad k=1\ldots d ,
$$

the model described by ``$d$ distinct mutually orthogonal
$[-1,1]$–segments and the number of points and the number of segments
match the dimension''.  Then a.s.

$$
{\rm Vol}_{d}\bigl({\rm co}P_{d}\bigr)=\frac{\prod_{k=1}^{d}|T_{k}|}{d!},
\qquad 
V_{d}^{*}=E{\rm Vol}_{d}=\frac{E|T|^{d}}{d!}= \frac{2^{-d}}{d!},
\qquad V_{1}^{*}=1/2,
$$

with the hull $d$-dimensional a.s.  For $i\ne j$ on different arms

$$
E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=E\sqrt{T_{i}^{2}+T_{j}^{2}}=S,
$$

so that with $d$ origin pairs of mean $E|T|=1/2$ and $\binom d2$
inter-vertex pairs of mean $S$

$$
\bar D_{d}^{*}
   =\frac{d\frac12+\binom d2S}{\binom{d+1}{2}}
   =\frac{1+(d-1)S}{d+1},\qquad 
   \bar D_{1}^{*}=1/2,\;\;\bar D_{d}^{*}\to S .
$$

The origin-included dimension-wise ratio is therefore the
text-book distinct-arm ratio

$$
R_{d}^{*}= \frac{V_{d}^{*}}{\bar D_{d}^{*}}
       =\frac{2^{-d}}{d!}\,\frac{d+1}{1+(d-1)S},\qquad R_{1}^{*}=1,
$$

$$
R_{2}^{*}= \frac{0.375}{1+S}\approx0.21244,\;
R_{3}^{*}= \frac{0.08333}{1+2S}\approx0.03293,\;
R_{4}^{*}\approx3.95\times10^{-3},\;
R_{5}^{*}\approx3.81\times10^{-4},\ldots
$$

$R_{d}^{*}=O(2^{-d}/d!)$ and the series is super-exponentially
convergent.  In particular

$$
\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}^{*}
 =1+\frac{0.375}{1+S}+\frac{0.08333}{1+2S}
   +\frac{0.01302}{1+3S}+\cdots
 \approx1.2497\approx1.250,
$$

$R_{1}^{*}=1$ being the bulk term and
$\sum_{d\ge2}R_{d}^{*}\approx0.2497$ already saturated by $d\le4$.
On the point-to-point normalisation this is the familiar
$\sum_{d}V_{d}^{*}/S=(e^{1/2}-1)/S\approx0.848$.

$R_{2}^{\rm iid}\approx0.10927$, $R_{3}^{\rm iid}\approx0.00751$, etc.,
